We welcome your application!

jobs.title: PHD student in Epigenetics and Chromatin Dynamics
jobs.description_html:
Description of the workplace

The Laboratory of Epigenetics and Chromatin Dynamics at the Department of Experimental Medical Science (Faculty of Medicine), is currently conducting research investigating the epigenetic regulation of repetitive and transposable genetic elements – so-called 'genomic dark matter' – in human brain development and disease. The group consists of 8 research-active members and is led by Dr Christopher Douse. We are fascinated by how these underexplored regions of the human genome contribute functionally to human neurobiology and neurological disease. Our work integrates state-of-the-art wet and dry lab methods. More information can be found here . As a workplace, we safeguard a good work environment with respect and consideration in our relationships with each other. We commit to the following core lab values: Equity – all lab members have value and contribute, there are no stupid questions; People-centric - our work is collaborative and we communicate openly with eachother, the community and the outside world; Integrity – we do not take shortcuts and emphasize reproducibilty and rigor in our data. Curiosity - we are humble about what we don't know, actively seek feedback and are open to ideas; Diversity – we will do better research if we have diversity of background and scientific expertise.

Project description

We are particularly focused currently on three types of element that are repetitive in different ways, but unified by an importance to human brain function and disease: clustered protocadherin repeat genes, viral-like sequences called retrotransposons, and CGG microsatellite tandem repeats. In all cases there are significant knowledge gaps surrounding the epigenetic control and influence of the elements. What are the factors that bind and regulate these REs in neural lineages? How do they functionally impact the epigenome and local transcriptional dynamics, and disease traits? To answer these questions we will combine chromatin biochemistry and cutting-edge functional epigenomics with advanced neural cellular models and tailored bioinformatic analyses. In doing so we will discover new, basic human neurobiology and much-needed insights on the mechanisms underpinning RE-associated neurological disorders.

This PhD project will combine chromatin biochemistry with functional (epi)genomics in stem cell models of the human brain. Importantly, this PhD project will require a balance of wet and dry-lab approaches.

In particular the doctoral student will use the following methods:

  • Stem cell culture (iPSCs, 2- and 3D neural progenitors)
  • RNA-seq, CUT&RUN/Tag, Oxford Nanopore sequencing (cDNA, DiMeLo-seq) and associated bioinformatic analyses
  • Co-immunoprecipitation and/or proximity labelling proteomics

Tasks and responsibilities

The main task for a doctoral student is to devote yourself to your doctoral studies, therefore you will be both admitted as a student and employed at Lund University. In addition to your full-time research studies, you may be involved in the supervision of bachelor or master students.

We offer

Lund University is a public authority which means that employees get particular benefits, generous annual leave and an advantageous occupational pension scheme. Read more on the University website about being a Lund University employee Work at Lund University

Qualifications

 

Requirements for admission are:

  • a second-cycle degree, completed course requirements of at least 240 higher education credits, of which at least 60 higher education credits are at second-cycle level, or substantially equivalent knowledge acquired in Sweden or abroad
  • the ability to benefit from doctoral studies

Requirements for the position are:

  • experience in functional (epi)genomics and/or chromatin biochemistry
  • experience with stem cell culture and differentiation models
  • a demonstrable interest in the repetitive genome, either in humans or model organisms, through previous experience or as described in your cover letter or during an interview
  • excellent knowledge of molecular biology and molecular genetics
  • excellent spoken and written English
  • good analytical skills and an independent, problem-solving approach
  • an open and collaborative approach to research, in line with the lab values described above

The following qualifications are considered an advantage:

  • being highly organised and self-motivated
  • experience with long-read sequencing approaches
  • experience with protein biochemistry
  • experience working collaboratively on ambitious research projects
  • being receptive to constructive feedback and demonstrating a willingness to develop and learn throughout the doctoral studies

Further information

Limit of tenure, four years according to HF 5 kap 7§. Start date 1th of December 2026, or as agreed.

How to apply

The application should include a personal letter justifying your interest in the position and how it matches your qualifications. The application should also include a CV, degree certificates or equivalent and any other document to which you would like to draw attention (copies of grade transcripts, details of referees, letters of recommendation, etc.) Candidates will be considered on an ongoing basis during the application period.

About the Faculty of Medicine

jobs.title: Doktorand inom medicinsk vetenskap inriktning hälsovetenskap
jobs.description_html:
Placering

Som doktorand blir du en del av forskargruppen Aktivt och hälsosamt åldrande vid Institutionen för hälsovetenskaper. Forskargruppen är knuten till det tvärvetenskapliga Centre for Ageing and Supportive Environments (CASE), där seniora och juniora forskare från fyra av universitetets fakulteter samarbetar.

Hos oss får du en stimulerande och inkluderande arbetsmiljö där samarbete, kunskapsutbyte och utveckling står i centrum. Du får stöd av engagerade kollegor och handledare samt möjlighet att växa i en tvärvetenskaplig och internationell forskningsmiljö. Läs mer om att arbeta på Lunds universitet här.

Beskrivning

Forskarutbildningen leder till en doktorsexamen i medicinsk vetenskap med inriktning hälsovetenskap. I doktorandprojektet bidrar du till ökad kunskap om vad tillgängliga och användbara publika miljöer innebär för personer med olika kognitiva funktionsnedsättningar. Du undersöker också hur kunskapen kan omsättas i nya sätt att utforma publika anläggningar och digital information som stärker människors delaktighet i samhället.

Studierna genomförs inom det fyraåriga projektet ”PRO-COG: Tillgängliga och användbara publika anläggningar som främjar delaktighet i samhället för personer med kognitiva funktionsnedsättningar”. Projektet finansieras av Forskningsrådet för miljö, areella näringar och samhällsbyggande (FORMAS) och bedrivs i en tvärvetenskaplig forskningsmiljö. Du kommer främst att arbeta med kvalitativa metoder för datainsamling och analys. Dina handledare representerar hälsovetenskap och arbetsterapi.

Arbetsuppgifter

Som doktorand ägnar du dig främst åt din egen forskarutbildning. Enligt 5 kap. 2 § högskoleförordningen (HF) kan även utbildning, forskning och administration ingå, dock högst 20 procent av en heltidsanställning innan doktorsexamen har avlagts.

Med stöd av dina handledare kommer du att:

  • medverka i planeringen av projektet,
  • samla in, analysera och sammanställa data,
  • rapportera resultat i vetenskapliga artiklar på engelska,
  • sammanfatta doktorandprojektet i en engelskspråkig ramberättelse och presentera det i en doktorsavhandling,
  • genomföra obligatoriska kurser på forskarnivå och aktivt delta i seminarier och andra relevanta aktiviteter,
  • fördjupa dig i litteratur inom forskningsområdet, samt
  • kommunicera och omsätta forskningsresultat för målgrupper inom och utanför forskarsamhället.

Resor inom Sverige och internationellt förekommer. En forskningsvistelse vid ett annat universitet i Sverige eller utomlands kan också bli aktuell.

Du förväntas också bidra till relevanta aktiviteter och uppdrag inom forskargruppen, institutionen och CASE. Även andra arbetsuppgifter kan förekomma.

Behörighet

För att vara behörig till utbildningen på forskarnivå ska du uppfylla något av följande:

  • avlagt en examen på avancerad nivå, eller
  • fullgjort minst 240 högskolepoäng, varav minst 60 högskolepoäng på avancerad nivå, eller
  • på annat sätt, inom eller utanför Sverige, förvärvat i huvudsak motsvarande kunskaper.

Forskarutbildningsnämnden kan medge undantag från kravet på grundläggande behörighet om det finns särskilda skäl.

Särskild behörighet

För särskild behörighet krävs minst 60 högskolepoäng inom medicinsk vetenskap och tillräckliga kunskaper inom forskarutbildningens ämnesområde.

Om du har en utomnordisk grundexamen, och ditt hemspråk inte är engelska, behöver du även styrka kunskaper i engelska motsvarande treårig gymnasieutbildning genom ett godkänt prov.

Krav

  • God datorvana.
  • Goda kunskaper i tal och skrift i svenska eller ett annat skandinaviskt språk.
  • Goda kunskaper i engelska.

Meriterande

  • Erfarenhet av att möta och samverka med personer med kognitiva funktionsnedsättningar.

Personliga egenskaper

Vi lägger stor vikt vid personlig lämplighet. För att trivas och lyckas i rollen behöver du kunna arbeta självständigt och noggrant samt samarbeta väl med andra.

Bedömningsgrund

Bestämmelser om anställning som doktorand finns i förordning SFS 1998:80. Endast den som är antagen till utbildning på forskarnivå kan anställas som doktorand. Vid urvalet bedömer vi framför allt din förmåga att tillgodogöra dig forskarutbildningen.

Villkor

Anställningen är på heltid med planerat tillträde den 11 januari 2027 eller enligt överenskommelse.

Anställningen är tidsbegränsad till fyra år enligt 5 kap. 7 § högskoleförordningen.

Kontakt
Har du frågor om anställningen är du välkommen att kontakta huvudhandledare och biträdande forskare Björn Slaug på telefon 046 222 18 38 eller via e-post: bjorn.slaug@med.lu.se.

jobs.title: Doctoral student in Industrial Design with focus on strategic design
jobs.description_html:
Description of the workplace

The position is located in the division of Industrial Design at the Department of Design Sciences at LTH, Lund University. Design Sciences is an interdisciplinary department that integrates design, technology, and people in its research and education.

As a doctoral student you will become part of an interdisciplinary research environment and work alongside doctoral students, senior researchers and teaching staff within Industrial Design and the wider Department of Design Sciences.

Being a doctoral student

As a doctoral student, you are both admitted as a student and employed at Lund University. You will be trained in a scientific approach. In short, you will be trained to think critically and analytically, to solve problems independently using the right methods, and to develop an awareness of research ethics. In addition, you will have the opportunity to work on projects, to develop your leadership and pedagogical skills. Throughout your studies, you will be guided by supervisors. Doctoral studies end with a thesis and a doctoral degree.

More about being a doctoral student at LTH on lth.se. 

Subject and project description

Research in Industrial Design investigates how design shapes and responds to technological, environmental and societal change. It develops and critically examines design knowledge, methods and practices, with the aim of understanding how design can contribute to meaningful and responsible transformation.

Our research combines scientific and artistic approaches and is often conducted in collaboration with academic, industrial and public-sector partners as well as communities and third-sector organizations. The research environment encompasses sustainable design; emerging technologies and AI; design strategy, management and innovation; design practice and methods; and critical and participatory perspectives on design and design education.

This doctoral position has a particular focus on strategic design. The research will investigate how design can operate as a strategic capability in organizations and society and contribute to processes of innovation, transformation and value creation. Possible areas of inquiry include how design capabilities are developed and embedded in organizations; the role of design and design approaches in enabling organizational change; design in complex settings; systemic design; and user and citizen engagement in strategic design processes. The research may also investigate futures-oriented approaches, including designerly ways of navigating complex and uncertain societal, technological and environmental conditions.

Within this overall research area, the doctoral student will develop and refine the specific research direction and project in dialogue with the supervisors. The project is expected to combine theoretical inquiry with empirical research and may incorporate experimental, participatory or practice-based design approaches where relevant.

Work duties

You will primarily devote yourself to your doctoral programme. You will develop and conduct an independent doctoral research project. Your work will include formulating research questions, reviewing and developing relevant theoretical perspectives, designing and conducting empirical studies, analysing research material, communicating findings through academic publications and conferences, and completing a doctoral thesis.

You will also be expected to participate actively in the research environment of the Division of Industrial Design and the Department of Design Sciences and to engage with relevant academic and external research partners. Additional duties include participation in teaching and other departmental work (however, a maximum of 20% of working hours).

The position requires regular on-site presence at Lund University in Lund to carry out the work and participate fully in the research environment.

Qualifications

To be eligible for admission and employment as a doctoral student, you must fulfil the requirements below.

Admission requirements

A person meets the general admission requirements for third-cycle courses and study programmes if the applicant:

  • has been awarded a second-cycle qualification, or
  • has satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second cycle, or
  • has acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad.

A person meets the specific admission requirements for third cycle studies in Industrial Design if the applicant has:

  • at least 30 higher education credits relevant to the subject area, of which at least 15 credits must be at an advanced level, or
  • an in-depth study of at least 20 higher education credits at an advanced level relevant to the subject area, or
  • a degree in fine arts, engineering, Master's or Magister's degree relevant to the subject area.

Additional requirements

In order to complete the doctoral programme in question, the following are also required:

  • Knowledge and skills relevant to industrial design and to the proposed area of doctoral research.
  • Ability to to independently formulate and address research problems.
  • Analytical skills and the ability to engage critically with theoretical perspectives and empirical material.
  • Excellent written and oral communication skills in English.

Other qualifications (advantages)

For the doctoral programme in question, the following are considered as other qualifications:

  • Experience of conducting empirical, practice-based or participatory research.
  • Experience of interdisciplinary or multidisciplinary work.
  • Experience of managing complex projects involving multiple actors or perspectives.
  • Experience of using design methods and practices as part of research or inquiry.
  • Experience of collaboration with academic, industrial, public-sector or other societal actors.
  • Experience of communicating research or complex design work to different audiences.

Consideration will also be given to the applicant's ability to take initiative, work independently, collaborate with others, and develop and complete a long-term research project.

We offer

Lund University is a public authority which means that employees get particular benefits, generous annual leave and an advantageous occupational pension scheme.

More about working at Lund University on lu.se. 

About the employment

The employment is a fixed-term employment at full time, starting on 2027-01-01 or soon after. Third cycle studies at LTH consist of full-time studies for 4 years. In the case of teaching and other departmental duties, the employment is extended accordingly. Doctoral studentships are regulated in the Higher Education Ordinance (1993:100), chapter 5, 1-7 §§.

More about terms of employment for doctoral students on Lund University’s Staffpages. 

Other

This doctoral position is funded by the Ingvar Kamprad Design Foundation (IKDF).

How to apply

Applications must be written in English and include:

  • CV
  • A cover letter describing your reasons for wishing to undertake a PhD in Industrial Design, your interest in this position, and how your academic, professional and/or personal experiences have shaped your research interests and prepared you for doctoral studies.
  • Copies of degree certificates and transcripts confirming that you meet the general and specific admission requirements;
  • A research statement (maximum 1,500 words) describing the research questions, problems or phenomena within Strategic Design that you are interested in exploring, why you consider them important, and how you might approach investigating them. The statement is intended to demonstrate your research interests and ability to formulate a potential direction for doctoral research; it is not expected to constitute a fully developed research proposal.
  • A portfolio or selection of work samples demonstrating relevant design, research, or professional work. These may include design projects, research projects, publications or other written work, collaborative or community-based projects, or other work relevant to the position. For collaborative work, clearly describe your own role and contribution.
  • Contact information for three references and
  • Any other documents you wish to be considered.

We welcome your application.

jobs.description_html:
Description of the workplace

The Department of Aviation and Aeronautical Sciences strives to be a leading center for aeronautics research, development, and education. The department operates a certified commercial flight school (ATO) and an authorized drone school (ADS) under the name of Lund University School of Aviation, Sweden's only state-run civilian flight school. The department’s research facilities are based at Campus Ljungbyhed, providing a unique setting that integrates research, development, and education with access to airport infrastructure, including a runway system and controlled airspace. We seek to understand, innovate, and advance aviation through collaborative efforts, making it more accessible, sustainable, and safe in the digital age. The research emphasizes three primary areas: sustainable aviation, unmanned aviation, and aviation safety, with safety being a central theme across all initiatives.

This doctoral student position is at the Department of Aviation and Aeronautical Sciences and will work at the intersection between unmanned aviation and aviation safety, as part of the Center for Heterogeneous Adaptive Swarm Systems (CHASS) funded by Stiftelsen för Strategisk Forskning*  (SSF). CHASS includes three dual-use relevant large industrial partners (Saab, Sectra Communications and BAE Systems Hägglunds) and societal participation from the Swedish Defence Research Institute (FOI), the Swedish Civil Defence and Resilience Agency (MCF) and the Swedish Civil Aviation Administration (LFV).

The duty station is Ljungbyhed.

*More about SSF

Being a doctoral student

As a doctoral student, you are both admitted as a student and employed at Lund University.

As a doctoral student, you will be trained in a scientific approach. In short, you will be trained to think critically and analytically, to solve problems independently using the right methods, and to develop an awareness of research ethics. In addition, you will have the opportunity to work on projects, to develop your leadership and pedagogical skills. Throughout your studies, you will be guided by supervisors. Doctoral studies end with a thesis and a doctoral degree.

More about being a doctoral student at LTH on lth.se

Subject and project description

The research area is Risk and Safety of heterogeneous swarm systems.

The multi-disciplinary center for heterogeneous adaptive swarm systems, CHASS, is a national effort funded by the Swedish Strategic Research Foundation (SSF) to bring together leading researchers in AI, autonomous systems, robotics, and swarm intelligence to develop novel solutions for autonomous heterogeneous swarm systems for the benefit of Swedish industry and society. The vision is to make Sweden a leader in intelligent, adaptive, and trustworthy swarm systems by pioneering autonomous heterogeneous collectives of space, aerial, ground, surface, and underwater platforms that can operate as a unified intelligent entity with minimal human intervention. The research program focuses on six key themes: Drone Design, Adaptation, & Production; Perception, Sensing, & Communication; Autonomy, Localization, Mapping & Navigation; Coordination, Self-Governance, & Self-Improvement; Human Swarm Interaction; and Swarm-based Services & Socio-Technical Aspects.

CHASS is led by Linköping University and besides Lund University also includes Örebro University, each with CHASS-affiliated doctoral students, as well as a large number of industry and government stakeholders, providing a stimulating research environment. CHASS will drive world-class research in autonomous swarm systems through a strong, stimulating, and well-connected international research environment. Research outcomes will be validated in real-world scenarios with industry and public-sector partners. CHASS will also serve as a national hub for autonomous swarm systems, promoting education, knowledge sharing, innovation, and policy development.

The doctoral student position in this announcement will work within the theme of Swarm-based Services & Socio-Technical Aspects. It develops and evaluates risk assessment and safety management methodologies (for the phases before, during, and after operations) for heterogeneous swarms, including frameworks for risk assessment, adaptive capacity and control, and accountability and responsibility. The position will include interaction with other doctoral students and researchers within this theme, as well as the Human Swarm Interaction theme and the other technological development themes.

Work duties

You will primarily devote yourself to your doctoral programme, which includes participation in research projects as well as third cycle courses, seminars and conferences.

The work duties include:

  • You will work in a multi-disciplinary research project focused on socio-technical aspects of control, risk, and safety of heterogeneous swarms resilience.
  • You will likely combine qualitative (e.g. interviews) and quantitative (e.g. modelling, statistics) methods.
  • You will travel in Sweden and abroad to interact with fellow researchers to collaborate and present research findings at scientific conferences.
  • As parts of the research may be conducted in collaboration with defence-related organisations, a security screening will be carried out if applicable.
  • The duties also include participation in teaching and other departmental work (however, a maximum of 20% of working hours).

Qualifications

Admission requirements

A person meets the general admission requirements for third-cycle courses and study programmes if the applicant:

  • has been awarded a second-cycle qualification, or
  • has satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second cycle, or
  • has acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad.

A person meets the specific admission requirements for third cycle studies in Risk and Safety (TEVBRF11) if the applicant has:

  • at least 90 credits in subjects of relevance to the field, including at least 60 second cycle credits, or
  • a BSc in Fire Protection Engineering amounting to 210 credits.

Additional requirements

In order to complete the doctoral programme in question, the following are also required:

  • good knowledge in risk, system safety, design, and governance of socio-technical systems in complex settings,
  • good ability to take initiative and solve research challenges with drive, creativity, and persistence,
  • good ability to work in a structured way in a collaborative and inter-disciplinary environment,
  • good ability to work independently and to formulate and tackle research problems,
  • good written and oral communication skills,
  • good ability to cooperate with other researchers and practitioners,
  • very good knowledge of English, spoken and written.

Other qualifications

For the doctoral programme in question, the following are considered as meriting qualifications:

  • knowledge of aeronautical engineering, human-computer interaction, human factors engineering, cognitive science, human control of AI, unmanned aviation, critical infrastructure resilience, interaction design, industrial design engineering, and related disciplines,
  • skills and experience in modelling and simulation,
  • skills and experience in relevant software and programming environments, such as Matlab, Python, C++, UAS communication protocols (MAVLink), ROS2, git.
  • skills and experience in statistical analysis and quantitative research methods,
  • skills and experience relating to relevant qualitative research methods, such as interviews,
  • driving licence B,
  • practical experience of operations in manned or unmanned aviation.

Consideration will also be given to how the applicant, through his or her experience and skills, is deemed to have the abilities necessary for successfully completing the third cycle programme.

jobs.title: Doctoral student in Technology and Society on regulatory learning and supervisory competence
jobs.description_html:
Description of the workplace

This doctoral position is part of REGULAIRE, which is a MSCA doctoral pan-European network that studies how regulation can learn and adapt in situations where technologies, risks, and expectations change quickly. The network will train fifteen fellows to examine this learning process from different angles. They will look at how authorities detect early signals, design and test interventions, evaluate what works, and share findings across organisations. 

REGULAIRE stands for Regulatory Learning for the Governance of Transformative Technologies, and the consortium is led by Technical University Munich. The consortium includes technical universities, business schools, social and legal scientists, and public sector actors.

This call is of a doctoral position at LTH, Lund University. The research group environment at LTH in Lund, led by Stefan Larsson, focuses on social science-oriented but multidisciplinary issues linked to AI, with affiliated researchers at both junior and senior levels. The research group has a working space at LTH and is part of the Department of Technology and Society. Read more about the research group on the Research Portal of Lund University.

Being a doctoral student

As a doctoral student, you are both admitted as a student and employed at Lund University. 

As a doctoral student, you will be trained in a scientific approach. In short, you will be trained to think critically and analytically, to solve problems independently using the right methods, and to develop an awareness of research ethics. In addition, you will have the opportunity to work on projects, to develop your leadership and pedagogical skills. Throughout your studies, you will be guided by supervisors. Doctoral studies end with a thesis and a doctoral degree.

More about being a doctoral student at LTH on lth.se. 

Subject and project description

The doctoral subject Technology and Society encompasses multi- and interdisciplinary studies on the role, interaction, regulation and significance of technology within society. Research includes both qualitative and quantitative studies and is often characterized by a diversity of methods and theories.

Regulatory flexibility helps law keep pace with fast-moving technologies, but law also needs predictable norms. This doctoral project studies how the two sit together, asking whether flexibilities, delegations, open-textured duties and codes of practice shift authority among legislators, the Commission, standardisers, private actors, and with a special attention to supervisory authorities.

Work duties

You will primarily devote yourself to your doctoral programme, which includes participation in research projects as well as third cycle courses, seminars and conferences. 

You will map supervisory competence, organisation and tooling in selected jurisdictions, using the AI Act to structure comparison, and combine document analysis, interviews and process tracing to link design choices to predictability for firms and protection for citizens.

The work will from a critical perspective analyse flexibility mechanisms and their governance implications. It could be grounded in supervisory practice, comparative case reports and contribute to an assessment framework for supervisory capability. It will also translate evidence into guidance on aligning flexibility with foresight without eroding legal certainty, if possible. This project offers a focused route into socio-legal research, AI governance and the study of technology-oriented supervision.

The employment will include a three-month intersectoral secondment in another country.

The work duties include:

  • Refine the research questions and design with the supervision team, and prepare ethics, data-management and open-science materials.
  • Collect, manage and analyse research data using the approved project-specific methods.
  • Complete a doctoral thesis and related research outputs under the doctoral programme and the REGULAIRE plan.
  • Take part in local and network-wide training, cohort activities, network reviews, dissemination and practitioner engagement, including three residential summer schools and monthly paper development seminars.
  • Undertake the planned three-month intersectoral secondment with a partner institution within REGULAIRE.
  • The duties may also include participation in teaching and other departmental work (however, a maximum of 20% of working hours).

Qualifications 

To be eligible for admission and employment as a doctoral student, you must fulfil the requirements below.

Admission requirements

A person meets the general admission requirements for third-cycle courses and study programmes if the applicant: 

  • has been awarded a second-cycle qualification, or 
  • has satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second cycle, or

A person meets the specific admission requirements for third cycle studies in Technology and Society if the applicant has: 

  • at least 30 credits awarded in the second cycle relevant to the subject area.

Additional requirements

In order to complete the doctoral programme in question, the following are also required: 

  • An educational background in relevant field, for example law, socio-legal studies, political science, science and technology studies, or related social science and interdisciplinary fields.
  • You take initiatives, are structured and persistent.
    Good ability to work independently and to formulate and tackle research problems. 
  • Good written and oral communication skills
  • Good ability to cooperate
  • Very good knowledge of English, spoken and written 

To be eligible for MSCA funding, the selected candidate must also, on the first day of employment: 

  • not hold a doctoral degree; candidates who have successfully defended a doctoral thesis but have not yet formally received the degree are not eligible; 
  • comply with the MSCA mobility rule, meaning you must not have resided or carried out your main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Sweden for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately preceding that date, excluding compulsory national service, short stays such as holidays, and time spent in a procedure for obtaining refugee status under the Geneva Convention.

Other qualifications

For the doctoral programme in question, the following are considered as other qualifications: 

  • experience of qualitative methods, such as document analysis, interviews or process tracing.
  • sociolegal knowledge on how society and law interacts.
  • technological knowledge of emerging technologies.

jobs.description_html:
Description of the workplace

The Planet Formation Group at the Department of Physics (Division of Astrophysics) at Lund University is seeking a PhD student to work on models of planet formation on a galactic scale. Research within the division encompasses galaxy formation, galactic dynamics and evolution, star formation and dynamics, stellar evolution, stellar spectroscopy and astrometry, planet formation and dynamics, as well as exoplanet atmospheres.

Being a doctoral student

As a doctoral student, you are both admitted as a student and employed at Lund University.

As a doctoral student, you will be trained in a scientific approach. In short, you will be trained to think critically and analytically, to solve problems independently using the right methods, and to develop an awareness of research ethics. In addition, you will have the opportunity to work on projects, to develop your leadership and pedagogical skills. Throughout your studies, you will be guided by supervisors. Doctoral studies end with a thesis and a doctoral degree.

More about being a doctoral student at the Faculty of Science at naturvetenskap.se.

  • Allmän studieplan för forskarutbildning

Work duties

We are seeking a PhD student in theoretical astrophysics. The PhD student will study how planets form at different times and in different regions of our galaxy. The PhD student will also calculate how certain planetesimals are ejected from planetary systems to become free-flying interstellar planetesimals. The PhD project will give astronomers new insight into where interstellar comets came from.

Your primary responsibility will be to pursue your doctoral studies, which will mainly consist of conducting research and writing a doctoral thesis. In addition, you will be expected to:

  • Conduct research within the subject area.
  • Publish results in high-quality scientific journals.

jobs.title: Doctoral student in Biomedical Engineering specializing in engineering acoustics
jobs.department: Lund University, Faculty of Engineering, LTH, Dep. of Biomedical Engineering
jobs.description_html:
Description of the workplace

The position is based at the Department of Biomedical Engineering and is linked to researchers working in marine biology, medical ultrasound, biomechanics, physics, e-science, and the strategic research area eSSENCE in Lund. The research group you will join conducts research in areas including engineering acoustics, medical ultrasound, acoustic measurement technology, non-destructive testing based on acoustic methods, signal processing, and numerical modelling, with applications in, among other fields, biomedical engineering, civil engineering, and biological systems.

The working environment is highly interdisciplinary and is characterized by close collaboration between doctoral students, researchers, and academic staff, often with very different technical and scientific backgrounds and areas of expertise. The group strives to provide an open and inclusive working environment with good access to supervision, knowledge exchange, and broad scientific and interdisciplinary collaborations.

More about the strategic research area eSSENCE - on Lund University's website

Being a doctoral student

As a doctoral student, you are both admitted as a student and employed at Lund University. 

As a doctoral student, you will be trained in a scientific approach. In short, you will be trained to think critically and analytically, to solve problems independently using the right methods, and to develop an awareness of research ethics. In addition, you will have the opportunity to work on projects, to develop your leadership and pedagogical skills. Throughout your studies, you will be guided by supervisors. Doctoral studies end with a thesis and a doctoral degree.

We are looking for a candidate who is curious, focused, and highly motivated by scientific questions. You have a creative and open-minded approach and enjoy combining methods and perspectives from different fields, such as physics, acoustics, computational modelling, and biology. You are driven by a desire to understand complex phenomena and to contribute new knowledge that is relevant to technology and society, as well as to our understanding of biological systems.

More about being a doctoral student at LTH - lth.se

Work duties

You will primarily devote your time to your doctoral studies, which include participation in research projects as well as doctoral-level courses, seminars, and conferences.

You will be part of an interdisciplinary research project investigating the physical mechanisms underlying dolphin echolocation. The overall aim of the project is to develop and apply computational models in acoustics and structural mechanics to describe how the short, broadband ultrasonic pulses generated in the dolphin’s head propagate through tissues and other anatomical structures and are thereby shaped into a forward-directed echolocation beam. Particular emphasis will be placed on how variations in acoustic material properties, geometry, and potential reflective or refractive structures influence the direction, frequency-dependent shape, and temporal structure of the beam.

The work is interdisciplinary and lies at the interface of engineering acoustics, computational physics, biomedical engineering, and zoology/bioacoustics. The project also includes developing the technical aspects of the results into practically useful concepts for human-made technologies, for example medical applications in diagnostic ultrasound, underwater acoustic sonar systems, or non-destructive testing of civil engineering structures.
 
The work duties include:

  • research on the acoustic properties of relevant tissues and anatomical structures, for example by measuring sound speeds, densities, and attenuation properties, as well as assisting with anatomical CT imaging of the physiology of stranded harbour porpoises and related specimens
  • development of computer-based three-dimensional finite element models (FEM) of acoustic wave propagation in the sound-generating organs of dolphins and surrounding tissues, with the aim of creating a physically accurate so-called digital twin
  • collection and analysis of acoustic, mechanical, and anatomical data from toothed whales
  • development and use of computational and analysis code, with or without machine-learning components, in MATLAB and COMSOL or equivalent environments for model setup, post-processing, signal analysis, visualisation, and comparison between simulations and measurement data
  • collaboration with researchers in, among other fields, physics, marine mammal research, and computational sciences, acting as an interdisciplinary knowledge bridge between different scientific disciplines
  • communication of research results at scientific conferences and through the publication of scientific articles.

The duties may also include participation in teaching and other departmental work, up to a maximum of 20% of working hours.

Qualifications

Admission requirements

A person meets the general admission requirements for third-cycle courses and study programmes if the applicant: 

  • has been awarded a second-cycle qualification, or 
  • has satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second cycle, or 
  • has acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad.

A person meets the specific admission requirements for third cycle studies in Biomedical Engineering if the applicant has: 

  • at least 45 credits at second-cycle level relevant to the subject area

Additional requirements

In order to complete the doctoral programme in question, the following are also required: 

  • Knowledge and skills relevant to the doctoral project and the subject area (e.g. engineering or theoretical physics, wave propagation, engineering acoustics, programming, modelling, bioacoustics, computational methods, electronics, applied mathematics, zoology, materials physics, etc.). 
  • Very good analytical skills, including problem-solving and data analysis. 
  • Goal-oriented approach, which may be demonstrated through perseverance and the ability to work methodically, in a structured manner, and with focus.
  • Good ability to work independently and to formulate and tackle research problems. 
  • Good collaborative skills (i e manifested as a willingness to share ideas, constructive approach to challenges etc).
  • Very good written and oral communication skills.
  • Very good knowledge of English, spoken and written 

Other qualifications (advantages)

For the doctoral programme in question, the following are considered as other qualifications: 

  • Master’s degree in engineering physics or theoretical physics, electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, mathematics, computer engineering, engineering acoustics, or another subject relevant to the research area
  • Knowledge of numerical computational methods and/or FEM-based modelling of physical problems
  • Experience of finite element modelling in acoustics and multiphysics
  • Knowledge of marine mammals, toothed-whale echolocation or other areas of bioacoustics
  • Practical experience of acoustic or measurement systems
  • Practical experience of measurement technology and electronics
  • Programming experience beyond introductory-level courses
  • Experience of working with computing clusters
  • Experience of classical machine-learning or deep-learning-based signal analysis.

jobs.title: Doctoral student (licentiate) in efficient cooling and overheating
jobs.department: KTH, School of Architecture and Built Environment
jobs.description_html:
Project description

Third-cycle subject: Civil and Architectural Engineering

This research project studies energy- and cost-efficient cooling for elderly homes in current and future climates. With KTH, property owners and engineering firms, you will use measurements, calibrated simulations, and techno-economic analysis to assess shading, envelope measures, water-based and borehole-free cooling for climate-resilient design and operation.

Supervision: Adnan Ploskic, Sasan Sadrizadeh and Amirmohamad Behzadi are proposed to supervise the doctoral student. Decisions are made on admission.

Admission requirements

To be admitted to postgraduate education (Chapter 7, 39 § Swedish Higher Education Ordinance), the applicant must have basic eligibility in accordance with either of the following:

  • passed a second cycle degree (for example a master's degree), or
  • completed course requirements of at least 240 higher education credits, of which at least 60 second-cycle higher education credits, or
  • acquired, in some other way within or outside the country, substantially equivalent knowledge

At least 60 credits at second-cycle level or above in civil and architectural engineering or subjects deemed directly relevant to the specialization. 

In addition to the above, there is also a mandatory requirement for English equivalent to English B/6.

Selection

In order to succeed as a doctoral student at KTH you need to be goal oriented and persevering in your work. During the selection process, candidates will be assessed upon their ability to:

  • independently pursue his or her work
  • collaborate with others,
  • have a professional approach, 
  • analyze and work with complex issues, 
  • present knowledge of building energy, HVAC, thermal comfort or building physics, 
  • present knowledge of building simulation (e.g. IDA ICE/TRNSYS/EnergyPlus), coding/data analysis,  (Python/MATLAB), measurement, monitoring or building experiment experience, 
  • present knowledge of optimization, techno-economic or statistical knowledge, 
  • present strong spoken/written English research experience and 
  • present experience from project work with industry or the public sector.

The ideal candidate has a master in building technology, services, energy, mechanical or civil engineering, building physics or related fields. 

The ability to communicate in Swedish, both spoken and written, is considered as strongly meritorious since it is needed during everyday work. 

After the qualification requirements, great emphasis will be placed on personal skills. 

Target degree: Licentiate degree

Information regarding admission and employment

Only those admitted to postgraduate education may be employed as a doctoral student. The total length of employment may not be longer than what corresponds to full-time doctoral education in four years' time. An employed doctoral student can, to a limited extent (maximum 20%), perform certain tasks within their role, e.g. training and administration. A new position as a doctoral student is for a maximum of one year, and then the employment may be renewed for a maximum of two years at a time. In the case of studies that are to be completed with a licentiate degree, the total period of employment may not be longer than what corresponds to full-time doctoral education for two years.

As a doctoral student, you are entitled to a workplace with many employee benefits and monthly salary according to KTH’s Doctoral student salary agreement. Read more about Doctoral studies (PhD) | KTH | Sweden.

Applications must include the following elements:

Third-cycle subject: Production engineering

We are seeking a motivated PhD student to develop AI and robotic methods for adaptive manufacturing systems, with a particular focus on agentic and embodied AI. The research addresses how robots and intelligent production systems can perceive changing conditions, reason about process requirements and constraints, and adapt their actions in real time. The project brings together task level decision intelligence, multimodal perception, digital twin based learning and robot control to enable more flexible and intelligent manufacturing.

The division for Concrete Structures at KTH Civil and Architectural Engineering is in search for a doctoral student to be assigned a project on hydraulic design of structures within hydropower. Many dam facilities have been rebuilt or are to be upgraded to achieve a higher level of safety. A bottom outlet is a critical structure from both a dam safety and operational point of view. Emergency lowering of a reservoir's water level is entirely dependent on it and the outlet can also be used in the event of a spillway overflow. To ensure safe operation and long service life, it is necessary to understand the mechanisms and take appropriate measures.

jobs.title: Doctoral student on structural rehabilitation of concrete hydro dams
jobs.department: KTH, School of Architecture and Built Environment
jobs.description_html:
Project description

Third-cycle subject: Civil and Architectural Engineering

The division for Concrete Structures at KTH Civil and Architectural Engineering is in search for a doctoral student to be assigned a project on reinforced concrete structures within hydropower. Dams in Sweden and many other countries are aging and have an average age of over 50 years. Spillways and associated concrete structures play a crucial role in reducing the risk of dam overflow and serious damage. However, over the years, these have been exposed to varying flows, including extreme high flows, which in many cases has caused damage. The most common repair method today is underwater concrete casting, which is costly and experience shows that many such repairs do not last as long as planned.

The project is part of a national research program within the hydropower area called SVC – Swedish Centre for Sustainable Hydropower. The research is carried out together with senior researchers at KTH and in interdisciplinary research collaboration with international researchers and industry partners. The aim is to create a better understanding of how damage occurs, what forces and hydraulic loads act, and how these affect both concrete and the rock subsurface. The project is expected to provide decision-making information for maintenance, repair and reconstruction of embankments and associated structures.

jobs.title: Doctoral student on structural health monitoring of concrete hydro dams
jobs.department: KTH, School of Architecture and Built Environment
jobs.description_html:
Project description

Third-cycle subject: Civil and Architectural Engineering

The division for Concrete Structures at KTH Civil and Architectural Engineering is in search for a doctoral student to be assigned a project on reinforced concrete structures within hydropower. Dams in Sweden and many other countries are aging and have an average age of over 50 years. As they age, damage becomes more common. Typical visible damage includes cracks, leaching and scratching of the concrete surface and can be detected by visual inspections. However, there are also many other types of damage that may be more difficult to detect, such as reinforcement corrosion. In order to maintain older dams in full operation with a high level of safety, the response of the dams should be continuously monitored.

The project is part of a national research program within the hydropower area called SVC – Swedish Centre for Sustainable Hydropower. The research is carried out together with senior researchers at KTH and in interdisciplinary research collaboration with international researchers and industry partners. The aim is to create a good understanding of the structural response of concrete dams during normal operation, what should be measured and where sensors should be placed. The project will also identify which types of sensors are appropriate to use and identify reasonable alarm limits.

Third-cycle subject: Sustainability studies

We are seeking applicants with an interest in wetland restoration as a nature-based solution for sustainable water supply under changing climate conditions. The  will combine methods such as policy analysis, value mapping, socio-economic analysis, and qualitative research methods. The overall aim is to develop policy and valuation frameworks that link wetland indicators to societal benefits and costs, as well as to practical policy instruments and financing mechanisms. The successful applicant will primarily contribute to: (1) developing policy-relevant indicators for the water-related benefits of restored wetlands and exploring how these can be translated into information relevant for valuation, decision-making, and policy development; and (2) analyzing and mapping the values generated by wetland restoration for different stakeholders and society as a whole, including benefits, costs, and risks, as well as how these are distributed among different actors.

The work will be carried out in close collaboration with researchers and societal stakeholders in two interdisciplinary research projects. The position is based at the Department of Sustainable Development, Environmental Science and Engineering (SEED).

Third-cycle subject: Applied Physics or Biotechnology

Hormones shape metabolism, fertility, mood and sleep, yet they are rarely measured, and then mostly by blood tests in a clinic. In the Hormones Project, funded by KTH InspireLab, we are developing an affordable optical system that measures six hormones in urine, at home, every day. jobs.title: Doctoral student in Organizational Implications of Artificial Intelligence
jobs.department: KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Industrial Engineering and Management
jobs.description_html:
Project description

Third-cycle subject: Industrial Economics and Management

The deployment of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has expanded rapidly across public and private sectors. AI-driven technologies—particularly machine learning algorithms and large language models —are becoming integral to knowledge creation, task augmentation, and business analytics. This shift has catalyzed a rise of AI ecosystems, which brings together AI startups, intermediaries, and established enterprises, fundamentally reshaping how employees, businesses, and entire industries function. However, while certain use cases offer efficiency gains, organizations frequently grapple with critical challenges, such as low returns on investment, output unreliability, and pressing ethical dilemmas.

This PhD project aims to critically analyze the organizational implications of AI. The PhD student may explore questions such as, but not limited to: How do organizations mitigate the managerial challenges stemming from the probabilistic nature of AI technologies? How will AI transform the modern industry; and what are the opportunities and risks associated with such transformation? Along with the Big Tech companies and AI giants, what role do startups and intermediaries play in a more responsible transformation towards AI-based economy?

The PhD position is a part of the Wallenberg AI, Autonomous Systems and Software Program - Humanity and Society (WASP-HS), a national research program in Sweden. WASP-HS fosters novel interdisciplinary knowledge about AI and autonomous systems and their impact on humanity and society. WASP-HS enables cutting-edge research, expertise, and capacity building in the social sciences and humanities. For more information, see here.

Supervision: Emrah Karakaya will be the main supervisor and Mats Engwall will be the co-supervisor. Decisions are made on admission. 

Admission requirements

To be admitted to postgraduate education (Chapter 7, 39 § Swedish Higher Education Ordinance), the applicant must have basic eligibility in accordance with either of the following:

  • passed a second cycle degree (for example a master's degree), or
  • completed course requirements of at least 240 higher education credits, of which at least 60 second-cycle higher education credits, or

jobs.department: KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Engineering Sciences
jobs.description_html:
Project description

Third-cycle subject: Engineering Mechanics

FLOW is a strong community of researchers engaged in fundamental and applied research in fluid mechanics within the department of Engineering Mechanics.

We are currently seeking a PhD student in probabilistic machine learning to join the Fluids and Surfaces Group within FLOW. AI is becoming a critical investment across science and engineering, but fluid mechanics poses particular challenges: flows are often high-dimensional and chaotic, and couple physical processes across many scales.

This position offers an exciting opportunity for a highly motivated candidate to develop trustworthy probabilistic methods for inference, optimization and data assimilation. These methods will integrate simulations and experimental data into reliable tools for the design, prediction and control of complex fluid systems.

The work focuses on turbulent flows that carry electric charge, as found for example in power transformers. These systems involve coupled processes that are only partly understood, and measurements are sparse and costly. This makes them an ideal testbed, where models must be calibrated, uncertainties quantified and experiments chosen with care, with direct impact on safer and more sustainable power infrastructure. The project is funded by Digital Futures och Hitachi Energy

jobs.department: KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
jobs.description_html:
Project description

Third-cycle subject: Electrical Engineering 

The provision of plasma-facing components (PFCs) with sufficient lifetime is one of the major technological obstacles to be overcome in developing fusion reactors. Recently, the damage of PFCs due to interaction with runaway electrons (RE) has become a highly critical issue in evaluations of disruption consequences. ITER, currently seeks for the validation of relevant numerical models and tools against existing experimental evidence in order to gain confidence in their applications to predictive reactor modelling.

PhD project will focus on the development of modelling tools for simulations of RE-induced PFC damage and their validation against data from EUROfusion Consortium, and DIII-D (USA). The validated models will be employed for predictive modelling of specific ITER scenarios following input from the ITER Organization. The modelling of MeV RE energy deposition in PFCs will be performed with Monte Carlo simulations. These results will serve as input for the thermomechanical models to be developed in FEM and CFD software to address severe deformation and potential explosion of the material.

We offer expertise in the theory and modelling of plasma-surface interactions and electron transport into matter, access to state-of-the-art experimental data from the largest tokamaks worldwide and close collaboration with the Experiments & Plasma Operation Section of the ITER Organization.

Supervision: Prof. S. Ratynskaia. Decisions are made on admission.

Projektbeskrivning

Forskarutbildningsämne: Kemi

Doktoranden ska vara med och utveckla metoder och program för att göra kvantmekaniska simuleringar av stora molekylära system. Målet är att utveckla program för att skala sådana simuleringar till världens största datorer. Vi söker dig om är djupt kunnig i parallellprogrammering på GPU:er och har en grundläggande kunskap om kvantkemi. Finansiering för 4 års studier tillhandahålls av handledaren. Du blir en del av avdelningen för Teoretisk kemi och biologi och rapporterar till handledaren Patrick Norman.

Handledning: Patrick Norman. Beslut tas vid antagning. 

Behörighet för antagning

För att bli antagen till forskarutbildning (kap 7 39 § högskoleförordningen) krävs att den sökande har grundläggande behörighet:

  • avlagt en examen på avancerad nivå, eller
  • fullgjort kursfordringar om minst 240 högskolepoäng, varav minst 60 högskolepoäng på avancerad nivå, eller
  • på något annat sätt inom eller utom landet förvärvat i huvudsak motsvarande kunskaper.

För denna tjänst krävs även kunskaper i programmering av GPU:er på avancerad nivå med CUDA samt grundäggande kunskaper i kvantkemi och täthetsfunktionalteori.

Utöver ovanstående  finns också ett obligatoriskt krav på engelska motsvarande Engelska B/6.

jobs.title: PhD student in plant demography
jobs.department: Uppsala University, Department of Ecology and Genetics
jobs.description_html:
Do you want to conduct research on the population ecology of plants? Do you want to join an outstanding academic environment at Uppsala University’s Evolutionary Biology Centre? We are now looking to recruit a PhD student who wishes to begin their research career together with us.

The Department of Ecology and Genetics (IEG) Department of Ecology and Genetics – Uppsala University at the Evolutionary Biology Center (EBC) is an international environment with staff that conducts research to understand ecological and evolutionary processes across all levels of biological organization. IEG provides access to advanced national and local research infrastructures, including free super computing resources (NAISS) and the latest molecular technologies and sequencing platforms (SciLifeLab platforms). IEG hosts a Climate Lab with controlled environmental chambers, greenhouses and a state-of-the-art molecular lab. PhD-students at IEG can join the PhD school which provides ample opportunities for networking on and off campus with PhD-students from the other two biology departments at Uppsala University (The Department of Organismal Biology, and the Department of Cellular and Molecular Biology).

The position is offered by the research program in Plant Ecology and Evolution at IEG. Information about the program’s current research can be found here.

Duties
The PhD project will address central current questions about plant life history and population dynamics, with focus on how demographic parameters (survival and reproduction) are affected by plant ageing and how environmental factors influence the same “vital rates” and thus the dynamics and distribution patterns of populations. The goals of the research will be to address key basic ecological questions and to achieve knowledge on how environmental changes will affect populations and communities. For examples of our previous work on demographic ageing see key papers here and here, and on environmental drivers of population dynamics here and here.

The main supervisor of the PhD candidate will be Johan Dahlgren. Specific aims and focus of the project will be decided together with the supervisor but will involve a combination of independent field work and mathematical modelling, and utilize ongoing long-term studies of Actaea spicata, Pulsatilla vulgaris subsp. gotlandica, and orchids of the genera Dactylorhiza and Gymnadenia. The exact balance between tasks will depend on the candidate's interests and the project's development.

PhD students at the Institute of Ecology and Genetics (IEG) have the option to engage in teaching and to develop their pedagogic CV by taking courses. The type and level of teaching will depend on availability and the student's interests but cannot exceed 20% full-time employment. The position and funding are extended by the time the student has engaged in teaching.

Requirements
To meet the entry requirements for doctoral studies, you must:

  • hold a Master’s (second-cycle) degree in biology with focus on ecology or a related field, or
  • have completed at least 240 credits in higher education, with at least 60 credits at Master’s level including an independent project worth at least 15 credits, or
  • have acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way.

We attach great importance to personal qualities such as motivation, independence, and problem-solving analytical skills. We value highly other personal qualities including initiative, creativity, and the ability to cooperate and collaborate with others. 

The candidate is also expected to:

  • have a valid international driver’s license,
  • have good understanding of central ecological concepts,
  • have experience with statistical analysis and population modelling, especially using the software R,
  • be highly motivated and curious and thrive in a collaborative environment,
  • be able to take responsibility for carrying out and finishing independent tasks and projects, and
  • express themselves at a high level in spoken as well as written English.

Additional qualifications
Experience with ecological field work, plant species identification and all forms of quantitative skills are meriting.

About the employment
The employment is a temporary position according to the Higher Education Ordinance chapter 5 § 7. Scope of employment 100 %. Starting date 1 April 2027 or as agreed. Placement: Uppsala.

Rules governing PhD students are set out in the Higher Education Ordinance chapter 5, §§ 1-7 and in Uppsala University's rules and guidelines.

Instructions for the application
The application must include:

  1. A cover letter describing yourself, your research interests, why you want to pursue a PhD, and why you are suitable for this specific position (maximum 2 pages).
  2. CV.
  3. A brief description of your education.
  4. A copy of your master's degree and course transcripts, as well as a copy of your master's thesis.
  5. Names and contact details of at least two references (email and phone number).
  6. Any publications.

For further information about the position, please contact: Johan Dahlgren, johan.dahlgren@ebc.uu.se.

Please submit your application by 18 January 2027, UFV-PA 2026/3293.

jobs.title: PhD student in Chemistry with specialization in Analytical Chemistry
jobs.description_html:
The Department of Chemistry for Life Sciences conducts research and education in analytical chemistry, biochemistry and organic chemistry. More than 100 people, including around 45 PhD students, work at the department. New employees and students are recruited from all over the world and English is the main working language. The department is located at the Biomedical Centre in Uppsala, which facilitates collaborations with research groups in biology, pharmacy, medicine and SciLifeLab and gives access to advanced infrastructure for experimental and theoretical studies. The international environment and good opportunities for interdisciplinary collaborations enables PhD students at the department to participate in relevant research projects and prepare for an international research career. You can find more information about us here.

Project description
We are looking for a PhD student in analytical chemistry to develop novel methods for single-cell analysis and quantification using direct infusion mass spectrometry. A key objective is to optimize sampling and ionization probes for sensitive detection of metabolites and lipids from individual cells, enabling studies of cellular heterogeneity. The project will involve custom-built analytical platforms coupled to high-resolution mass spectrometry and span the full workflow, from cell culture and experimental design to data acquisition, molecular annotation, and data processing. The work will also include development of targeted tandem mass spectrometry methods and reactive chemistry strategies for confident analyte identification and quantification.

As a PhD candidate, you will be involved in all aspects of the project and collaborate with interdisciplinary teams in chemistry, biology, medicine, and information technology. You will contribute to the development of innovative analytical methodologies through experimental work and  molecular annotation strategies. The position offers access to state-of-the-art instrumentation and opportunities to develop creative solutions for studying metabolites and lipids in biological systems.

The project is expected to result in internationally competitive research and provides excellent opportunities for pushing the boundaries of analytical chemistry and collaborating with leading researchers across disciplines.

Tasks may include
Independent planning, execution, and analysis of experimental work Method development, optimization, problem solving, and technology development Scientific collaboration within and outside the research group Communication of research results

The position is based in the research group of Prof. Ingela Lanekoff, which develops innovative mass spectrometry methodologies to address fundamental questions in biology and medicine. The group's research focuses on mass spectrometry imaging and single-cell mass spectrometry to reveal chemical processes underlying biological function and dysfunction. The group has secured several major research grants, providing long-term resources, access to cutting-edge instrumentation, and opportunities for international collaborations. More information can be found on the group's website and Google Scholar profile.

Duties
The main duties of PhD students are to devote themselves to their research studies, which includes participating in research projects and third cycle courses. The work duties can also include teaching and other departmental duties (not more than 20 % of full time).

jobs.title: PhD student in experimental nuclear physics with a focus on nuclear fission and gamma-ray emission
jobs.department: Uppsala University, Department of Physics and Astronomy
jobs.description_html:
Are you interested in working with experimental nuclear physics, with the support of competent and friendly colleagues in an international environment? Are you looking for an employer that invests in sustainable employeeship and offers safe, favourable working conditions? We welcome you to apply for a PhD position at Uppsala University.

The research conducted at the Department of Physics and Astronomy encompasses a wide range of physics topics, distributed over nine divisions. The department is located in the Ångström laboratory and employs nearly 400 people, 100 of whom are doctoral students. It offers a broad physics curriculum to undergraduate and graduate students, participation in nationally and internationally leading projects for researchers, and opportunities for partnership with industry and various outreach activities. Read more on www.uu.se/physics.

The Department of Physics and Astronomy, Division of Applied Nuclear Physics, at Uppsala University conducts research and education in applied nuclear physics. Its activities aim to deepen our understanding of the properties of atomic nuclei and apply this knowledge in areas such as energy and materials research.

The successful candidate will join an internationally active research group investigating nuclear-reaction dynamics and nuclear fission through experiments and modelling. Our research tests theoretical predictions and addresses fundamental questions relevant to nuclear physics and astrophysics. It also produces high-precision nuclear data for applications in nuclear-energy systems, cancer treatment, and radiation-tolerant microelectronics. The group collaborates with leading research facilities across Europe.

This doctoral project forms part of a Nordic collaboration between Uppsala University and the University of Oslo (UiO), within the Norwegian Nuclear Research Centre (NNRC). It brings together expertise in nuclear fission, nuclear structure, gamma-ray spectroscopy, detector development, and nuclear modelling. A substantial part of the experimental work will take place at the Oslo Cyclotron Laboratory (OCL).


Duties

The doctoral project will ultimately investigate how excitation energy and angular momentum are shared between fission fragments and subsequently carried away by gamma-ray emission. You will measure prompt fission gamma-ray spectra, multiplicities, and total energies as functions of excitation energy, and attempt to extract fission-product yields and isomeric yield ratios. These measurements will test our understanding of nuclear fission and provide data to improve predictions of gamma-ray heating and other fission observables relevant to Generation IV reactors operating with fast neutron spectra.

You will prepare and conduct experiments at OCL in close collaboration with researchers and technical specialists at UiO. The experiments will use the uranium-235(d,pf) reaction as a surrogate for neutron-induced fission of uranium-235. Detecting the outgoing proton together with fission fragments and gamma rays will allow the measured observables to be related to the excitation energy of the fissioning nucleus.

A central part of your work will be centered around the OSCAR gamma-ray detector array, charged-particle detectors, and a newly developed fission chamber. You will contribute to detector characterisation, calibration, commissioning, and optimisation of the experimental setup.

You will analyse the experimental data using coincidence techniques, detector-response corrections, background subtraction, and uncertainty analysis. Characteristic gamma-ray transitions will be used to identify selected fission products, while delayed emission will provide complementary information about fragment angular momentum through isomeric yield ratios.

The project also includes computational fission modelling in close collaboration with the nuclear data section at the International atomic energy agency. Using TALYS and fission models such as FREYA and GEF, you will assess how well current calculations describe energy sharing, angular momentum, and fragment de-excitation. Comparisons with the measurements will help identify model limitations and guide further development.

The position involves extended research visits to Oslo and may include detector tests and experiments at other international facilities. You will present your research in peer-reviewed publications, at scientific conferences, and in collaboration meetings.


Requirements

Applicants must meet the general eligibility requirements for doctoral studies through one of the following:

  • Hold a Master’s degree in physics, engineering physics, nuclear engineering, applied physics, or another subject relevant to the project;
  • or Have completed at least 240 higher education credits, including at least 60 credits at Master’s level and an independent project of at least 15 credits;
  • or Have acquired substantially equivalent knowledge through other studies or professional experience.

The position also requires:

  • An interest in physics, experimental work, data analysis, and physical modelling.
  • The ability to work independently and systematically, with attention to data quality.
  • Good collaboration skills.
  • Good oral and written communication skills in English.
  • Willingness and ability to undertake research visits abroad, particularly to Oslo, and participate in experimental campaigns and scientific conferences.


Additional qualifications

Desired qualifications that will be used in the ranking of the candidates:

  • Good knowledge of physics, including nuclear physics and radiation detection.
  • Programming experience, for example in Python or C++, and an interest in developing your scientific-computing skills.
  • Gamma-ray spectroscopy, coincidence measurements, or nuclear-fission experiments. Radiation detectors, detector electronics, or data-acquisition systems.
  • Experimental data analysis using ROOT or comparable tools.
  • Monte Carlo simulations of radiation transport and detector response, for example using Geant4.
  • Nuclear-reaction or fission calculations using TALYS, FREYA, GEF, or related codes.
  • Statistical analysis, uncertainty propagation, or detector-response unfolding.
  • Scientific computing involving large experimental or simulated datasets.

Rules governing PhD students are set out in the Higher Education Ordinance chapter 5, §§ 1-7 and in Uppsala University's rules and guidelines.
