jobs.title: PhD student - Traumatic Brain Injury
jobs.description_html:
Team
A PhD position is available in the Neurogenesis & Neurodegeneration group at the Netherlands Institute for Neuroscience in Amsterdam. The Neurogenesis & Neurodegeneration laboratory led by Evgenia Salta employs transcriptomics and other molecular and cellular approaches to map the cellular and molecular complexity of the adult human hippocampus and dissect the biological pathways that are deregulated in dementia. The team employs primarily human postmortem brain tissue and iPSC reprogramming.

Project
The project is funded by the Dutch Research Council (NWO) Open Competition and is a collaboration between the Netherlands Institute for Neuroscience (NIN) and the Swammerdam Institute of Life Sciences (SILS) at the University of Amsterdam.
Repeated mild head injuries, the kind sustained by athletes, veterans, and victims of domestic violence, are increasingly linked to long-term memory problems and a higher risk of dementia later in life. Strikingly, these lasting effects can occur even when no visible brain damage is present. Yet, we still don't understand how repeated injury leads to memory decline, and there are currently no treatments that address these long-term cognitive consequences.

Beyond helping high-risk groups, this work may also shed light on Alzheimer's and other dementias that share similar underlying processes.

The research will be performed at the Salta lab at the Netherlands Institute for Neuroscience in Amsterdam. This is a joint project with the group of Carlos Fitzsimons at the SILS, University of Amsterdam.
This study is a follow up of our previously published work:
https://www.cell.com/cell-stem-cell/fulltext/S1934-5909(26)00142-6
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-49299-6

What you will do
In this project, you will investigate what happens in the brain after repetitive mild traumatic brain injury, focusing on the hippocampus, the brain region central to memory. We are particularly interested in long-lasting inflammatory and neurogenic alterations and the cells involved in them, including microglia, astrocytes and immature neurons. By uncovering these mechanisms, you will help us to identify cellular or molecular targets that could guide the development of future therapies.

As a PhD candidate in our group, you will use state-of-the art single-nucleus RNA sequencing pipelines to process postmortem human brain from donors with a record of traumatic brain injury. You will be in charge of sample collection and stratification and apply advanced computational pipelines to identify cellular and molecular programs involved in the hippocampal response to injury and the downstream cognitive effects. Ultimately, you will establish in vitro human cell models to probe causal relationships between candidate targets and cellular phenotypes.

What we expect from you
  • A Master’s degree in biomedical sciences, neuroscience or similar
  • Strong affinity and hands-on experience with coding and omics-related computational analyses are a prerequisite
  • Strong affinity and hands-on experience with single-cell transcriptomics are a prerequisite
  • Strong experience with (iPSC) cell culture is a plus
  • Excellent communication skills, as well as proficiency in spoken and written English, are expected
  • Strong organizational skills, methodical and structured approach to your work, rigor, accuracy and attention to detail
  • A reliable, collaborative team player who is easy to work with and delivers on commitments
  • Genuine passion for scientific research
  • Drive, persistence and positive attitude to tackle difficult problems that require iterative approaches, while systematically checking results against expectations to catch issues early

What we offer
  • A stimulating, innovative and dynamic international research environment
  • Opportunity to work with novel, exciting datasets and develop creative concepts and pipelines
  • A strong community of care, support and scientific challenge
  • Access to state-of-the art infrastructure and work conditions
  • Active mentoring, supervision and training
  • Opportunities for personal growth
  • A particularly collaborative setting between the NIN and the SILS
  • Possibility to develop your own projects and apply for third-party funding

The position is for a period of 4 years in total. The first appointment is for one year with the option for an extension for the remaining period pending on evaluation.

Information
For additional information, please contact Dr. E. Salta. e.salta@nin.knaw.nl
More information about the laboratory can be found on: Salta - Netherlands Institute for Neuroscience - Master the Mind (nin.nl) & https://saltalab.github.io/

jobs.title: PhD Position Indoor Thermal Natural Variation for Heat Resilience
jobs.description_html:
How do residents experience changing indoor temperatures? As a PhD candidate at TU Delft, you will combine citizen science, field data and modelling to help develop healthier and more energy-efficien.


Job description
Hot weather events are increasing, making adaptation of existing dwellings increasingly important to protect residents from unhealthy indoor conditions and limit future energy use for cooling. While we are instinctively drawn to natural conditions, residents are most of the time exposed to static environmental indoor conditions. Hot weather events can even amplify static conditions, for example through constant mechanical cooling. To support health and to lower energy use, current guidelines and standards allow for some variation. Yet we still know too little about how residents perceive and accept natural variation in indoor thermal conditions, and how this relates to building characteristics and resident behaviour.

As a PhD candidate at TU Delft, you will conduct research within the NWO-funded Nature 4 Homes project. Your research will address how natural variation in thermal conditions influences residents’ perceptions, acceptance and interactions with the building envelope under current and future Dutch conditions. This a unique opportunity to contribute to one of the most pressing challenges facing cities today: adapting existing dwellings to climate change while enhancing quality of life.

Using a citizen science approach, you will investigate indoor and outdoor thermal and ventilation conditions in existing dwellings in different regions of the Netherlands. You will combine measurements of environmental conditions with information about residents’ perceptions and behaviour and relevant building characteristics. A key part of your research will be developing new methods to characterize natural variation of indoor conditions in relation to outdoor conditions, and predicting this variation using climate scenarios and data collected in dwellings, in co-creation with residents, housing corporations and industy partners.

You will join the Architectural Engineering + Technology (AE&T) Department at the Faculty of Architecture and the Built Environment, TU Delft, under the supervision of AnneMarie Eijkelenboom and Philomena M. jobs.title: PhD Position Natural Building Skins for Heat Resilience
jobs.description_html:
Join us in developing the next generation of climate-resilient building envelopes.


Job description
As a PhD candidate at TU Delft, you will explore how nature-based building skins can transform existing homes into healthier, cooler and more sustainable living environments. Working at the intersection of building physics, architecture, ecology and user-centered design, you will develop innovative façade solutions that combine vegetation, circular materials and smart ventilation strategies to improve indoor comfort without relying on energy-intensive cooling systems.

This is a unique opportunity to contribute to one of the most pressing challenges facing cities today: adapting existing housing to climate change while enhancing biodiversity and quality of life. Your work will move beyond theory. Through co-creation with residents and industry partners, full-scale prototyping and real-world testing, you will help bring innovative solutions from concept to demonstration.

While green façades and other nature-based solutions have demonstrated their potential to reduce surface temperatures and improve urban microclimates, limited knowledge exists on how integrated nature-based building skins can simultaneously deliver indoor heat resilience, ventilation performance, biodiversity enhancement, circularity and long-term user acceptance within affordable retrofit solutions for existing housing. As a PhD candidate at TU Delft, you will conduct research within the NWO-funded Nature 4 Homes project. Your research will focus on developing and demonstrating natural building skins for the heat-resilient retrofit of existing dwellings. The ambition is to create an affordable and easy-to-install building-envelope solution that integrates nature-based solutions and passive cooling strategies to mitigate overheating and regulate indoor conditions, while supporting biodiversity and circular renovation.

We are looking for a curious and motivated researcher who is excited to combine experimentation, design and stakeholder engagement. In return, you will join a collaborative and supportive research environment where independent thinking, creativity and interdisciplinary collaboration are encouraged.

At TU Delft, you will have access to world-class research facilities, international networks and the opportunity to work on solutions with direct relevance to society and the built environment sector.

Your research will combine co-creation, prototyping, experimental testing and modelling. Together with residents, manufacturers and other stakeholders, you will identify user-acceptance, maintenance and practical barriers affecting the design, installation and operation of natural building skins and translate these into design requirements. Successive prototypes will be developed and tested at MATELab, TU Delft’s outdoor full-scale façade testing facility, under real weather conditions to assess heat resilience, ventilation, heat and moisture transfer, and indoor environmental performance. The developed prototype systems will be evaluated through circular-design principles, considering material efficiency, adaptability, reuse potential and life-cycle environmental impacts. Experiments may also involve users to investigate comfort, interaction and acceptance, while numerical simulations will extend the experimental findings across different building and climate conditions.

You will join the Architectural Engineering + Technology (AE&T) Department at the Faculty of Architecture and the Built Environment and the Department of Materials, Mechanics, Management and Design, at the Faculty of Civil Engineering and Geosciences, TU Delft. You will work under the supervision of Marc Ottelé, Alessandra Luna-Navarro, and Atze Boerstra. You will collaborate closely with a postdoctoral researcher and three other PhD candidates, as well as research, industry and public-sector partners. We foster an open and collaborative environment where independent thinking, knowledge sharing and interdisciplinary research are encouraged.

Job requirements
  • You hold an MSc in architecture, architectural engineering, civil engineering or a related field.
  • You have a strong interest in human perception, building physics, building design and climate change.
  • You are motivated to conduct a combination of experimental research, prototyping and environmental assessments.
  • You have an affinity with measuring and modelling and analysing indoor and outdoor environmental conditions.
  • You are interested in developing new façade design methods following circular principles.
  • You enjoy interdisciplinary research and collaborating with academic, industry and public-sector partners.
  • You have excellent oral and written communication skills in English. For more details, please check the Graduate Schools Admission Requirements.

TU Delft (Delft University of Technology)
For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow.

These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future.

At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional.

Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward.

Challenge. Change. Impact!


Faculty Architecture & the Built Environment
The Faculty of Architecture and the Built Environment has a leading role in education and research worldwide. The driving force behind the faculty’s success is its robust research profile combined with the energy and creativity of its student body and academic community. It is buzzing with energy, with four thousand people enthusiastically studying, working, designing, conducting research and acquiring and disseminating knowledge. Our faculty has a strong focus on 'design-oriented research’, which has given it a top position in world rankings.

Staff and students are working to improve the built environment with the help of a broad set of disciplines, including architectural design, urban planning, building technology, social sciences, process management, and geo-information science. The faculty works closely with other faculties, universities, private parties, and the public sector, and has an extensive network in the Netherlands as well as internationally.

Click here to go to the website of the Faculty of Architecture and the Built Environment.

Conditions of employment
Doctoral candidates will be offered a 4-year period of employment in principle, but in the form of 2 employment contracts. jobs.title: PhD position in-Operando Neuromorphic OptoElectronics
jobs.description_html:
As a PhD student, you will work on a project focused on developing in-situ optical sensing for polymer-based electronics: using light to non-invasively inspect, understand, and improve their stability and performance, with the aim to develop energy-efficient optoelectronic devices. You’ll select and design conductive polymers, fabricate electronics devices, then build in-situ UV-Vis/Raman/surface enhanced Raman spectroscopies platform to reveal hidden processes such as interfacial charge transfer, redox switching, doping and dedoping, morphology dynamics, and local electric field effects. You’ll model electrical and optical inputs and responses for energy-efficient computing as a proof of concept.

What sets this opportunity apart:

World-class facilities: Conduct your research at the University of Twente, a vibrant campus in the east of the Netherlands equipped with state-of-the-art facilities.

Expert guidance: Work alongside leading experts Dr. Ivana Qianqi Lin and Prof. Christian Nijhuis in the Hybrid Materials for Opto-electronics group, as well as renowned expert Prof. Frederik Wurm in the Sustainable Polymer Chemistry group, all within the Department of Molecules and Materials.

Interdisciplinary collaboration: You’ll be part of the MESA+ Institute embedded in the world-class NanoLab infrastructure, and collaborate closely with Department of Applied NanoPhotonics, and Centre for Brain-Inspired Computing.

This is your chance to contribute to a more sustainable future while advancing your research career at a leading European university. Join us in shaping the future of hybrid materials and forefront technologies!

jobs.title: PhD Position in Understanding Cellular Mechanisms Driving Traumatic Brain Injury-Associated Dementia
jobs.description_html:
Are you passionate about uncovering what happens to the brain during impact, subsequent injury, and how the injury evolves, or resolves, afterwards? Then we are inviting you to join our interdisciplinary research teams to explore the long-term effects of repetitive mild traumatic brain injury (rmTBI) in both humans and mouse models.

Join Us!
Repeated mild head injuries, the kind sustained by athletes, veterans, and victims of domestic violence, are increasingly linked to long-term memory problems and a higher risk of dementia later in life. Strikingly, these lasting effects can occur even when no visible brain damage is present. Yet, we still don't understand how repeated injury leads to memory decline, and there are currently no treatments that address these long-term cognitive consequences.

In this project, our main goal is to dissect the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying traumatic brain injury (TBI)-associated neurodegeneration, memory decline and dementia. To this end we will study how rmTBI triggers long-term neuroinflammation and cellular and functional changes in the hippocampus, leading to memory impairment, as TBI may weaken the brain’s resilience, accelerating hippocampus-related memory decline.

This project is a collaboration between the Fitzsimons lab at the Swammerdam Institute for Life Sciences, University of Amsterdam (UvA) and the Salta lab at the Netherlands Institute for Neuroscience (NIN). The complementary expertise and conceptual understanding of brain insult models, specifically TBI mouse models, transcriptomics, detailed analysis of cell morphology, advanced microscopy techniques, neurodegenerative diseases, adult neurogenesis analysis in human brain samples and human iPSC culture and derivation, establish an ideal conceptual and technical synergy, making our team very well-suited to identify disease mechanisms involved in neurodegenerative diseases associated with repetitive TBI.

This project is funded by the Nederlandse Organisatie voor Wetenschappelijk Onderzoek (NWO), Open Competition Domain Science – M2 grant and will be performed at the Swammerdam Institute for Life Sciences, University of Amsterdam. It is a follow up of our previous published work on traumatic brain injury and adult hippocampal neurogenesis:

https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-49299-6

https://www.nature.com/articles/s41590-022-01208-z

https://www.cell.com/cell-stem-cell/fulltext/S1934-5909(26)00142-6?_returnURL=https%3A%2F%2Flinkinghub.elsevier.com%2Fretrieve%2Fpii%2FS1934590926001426%3Fshowall%3Dtrue

https://www.cell.com/cell-stem-cell/fulltext/S1934-5909(26)00037-8?_returnURL=https%3A%2F%2Flinkinghub.elsevier.com%2Fretrieve%2Fpii%2FS1934590926000378%3Fshowall%3Dtrue

We welcome applications from candidates with diverse backgrounds, experiences and perspectives.

This is what you will do
As a PhD candidate in our group, you will characterize the short- and long-term effects of rmTBI on the fate of resident neural stem cells in the hippocampus, including neurogenesis, astrogliogenesis, reactive astrogliosis, production of inflammatory mediators and, microglia activation, hippocampal function and memory impairment in a mouse model of repetitive TBI. Moreover, you will contribute to the identification of conserved cell populations, transcriptional programs and intercellular communication networks affected by TBI in the mouse and human hippocampus.

For this, you will use an established mouse model of closed head rmTBI in combination with single-nucleus/spatial transcriptomics, cellular morphology, electrophysiology, behavioural testing, and molecular assays to identify mechanisms linking rmTBI to persistent hippocampal dysfunction and neuroinflammation. All the necessary techniques, expertise and training opportunities are available in our labs.

Tasks and responsibilities:
  • complete a PhD thesis within the official appointment duration (four years);
  • systematically and independently designing, performing and documenting experiments;
  • setting up and running bioinformatic pipelines to complement experimental work;
  • be an active and responsible member of both our research groups and discuss work with group members during departmental meetings and incorporate their feedback;
  • taking a leading role in writing manuscripts for publication in peer-reviewed journals;
  • participating in PhD training programme of the University of Amsterdam and The Graduate School Neurosciences Amsterdam Rotterdam (ONWAR);
  • assist teaching and supervision of Bachelor and Master students at the UvA.

You will get the opportunity to:
  • present results at (inter)national scientific conferences;
  • expand your academic, professional and personal skills;
  • contribute to science communication and outreach activities;
  • thrive in a team that values impactful research and mutual support;
  • combine the advantages that a collaborative project offers, such as access to state-of-the art research facilities at both the Swammerdam Institute, and to those at the Netherlands Institute for Neuroscience.

What we ask of you
Your experience and profile:
  • a master’s degree in biomedical sciences with a neuroscience specialization or similar;
  • a strong affinity and hands-on experience with experimental work with laboratory animals and/or molecular and cellular biology. Having an Article 9 certificate to work with laboratory animals is a pre-requisite;
  • a strong (proven) interest in bioinformatics analysis of complex datasets
  • fluent in English, both written and spoken.

You are dedicated, accurate, stress-resistant, a pleasant colleague, well organized and prepared to, and capable of working at 2 different locations.

This is what we offer you
We offer a temporary contract for 38 hours per week for the duration of 4 years (the initial contract will be for a period of 18 months and after satisfactory evaluation it will be extended for a total duration of 4 years). The preferred starting date is January 2027. This should lead to a dissertation (PhD thesis). We will draft an educational plan that includes attendance of courses and (international) meetings. We also expect you to assist in teaching undergraduates and master students.

Based on a full-time appointment (38 hours per week) the gross monthly salary will range from €3.204 in the first year to €4.051 (scale P) in the last year. This does not include 8% holiday allowance and 8,3% year-end allowance. The UFO profile PhD candidate is applicable. A favourable tax agreement, the ‘30% ruling’, may apply to non-Dutch applicants. The Collective Labour Agreement of Universities of the Netherlands is applicable.

Curious about our extensive secondary benefits package? You can read more about it here.

You will work in this team
The Faculty of Science has a student body of around 8,000, as well as 1,800 members of staff working in education, research or support services. Researchers and students at the Faculty of Science are fascinated by every aspect of how the world works, be it elementary particles, the birth of the universe or the functioning of the brain. The position is located within the team of Dr. Carlos Fitzsimons (https://www.fitzsimonslab.eu), part of the Brain Plasticity group of the Swammerdam institute of the Faculty of Science.

The Swammerdam Institute for Life Sciences (SILS) is located at the vibrant Amsterdam Science Park. SILS is one of eight institutes of the University of Amsterdam's Faculty of Science (FNWI). With around 240 employees, SILS carries out internationally high-quality life science research and provides education within various university programs. Research is also carried out in close cooperation with the medical, biotech, chemical, flavor, food & agricultural, and high-tech industries, and revolves around 4 main themes, Cell & Systems biology, Neurosciences, Microbiology and Green Life Sciences.

Within the Brain Plasticity group of SILS we study how our brain adapts to changes in an (often challenging) environment. We try to understand how plasticity is 'programmed', and how external factors like (early life) stress, nutrition, drugs, exercise or enrichment) can modify plasticity, and what role it plays in cognition and disorders, such as depression and dementia.

Want to know more about our organisation? Read more about working at the University of Amsterdam.

If you feel the profile fits you, and you are interested in the job, we look forward to receiving your application. You can apply online via the red button. We accept applications until and including 30 November 2026. Evaluation of candidates will begin immediately and continue until the position is filled.

If you have any questions or do you require additional information? Please contact:
  • Dr. Carlos Fitzsimons, c.p.fitzsimons@uva.nl

Applications should include the following information (all files besides your cv should be submitted in one single pdf file):
  • a detailed CV including the months (not just years) when referring to your education and work experience;
  • a letter of motivation;

  • the names and email addresses of two references who can provide letters of recommendation.

jobs.title: PhD position: PFAS free membranes for use in electrolysers
jobs.description_html:
Why apply?
This multidisciplinary project integrates electrochemistry, metal–organic framework-based materials, and membrane chemistry to develop the next generation of high-performance membranes and unlock new possibilities for advanced molecular separation and transport.

Can you design the membrane that powers the next generation of electrolysers?
Electrolysis and electrocatalysis have a key role to play in creating a more sustainable chemical industry. At the heart of these technologies are membranes that control the transport of protons and other species—but today’s proton exchange membranes rely heavily on PFAS-based materials such as Nafion®. We are looking for a PhD candidate to develop a new generation of high-performance, PFAS-free proton-conductive membranes. In this project, you will combine the unique properties of proton-conductive metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) with those of proton-conductive polymers to create innovative membrane materials. You will systematically investigate how molecular structure, composition, and membrane architecture determine proton transport and overall performance. Your research will span materials chemistry, membrane science, and electrochemistry. You will establish design principles for high-performance proton-conductive membranes and put your materials to the test in different electrolyser configurations. This is an opportunity to work at the interface of fundamental materials science and real-world energy technology, with the ambition to develop membrane materials that can help enable a cleaner and more sustainable chemical industry. The PhD students will be supervised by Dennis Hetterscheid (Leiden Institute of Chemistry).

What you bring
We are looking for an enthusiastic and motivated candidate who is excited to pursue an interdisciplinary PhD at the interface of electrochemistry, materials chemistry, and membrane science. The project combines electrochemistry, MOF synthesis and characterization, physical measurements, and electrolysis studies, offering the opportunity to develop expertise across multiple fields.

You hold an MSc degree in Physical Chemistry, Chemistry, Materials Science, or a related discipline, with a background in one or more of the following areas: electrochemistry, membrane chemistry, MOF synthesis, or materials characterization. Most importantly, you are curious, eager to learn, and motivated to work across disciplinary boundaries.

You will join a highly collaborative and international research team of PhD candidates, postdoctoral researchers, MSc students, and scientific staff. We collaborate extensively with research groups both locally and internationally, and work closely with industry partners to translate fundamental scientific discoveries into technologies with real-world societal impact.

We are committed to creating an environment where everyone can thrive. Our lab values diversity, accessibility, and inclusion in all their forms, and we strive to foster a safe and supportive workplace that encourages personal and professional growth, well-being, scientific integrity, and responsible research.

If you are excited by the opportunity to combine fundamental materials chemistry with electrochemical energy technologies and help develop the membranes of the future, we would love to hear from you.

Skills:
  • Hands-on experimental experience, with co-authorship of one or more scientific publications considered an advantage.
  • A strong interest in fundamental science and a genuine curiosity about understanding the principles underlying new materials and technologies.
  • High motivation for research, combined with a solid theoretical understanding of relevant scientific principles.
  • Strong organizational and time-management skills, with the ability to plan your work, work independently, and communicate your progress clearly.
  • Excellent written and spoken English.
  • A collaborative mindset and the ability to work effectively as part of a diverse, interdisciplinary team.

What we offer
Our goal is to work together to create a transparent and inclusive work environment in which everyone feels welcome and appreciated. Our organization is always evolving and we need your ideas for improvement and innovation to take us further. We want to devote attention to your personal development.

You can count on an enjoyable job within the socially relevant world of education and research. The University's challenging and international work environment is located just steps away from Leiden’s lively city centre or the bustling city centre of The Hague. We also want to work with you to devote attention to your health and vitality, for example with the fun activities we organize through Healthy University.

The position will be for a maximum of 4 years, and the candidate is expected to complete a PhD thesis at the end of this period. A contribution to classroom teaching (maximum 10% of the time) will be part of the responsibilities of the candidate, as well as supervision of BSc and MSc research projects that contribute to the goals of this PhD project.

We offer a stimulating and interactive research environment, free use of all state-of-the-art facilities, and a competitive salary.

We also offer:
  • An employment contract for 12 months initially, to be extended for 3 more years upon satisfactory performance. This contract falls under the CLA of Dutch Universities;
  • A salary between € 3.204,- and € 4.051,- gross per month, based on a full-time appointment (38 hours - PhD student);
  • A holiday allowance (8%), an end-of-year bonus (8,3%), and an attractive pension scheme at ABP;
  • Full reimbursement of public transport commuting costs for home-to-work travel;
  • Flexible working hours: as a standard, you are entitled to a minimum of 29 leave days on the basis of a full-time working week of 38 hours; you can also save for extra leave, for example by working 40 hours a week, and in this way accrue an extra 96 leave hours, or exchange 96 leave hours for a 36-hour week.
  • Lots of options when it comes to secondary employment conditions; we can, for example, discuss options for paid parental leave. Within our terms of employment individual choices model, you can exchange leave days and/or salary for benefits such as an advantageous sports subscription and bicycle scheme;
  • If your work allows it, hybrid working is possible within the Netherlands;
  • A home-working allowance (day and internet allowance) and attention for good workplaces.

For more information about employment conditions, see https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/working-at/job-application-procedure-and-employment-conditions

Where you will work

Leiden University is one of Europe’s leading international research universities.

Thanks to its committed and inspired employees, the university enjoys a leading role in academic research and education. Every year, Leiden University scores very well in prominent rankings. This means that, to maintain our position, the bar is set very high. Regardless of the work you do at our university, you are always encouraged to broaden your horizons, develop your talents and reach your full potential.

Faculty of Science & Leiden Institute of Chemistry
The Faculty of Science at Leiden University is a world-class faculty where staff and students work together in a dynamic international environment. It is a faculty where personal and academic development are top priorities. Our people are committed to expand fundamental knowledge by curiosity and to look beyond the borders of their own discipline; their aim is to benefit science, and to contribute to addressing the major societal challenges of the future.

The research carried out at the Faculty of Science is very diverse, ranging from mathematics, information science, astronomy, physics, chemistry and bio-pharmaceutical sciences to biology and environmental sciences. The research activities are organized in eight institutes. These institutes offer eight bachelors’ and twelve master’s programmes. The faculty has grown strongly in recent years and now has more than 2,300 staff and over 5,000 students. We are located at the heart of Leiden’s Bio Science Park, one of Europe’s biggest science parks, where university and business life come together.

The research is embedded within the Leiden Institute of Chemistry, with its long-standing traditions of excellence in research. Apart from a state-of-the-art electrochemistry laboratory, and excellent synthesis facilities, preparation and measurement facilities, unconventional nanofabrication equipment and experimental setups to measure ion transport will be designed supported by outstanding mechanical and electronic workshops. We foster an international and collaborative atmosphere and have close ties to other institutes housed within our Faculty of Science and with many research groups within the Netherlands, and many prominent labs abroad.

What we value
Promoting an inclusive community is central to Leiden University’s values and vision. We strive to be an open community in which all students and staff members feel valued and respected, and are able to fully develop themselves. We consider an inclusive academic environment, where students and staff can share their experiences and viewpoints, to be essential for the development of talent.

Want to apply or find out more?
If you want to apply straight away, click the application button.
If you would like more information about what the job entails, please contact Dr. Dennis Hetterscheid, at d.g.h.hetterscheid@chem.leidenuniv.nl. You can apply until 20 November 2026; You will receive a response to your application no later than two weeks after the vacancy closing date.

Your application should include a motivation letter clearly indicating WHY you apply for this position and project and WHAT makes you a suitable candidate, an extensive CV, the courses you took and grades you obtained in your Master’s studies, and the names and contact details of at least two references.

You will receive a response to your application no later than two weeks after the vacancy closing date.

If you have any questions about the procedure, please contact our management- & office assistent Angelo Philippi (a.philippi@lic.leidenuniv.nl).

jobs.title: PhD Candidate in Population-Scale Network Science (1.0 FTE, 4 years)
jobs.description_html:
About this position. In this 4-year fully funded PhD position, the focus is on devising new network science approaches for analyzing longitudinal, population-scale social network data on the Dutch population data, sourced from Statistics Netherlands. Such data presents distinctive methodological challenges: their scale and temporal character require fast algorithms and careful tailoring of commonly used network measures and algorithms.
One particular challenge for the candidate applying for this position, is to develop novel measures of structural (in)equivalence in social networks for obtaining an interpretable understanding of how social network structure differs between different subgroups of a population. Moreover, when applied to two entirely different populations, these methods of comparing network structure should facilitate cross-country comparative analyses of population-scale social network structure, enabling an understanding of similarities and differences in the social fabric of countries.
In addition to the above, there is also space for the candidate to pursue a direction of research related to network science that fits both the candidate and the broader aims of the group.

Embedding. The PhD candidate will be employed at the Leiden Institute of Advanced Computer Science (LIACS), which is the computer science and AI institute of the Faculty of Science of Leiden University. More in particular, the candidate will become part of 1) the interdisciplinary inter-university PLANET-NL initiative, which is a collaboration of the University of Amsterdam and Leiden University rooted in computational social science and network science, and 2) the Leiden Network Science group.
Both the research groups and the institute are highly international and feature a mix of disciplinal and cultural backgrounds. There are plenty of additional opportunities for other types of interaction and collaboration, for example at the Faculty of Science through the Leiden Complex Networks Network (LCN2) and nationally through the Dutch Network Science Society. The candidate will be asked to engage in (limited) BSc and MSc student (co-) supervision, small teaching assistance tasks, and potentially minor roles in scientific organizational activities.

What you will do
  • Conducting research in the area of network science;
  • Writing an article-based PhD thesis;
  • Engaging in collaborative research as a member of the PLANET-NL inter-university research group;
  • Membership of and engagement with the Leiden Network Science research group;
  • Co-supervising BSc and MSc students on topics related to data science and network science;
  • Engaging in minor scientific organizational organizing activities.

Where you will work
The Faculty of Science is a world-class faculty where staff and students work together in a dynamic international environment. Our people are driven by curiosity to expand fundamental knowledge and to look beyond the borders of their own discipline. The research carried out at the Faculty of Science is diverse, ranging from mathematics, artificial intelligence, computer science, astronomy, physics, chemistry and bio-pharmaceutical sciences to biology and environmental sciences.
The faculty is home to more than 2,700 staff members and over 6,000 students enrolled in nine bachelor's and fifteen master's programs. We are located at the heart of the Bio Science Park, one of Europe’s largest science parks, where academia and industry come together.
You will be part of the Leiden Institute of Advanced Computer Science (LIACS). LIACS offers the bachelor's programs in Computer Science and Data Science/Artificial Intelligence, as well as master's programs in Computer Science, ICT in Business and the Public Sector, Media Technology, and Science Based Business. jobs.title: Promovendus ‘Sociotherapeutische leefmilieu’s op woongroepen voor jonge mensen met dementie’
jobs.description_html:
Functie
Iedereen is verschillend en heeft een eigen persoonlijkheid. Waar de ene persoon behoefte heeft aan sociale contacten of uitdaging, zoekt de ander juist rust, structuur en veiligheid. Met sociotherapeutische leefmilieu’s (STL’s) stemmen we de leefomgeving binnen een zorginstelling af op de individuele kenmerken en behoeften van mensen met dementie die daar verblijven.

Binnen het landelijke onderzoeksprogramma YOD-INCLUDED zoeken wij een promovendus die onderzoek gaat doen naar STL’s op woongroepen en dagbesteding voor mensen die leven met dementie op jonge leeftijd. Juist voor deze groep sluiten de behoeften vaak minder goed aan bij het traditionele aanbod.

In dit promotietraject onderzoek je hoe STL’s momenteel worden toegepast binnen zorginstellingen met een gespecialiseerd zorgaanbod voor deze doelgroep, welke factoren implementatie bevorderen of belemmeren en hoe naasten hierbij betrokken kunnen worden. Op basis van een landelijke survey, observaties, literatuuronderzoek en interviews ontwikkel en verbeter je het zorgconcept. Vervolgens begeleid en evalueer je de implementatie in meerdere zorginstellingen in een haalbaarheidsstudie en ontwikkel je praktische materialen die implementatie op grotere schaal ondersteunen.

Zo draag je bij aan persoonsgerichte zorg voor mensen met dementie op jonge leeftijd.

jobs.title: PhD Position in Political Science
jobs.description_html:
The Department of Political Science is looking for a PhD candidate to work in the “Doctoral Network Democratic Institutions and Violence Network in Europe (DIViNE)” project, funded by the HORIZON MSCA action. The candidate will be supervised by Dr. Ursula Daxecker (University of Amsterdam and Max Planck Institute for Political and Social Science) and Dr. Hanne Fjelde (University of Uppsala) and join a network of 10 PhD candidates across five universities. At the University of Amsterdam, the PhD candidate will be part of the Amsterdam Institute for Social Science Research (AISSR) programme group Political Institutions and Identities (PII).

DIViNE brings together leading European research environments — UvA (Amsterdam), UESSEX (Essex), UMIL (Milan), UC3M (Carlos III de Madrid) and UU (Uppsala) — and partner organizations – including the new Max Planck Institute for Political and Social Science — to combine complementary strengths in quantitative conflict research, behavioral and experimental methods, historical and archival inquiry, institutional and normative theory, and applied policy engagement.

Join us!
Democracies are commonly seen as able to channel contestation through institutionalized processes and nonviolent action. Yet, democratic polities frequently experience a broad range of political violence — from riots and organized electoral intimidation to extremist mobilization and criminal violence — and violence can test and, at times, erode democratic norms and institutions. Moreover, democracies themselves may respond to perceived threats with measures (e.g., militarized policing, emergency legislation, selective repression) that threaten to undermine core features of liberal democracy such as the rule of law, civil liberties and institutional impartiality. The DIViNE Doctoral Network (Democratic Institutions and Violence Network in Europe) consolidates comparative, historical, theoretical and methodological strands to build a coherent new research program on political violence in democracies.

The position is part of WP2 on Democratization and Conflict Resolution, which explores the implications of regime transitions for patterns of violence. The PhD project analyzes endogenous processes through which political violence persists within democracies, focusing on how transitions reshape rent-seeking incentives, decentralization bargains, and relationships between national incumbents and local elites. It theorizes that democratization may inadvertently generate new incentives for electoral, ethnic, or criminal violence, depending on the nature of rents, types of institutional reforms, or elite-local configurations. Empirical work will combine cross-national statistical analysis, subnational mixed-methods studies, and process tracing in Global South contexts. The project will contribute a unified theoretical framework explaining why violence endures despite formal democratic reforms.

The doctoral trajectory includes a three-month secondment at Uppsala University and IDEA in Sweden, which will provide applied exposure to policy debates on democratization, institutional design, and violence prevention, alongside training in comparative policy analysis.

For more information about the network, consult https://divine.unimi.it/

What are you going to do
You will:
  • be affiliated with the AISSR and participate in its organized PhD training. The academic work is to result in a doctoral thesis that will be defended at the Faculty of Social Sciences with the goal of obtaining the degree of PhD.
  • conduct PhD research on democratization and the persistence of political violence, including quantitative analysis of data, surveys and survey experiments, and fieldwork interviews.
  • co-author publications with other project members;
  • take active part in DIViNE training network activities including network training modules, PhD colloquia, research workshops, secondments, and training workshops;
  • take active part of the research environment at the AISSR, including PII research seminars, AISSR center activities, among others.
  • teach Bachelor-level courses, depending upon availability and as suitable for the PhD schedule (for a max. of 10%).
  • assist with administrative responsibilities related to the project, such as the organization of workshops, conferences, or other project events.
  • make Amsterdam (or a location within commuting distance) your primary residence for the initial three years of the PhD project, and Göttingen (or a location within commuting distance) for the one-year extension. We will assist with finding adequate housing and with applying for visa and residence permits.

What do you have to offer
You have the following credentials:

Essential:
  • a Master’s degree or equivalent in political science or closely related discipline. The degree must have been obtained by the start of your employment;
  • an excellent command of social science research methods, including quantitative methodology such as panel regression, analysis of large administrative data, survey data, causal inference design, and statistical programming in Stata/R/etc.;
  • an interest to conduct fieldwork in the Global South;
  • excellent oral and written communication skills in English;
  • independent thinking and critical analytical skills;
  • the ability to work independently and in a team.

Desirable:
  • knowledge of regional contexts of special relevance to project members and supervisors, such as South Asia and Sub-Saharan Africa;
  • experience with qualitative methods and mixed-methods approaches;
  • expertise in research on political violence.

What else do we offer you
The position concerns temporary employment of 38 hours per week for a maximum term of three years at the University of Amsterdam, under the MSCA Doctoral Network employment conditions. The initial employment is for one year with an intended starting date of January 2027. Following a positive assessment and barring altered circumstances, this term will be extended by a maximum of two years. A one-year extension at the Max Planck Institute of Political and Social Science in Göttingen is envisioned. The employment should result in the conferral of a doctorate. We will put together a curriculum which will also include the opportunity to attend training courses and both national and international events. You will also be tasked with teaching Bachelor's students.

Please follow the links to learn more about the Department of Political Science and the AISSR at the University of Amsterdam, the Department of Peace and Conflict Research at the University of Uppsala, and the Max Planck Institute for Political and Social Science.

In this department, you will work
We offer a challenging work environment with a variety of duties and ample scope for individual initiative and development within an inspiring organisation. The social and behavioural sciences play a leading role in addressing the major societal challenges faced by the world, the Netherlands and Amsterdam, now and in the future.

To work at the University of Amsterdam is to work in a discerning, independent, creative, innovative and international climate characterised by an open atmosphere and a genuine engagement with the city of Amsterdam and society.

The UvA is an equal-opportunity employer. We prioritise diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for everyone. We value a spirit of enquiry and perseverance, provide the space to keep asking questions, and promote a culture of curiosity and creativity.

Please note that PhD researchers recruited on the project must satisfy the MCSA mobility requirements, which for this position means that they cannot have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the Netherlands for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before the recruitment date. Also note that the program will entail mobility across the institutions and partners in the network.

To apply, please submit the following five documents combined into a single PDF document with your name and the vacancy number in the document title:
  • a CV

  • a two-page proposal outlining a PhD project that fits the above parameters

Please do NOT include any other materials at this stage. No other materials will be reviewed by the committee.

jobs.title: PhD Position in Political Science: Militarization and Democratic Erosion in Latin America
jobs.description_html:
The Department of Political Science is looking for a PhD candidate to work in the “Doctoral Network Democratic Institutions and Violence Network in Europe (DIViNE)” project, funded by the HORIZON MSCA action. The candidate will be supervised by Dr. Abbey Steele (University of Amsterdam) and Dr. Juan Masullo (University of Milan) and join a network of 10 PhD candidates across five universities. At the University of Amsterdam, the PhD candidate will be part of the Amsterdam Institute for Social Science Research (AISSR) programme group Political Institutions and Identities (PII).

DIViNE brings together leading European research environments — UvA (Amsterdam), UESSEX (Essex), UMIL (Milan), UC3M (Carlos III de Madrid) and UU (Uppsala) — and partner organizations to combine complementary strengths in quantitative conflict research, behavioral and experimental methods, historical and archival inquiry, institutional and normative theory, and applied policy engagement.

Join us!
Democracies are commonly seen as able to channel contestation through institutionalized processes and nonviolent action. Yet, democratic polities frequently experience a broad range of political violence — from riots and organized electoral intimidation to extremist mobilization and criminal violence — and violence can test and, at times, erode democratic norms and institutions. Moreover, democracies themselves may respond to perceived threats with measures (e.g., militarized policing, emergency legislation, selective repression) that threaten to undermine core features of liberal democracy such as the rule of law, civil liberties and institutional impartiality. The DIViNE Doctoral Network (Democratic Institutions and Violence Network in Europe) consolidates comparative, historical, theoretical and methodological strands to build a coherent new research program on political violence in democracies.

The position is part of WP3 on Dynamics of Support for Violent Movements and Responses, which examines how democracies respond to violence and how these responses shape democratic quality. Many democratic governments increasingly rely on militarized policing, emergency measures, and “iron-fist” security policies that may temporarily reduce insecurity, but potentially at the cost of weakened accountability and distorted institutional responsiveness and constraints. WP3 analyzes the micro-foundations of public support for repression, the institutional incentives behind securitized policies, and alternative strategies better aligned with democratic principles. The PhD project, Militarization, Public Support, and Democratic Erosion in Latin America, examines the interplay between public support for militarized security, institutional legacies of civil–military relations, and democratic erosion. It investigates when and why citizens endorse the use of armed forces for domestic security, how exposure to violence and distrust in civilian institutions shape these preferences, and how public opinion interacts with institutional militarization and executive aggrandizement. Empirical work will combine survey experiments, cross-national quantitative analysis (drawing on datasets such as LAPOP, V-Dem, and Latinobarómetro), and qualitative fieldwork in selected Latin American contexts. The project will contribute to understanding how coercive governance becomes normalized and how democratic quality is affected by persistent militarization.

The candidate will divide their training between Amsterdam and Milan, acquiring expertise in mixed-methods research, Latin American politics, conflict analysis, and survey experimentation. The doctoral trajectory also includes a three-month non-academic secondment at Fondazione Giangiacomo Feltrinelli in Milan, which will develop skills in policy outreach, public communication, and engagement with human rights and security-sector organizations. jobs.title: PhD Position in "Modifying Synapses to Mitigate Alzheimer's Disease"
jobs.description_html:
Are you interested in the neurobiological processes of learning and memory, and how we can use this knowledge to make the brain more resilient to the cognitive decline seen in Alzheimer’s disease (AD)? Then this position might be perfect for you. Join us!

Join us!
Glutamatergic synapses are critical for synaptic plasticity and memory formation. The composition of their receptors can modulate resilience and sensitivity to memory deficits, in particular those induced by amyloid beta (Aβ), a major hallmark of Alzheimer’s Disease. In this project you will investigate whether and how modifying the composition of glutamatergic receptors at synapses, using both molecular tools and behavioral interventions, can reduce age-related cognitive decline in and thereby enhance resilience to AD pathology. In addition, you will study the role of engram cell ensembles in this process.

The position is embedded within the Memory and Plasticity team of dr. Harm Krugers at the Swammerdam Institute for Life Sciences, University of Amsterdam (UvA). This is a collaborative project with Prof. dr. Helmut Kessels (Cellular and Circuit Neuroscience group, UvAmsterdam) and Prof. dr. Paul J Lucassen (Brain Plasticity group, UvAmsterdam). The PhD candidate works in the respective groups where complementary and excellent expertise is available (e.g. electrophysiology will be combined with chemogenetics and behavioral interventions).

This is what you will do
You will use behavioral paradigms to assess learning and memory in a rodent model of AD. You will apply viral technologies to identify and measure the properties of synapses and engram cells and establish their role in memory. These techniques can include electrophysiology, proteomics, dendrite and spine reconstructions, chemogenetics, and memory engram-specific interventions.

Tasks and responsibilities:
  • complete and defend a PhD thesis within the official appointment duration of four years;
  • gain knowledge of the field through literature, discussions with team members and internal lab meetings;
  • contribute to the design of experiments, perform experiments in the lab and analyse and interpret results of these experiments;
  • take a leading role in writing manuscripts;
  • be an active member of the research teams at both the Swammerdam Institute for Life Sciences (UvA) and present results at (inter)national scientific meetings;
  • participate in the Faculty of Science PhD training programme;
  • assist in teaching and supervise Bachelor and Master’s students

What we ask of you
You are excited about science and have a particular interest in, and preferably have experience with neurobiological approaches towards learning and memory. You like a challenge and can combine work on preclinical rodent models with techniques like behaviour, electrophysiology, molecular biology and structural analysis. You have good statistical skills and experience with molecular tools and data-analysis. You are a team player and a pleasant colleague who enjoys being part of an interdisciplinary team of scientists. Finally, you have good time management skills enabling you to meet the projects’ deadlines for finishing analyses, reports and other deliverables.

Your experience and profile:
  • experience with learning and memory research.
  • a MSc degree in Neuroscience or related fields;
  • affinity and experience with performing animal experiments;
  • affinity and experience with common behavioural and/or neurobiological techniques;
  • good analytical, writing and presenting skills;
  • fluent in English, both written and spoken and the willingness to learn Dutch (in case not Dutch native speaker)

This is what we offer you
A temporary contract for 38 hours per week for the duration of 4 years (the initial contract will be for a period of 18 months and after satisfactory evaluation it will be extended for a total duration of 4 years). The preferred starting date of the project, which should lead to a PhD thesis, is 4 January 2027. We will draft an educational plan that includes attendance of courses and (international) meetings. We also expect you to assist in teaching undergraduates and master students.

Based on a full-time appointment (38 hours per week) the gross monthly salary will range from €3.204in the first year to €4.051 (scale P) in the last year. This does not include 8% holiday allowance and 8,3% year-end allowance. The UFO profile PhD candidate applicable. The Collective Labour Agreement of Universities of the Netherlands is applicable.

Besides the salary and a vibrant and challenging environment at Science Park we offer you multiple fringe benefits:
  • 232 holiday hours per year (based on fulltime);
  • multiple courses to follow from our Teaching and Learning Centre;
  • a complete educational program for PhD students;
  • a pension at ABP for which UvA pays two third part of the contribution;
  • the possibility to follow courses to learn Dutch;
  • help with housing for a studio or small apartment when you’re moving from abroad.

Are you curious to read more about our extensive package of secondary employment benefits, take a look here.

You will work in this team
The Faculty of Science has a student body of around 8,000, as well as 1,800 members of staff working in education, research or support services. Researchers and students at the Faculty of Science are fascinated by every aspect of how the world works, be it elementary particles, the birth of the universe or the functioning of the brain.

Krugers and Kessels are respectively part of the Brain Plasticity group and the Cellular and Circuit Neuroscience group (at the Swammerdam Institute for Life Sciences (SILS). SILS is located at the vibrant Amsterdam Science Park. SILS is one of eight institutes of the University of Amsterdam's Faculty of Science (FNWI). With around 240 employees, the Swammerdam Institute carries out internationally high-quality life science research and provides education within various university programs. Research is also carried out in close cooperation with the medical, biotech, chemical, flavor, food & agricultural, and high-tech industries, and revolves around 4 main themes, Cell & Systems biology, Neurosciences, Microbiology and Green Life Sciences.

Want to know more about our organisation? Read more about working at the University of Amsterdam.

jobs.title: PhD Candidate in the research project 'Entangled with Seaweed', case studies in Scotland
jobs.description_html:
Do you want to contribute to ethnographic research into the politics of valuing seaweed in Scotland?
The Leiden University's Institute of Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology, based within the Faculty of Social Sciences, is looking for an ambitious PhD-candidate to study the impacts of economization of seaweed as part of ‘blue economy’ strategies in Scotland. Research focuses on the impacts on coastal communities considering that in Scotland colonial legacies still influence patterns of unequal access to and use of coastal areas. You will work within the project ‘Entangled in seaweed: The politics of economising nature in Scotland and South Africa’ funded by an NWO Open Competition grant.

Project Description
The project investigates the impacts of economisation of seaweed as part of a global drive to develop ‘blue economy’ strategies. Seaweed harvesting and cultivation (as food, or fertilizer- and bioplastic ingredient) are increasing considerably and promoted as contributing to sustainable development. The project focuses on coastal communities in Scotland, which has developed a comprehensive blue economy strategy. Building on insights from political ecology and valuation studies and inspired by the multispecies turn in anthropology, this project aims to study local impacts of new forms of economisation of seaweed, and the possible contestations these may entail. It seeks to incorporate the ideas, interests, and knowledge from local groups who live from, in and with seaweed ecologies, examining how new versions of economisation affect local social relations, including the entanglements with non-humans these ecologies and economisations depend on. It does so by focusing on valuations of seaweed ecologies, based on an understanding of values as enacted through practices by all (human and non-human) stakeholders. The project employs a collaborative approach vis-à-vis research participants and a wider audience through a visual storytelling approach.

What you will do
You will work in a project team consisting of two PhD-candidates and researchers at Leiden University, collaborating with project partners in Scotland. You will:
  • Develop a research proposal in the context of the overall project theme, and conduct twelve months of ethnographic research in Scotland. An ethics review and contribution to the data management plan are included in the proposal development. Research includes historical document/policy analysis, participant observation, interviews, and the application of participatory visual storytelling methods.
  • Analyse research findings and write a dissertation that contributes to the objectives of the ‘Entangled with Seaweed’ project.
  • Actively contribute to the output and dissemination of the research project, which includes collaborating with the other team members on academic and non-academic publications, science communication, and the organisation of workshops, seminars and an exhibition.
  • Participate in relevant PhD-courses and masterclasses, organised in accordance with the guidelines of the Faculty of Social Science and the Institute of Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology. PhD-courses at the University of Edinburgh, our partner in the project, can be included in the individual training and supervision plan as well.
  • Participate in the PhD programme and other academic activities of the Institute of Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology at Leiden University. During your stay in Scotland you will also be able to participate in the PhD-programme at the University of Edinburgh as well as academic activities organised by the Scottish Association for Marine Science (SAMS).

jobs.title: PhD Position(s) Diffractive Electron Imaging of Surfaces
jobs.description_html:
Challenge: How do we watch material surfaces evolve?
Change: Building a surface-sensitive diffractive microscope.
Impact: Enabling high-resolution imaging of surfaces during operation.

Job description
We are looking for two PhD candidates to join the Curious Beams Lab at Delft University of Technology and develop a new approach to imaging materials surfaces with electrons. The positions are part of BEAMSurf: Diffractive Atomic-Scale Surface Imaging with Backscattered Electrons, an ERC Starting Grant project led by Dr. Georgios Varnavides.

Surfaces control many of the properties and processes that determine material functionality, from chemical reactions in catalysis to interfaces in nanoelectronic devices. Yet, observing surfaces at high spatial resolution while they operate remains challenging. BEAMSurf will develop a new scanning electron microscope that uses coherent backscattered electrons for diffractive imaging of surfaces, with the potential to overcome conventional resolution limits for low-energy SEM.

As a PhD candidate, you will help build the experimental and computational foundations of this imaging technique. The two PhD candidates will have complementary roles and work alongisde a postdoctoral researcher leading the instrumentation development.

PhD 1: Electron Optics and Experimental Imaging

You will help develop and experimentally realize the new electron-optical imaging platform. Working closely with the postdoc, you will design, characterize, and integrate miniature electron-optical components into a high-vacuum SEM. A central challenge is to separate the desired backscattered electron signal from the primary beam and direct it towards a dedicated detector.

Your work will span electron optics, ray tracing simulations, nanofabrication, vacuum technology, and experimental microscopy. As the project develops, you will also help establish the experimental imaging methodology and optimize the microscope for diffractive imaging.

This position is suited to candidates interested in building new instrumentation and working across physics and engineering. Experience with electron optics, electromagnetic simulation, MEMS, nanofabrication, vacuum systems or instrumentation is valuable but not required.

PhD 2: Computational Imaging and Surface Science

You will develop the computational methods needed to extract high-resolution surface information from coherent backscattered electron measurements. You will develop forward models and inverse-scattering approaches for reflection-mode electron imaging, using simulations and experimental reconstructions to understand the capabilities and limitations of the technique.

As the experimental platform matures, you will work closely with the instrumentation team to apply these methods to experimental measurements and establish high-resolution surface imaging. An important goal is to move beyond static images towards studying surfaces as they evolve, including processes such as oxidation, interfacial reactions, and electrically driven changes.

This position is suited to candidates interested in computational imaging, inverse problems, electron scattering, open-source numerical techniques, and/or surface science. Experience with electron microscopy datasets is useful but not essential.

Research Environment:

You will join the Curious Beams Lab, led by Dr. Georgios Varnavides, within the Microscopy and Instrumentation Techniques (MInT) cluster of the Department of Imaging Physics at TU Delft, Applied Sciences.

The MInT cluster brings together multiple research groups working across electron microscopy, from semiconductor inspection and metrology, to cryogenic electron microscopy for biological samples. The cluster has access to state-of-the-art field-emission SEMs and FIB-SEMS, with a new microscope being acquired primarily for this project.

More broadly, the ImPhys department provides an interdisciplinary environment spanning multiple imaging modalities, wavelengths, and length scaels, including extreme ultraviolet imaging, optical super-resolution, ultrasound and MRI, as-well as AI-based medical imaging.

Job requirements
We are looking for curious and motivated researchers who want to develop a new imaging technology from fundamental physics through to experimental demonstration.

jobs.title: PhD Position Optimizing Multi-actor Transport and Logistics Systems
jobs.description_html:
Would you like to develop new theory and algorithms for problems with multiple interacting actors? Are you interested in working at the intersection of game theory and mixed-integer optimisation?

Job description
Transport and logistics systems consist of many players with potentially conflicting objectives that continuously strive to maximize their performance. The competition and collaboration between these players can influence their decision-making, which is something that traditional Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) formulations with a single decision-maker cannot capture. The goal of this PhD is to develop novel methodologies at the intersection of operations research and game theory to address these problems. Applications can go beyond the transport and logistics domain.

Your research will focus on mathematical modelling and algorithm development for planning and operating multi-actor systems, taking into account that the actions of one actor influence the opportunities and performance of others. A central methodological component of the position is the development of scalable optimisation algorithms for large and computationally challenging problem instances. You will formulate mathematical programming models and design solution approaches based on techniques such as column generation, branch-and-price, and Benders decomposition.

You will be expected to:
  • develop new game-theoretic/optimization models for multi-actor decision problems;
  • design scalable solution methods for large-scale optimisation problems;
  • contribute to scientific publications in leading journals in operations research, transportation, and logistics;
  • communicate research findings to an interdisciplinary audience.

You will join the Transport and Logistics section of the Department of Engineering Systems and Services

jobs.title: PhD Position Quantum Physics - Rare-earth Ion single Photon Emitter
jobs.description_html:
Creating quantum networks with rare-earth ions

Job description
Silicon-based microchips are the essential building block of modern electronic hardware, such as computers and cell phones. Can silicon also play a critical role in building the next generation of the internet - the quantum internet? In order to realize a fully functional and scalable quantum network, we are developing highly coherent single photon emitters using erbium ions operating in the telecom C-band and directly embedded in a solid state crystal, such as silicon. Crucially, we are able to realize high-quality light-matter interfaces and directly enhance the photon emission into an optical channel using photonic crystal cavities. By leveraging different isotopes for long-lived and programmable quantum registers, we are planning on realizing all the critical parts for a quantum network using fully integrated and highly scalable structures.

In order to help us achieve our ambitious goals, we are looking for a talented and motivated person, with strong curiousity of rare-earth ion physics, single-emitters in solid-state systems or experimental AMO physics. The successful candidate will work in a dynamic team environment.
