jobs.title: Promovendus 'Samen beslissen over geavanceerde therapieën bij de ziekte van parkinson'
jobs.description_html:
Functie
De ziekte van Parkinson is een van de meest voorkomende progressieve hersenziekte. Naar schatting leven er momenteel rond de 67.000 mensen met parkinson in Nederland. Vijf tot tien jaar na de diagnose neemt de effectiviteit van orale medicatie vaak af en neemt de kans op complicaties van de medicijnen toe. Op dat moment komen de zogenaamde geavanceerde therapieën in beeld: diepe hersenstimulatie of continue toediening van medicijnen. Het kiezen van één van deze therapieën is een complex besluitvormingsproces waarin arts, patiënt en naasten “samen beslissen”. Enerzijds zijn ziekte kenmerken hiervoor belangrijk. Anderzijds wegen persoonlijke factoren, zoals leefstijl, dagelijkse routines, wensen en kwaliteit van sociale steunsysteem mee.

Doel van het promotie onderzoek is het 'samen beslissen' proces verder te personaliseren en een nieuwe (ondersteunende) keuzekaart te ontwikkelen. Hiermee beogen we te bereiken dat keuzes persoonsgericht en goed geïnformeerd gemaakt worden en dat tevredenheid over de keuze achteraf groter is. Het nieuwe 'samen beslissen' proces wordt ingevoerd in het Radboudumc en een aantal omringende ziekenhuizen. Dit vraagt een andere werkwijze en ook een aanpassing in de manier waarop het gesprek over de behandelkeuze wordt ingericht. Het promotieonderzoek richt zich op deze veranderingen in de zorg.

Word jij enthousiast om als promovendus je in te zetten voor dit project, om de zorg voor mensen met Parkinson te verbeteren? Dan ben jij misschien wel de kandidaat die we zoeken!

Als promovendus voer je de volgende taken uit:
  • Uitvoeren van literatuuronderzoek en een meta-analyse naar effecten en bijwerkingen van de verschillende behandelingen en het optimaliseren van de keuzekaart
  • Inhoud van “samen beslissen” gesprekken vorm geven samen met patiënten, mantelzorgers en zorgverleners.
  • Opzetten van een evaluatieonderzoek naar de impact van het vernieuwde “samen beslissen” proces en de keuzehulp in de klinische praktijk, inclusief werving, dataverzameling en analyse, zowel kwalitatief als kwantitatief.
  • Ondersteunen bij de implementatie van het nieuwe “samen beslissen” proces in het zorgpad voor geavanceerde therapieën, in de Zorg voor Parkinson regio.
  • Aanvragen van goedkeuring bij de medisch ethische commissie (CMO Radboudumc) voor de uitvoering van het onderzoek.
  • Inrichten en beheren van een datamanagement systeem.
  • Presenteren van bevindingen intern en extern, in het Engels en Nederlands, in de vorm van presentaties en (wetenschappelijke) publicaties.

Voor de implementatie van het zorgpad, inclusief de keuzehulp, werk je nauw samen met clinici uit het veld. Je ontvangt ondersteuning, supervisie en training gedurende het PhD-traject van een multidisciplinair en ervaren begeleidingsteam. Je sluit het project af met een wetenschappelijk proefschrift.

Voor kandidaten met een geneeskunde achtergrond bestaat de mogelijkheid om, naast het promotieonderzoek, om een beperkt aantal uren als trialarts aangesteld te worden op het Expertisecentrum voor Parkinson en Bewegingsstoornissen.

jobs.title: PhD in Art-Science-Action Integration & Challenge-Based Sustainability Education
jobs.description_html:
The Copernicus Institute of Sustainable Development at Utrecht University invites applications for a PhD position on the role of art-science-action integration and challenge-based learning towards transformative sustainability education.

Your job
The PhD candidate will investigate how higher education can prepare students to have meaningful contributions in complex sustainability challenges. Specifically, the PhD candidate will study how the integration of academic knowledge, the skills to make academic knowledge actionable in these complex challenges, and the use of artistic expressions can strengthen students’ professional impact.

A specific focus in the research lies on challenge-based learning environments, in which students from different disciplinary backgrounds work with educators, artists and societal partners on real-world sustainability issues. Situated at the intersection of sustainability education, transformative learning, challenge-based learning and arts-based interventions, the project combines scientific ambitions with the wish of the research having impact within Utrecht University and beyond. It aims to advance knowledge on transformative sustainability education while contributing to the development of effective and inclusive educational practices.

Your role and research
As a PhD candidate, you will develop and carry out an independent research programme within a broader project. Together with an interdisciplinary supervisory team and a range of academic and societal partners, you will explore how knowledge, skills and artistic expression can be combined to support sustainability learning and help students engage with complex sustainability challenges. Your research may address questions such as:
  • How can artistic practices contribute to cognitive, affective and action-oriented sustainability learning?
  • How can challenge-based education connect disciplinary knowledge with the experiences and priorities of societal partners?
  • What opportunities and tensions arise when artists, scientists, educators and societal actors collaborate?
  • How can skills be taught so that they enable action in practice?
  • What are the (educational or institutional) conditions that enable art-science collaborations that can have a real impact on student learning?

Your work will include designing and conducting empirical research in higher-education settings, analysing qualitative and/or quantitative data, and translating findings into both academic and practical outputs. Possible methods include interviews, surveys, observations, focus groups and the analysis of student work. The precise research questions and methodological approach will be developed together with the supervisory team.

You will also contribute to the evaluation and further development of sustainability skills and challenge-based courses, and help strengthen collaboration between educators, students, artists and societal partners. You will have opportunities to share your findings at conferences and workshops and to publish in international peer-reviewed journals. As part of the Copernicus Institute research community, you will also participate in relevant doctoral training activities.

jobs.title: PhD in Energy-Efficient Sensors and Computing Hardware from 2D Materials
jobs.description_html:
Are you eager to shape the next generation of chips using atomically thin materials? In this PhD position, you will develop 2D nanomaterials and devices for more energy-efficient sensing and computing. The project will be undertaken within the NanoComputing Research Lab in the Department of Electrical Engineering at Eindhoven University of Technology (TU/e), at the heart of Europe’s leading semiconductor region.

Information
In this PhD position, you will investigate 2D materials as a platform for next-generation sensing and computing devices. You will develop growth recipes for 2D materials and fabricate and characterize devices that could contribute to emerging energy efficient brain-inspired computing hardware.

What you'll contribute to
Specifically, you will:
  • develop metal-organic chemical vapour deposition (MOCVD) growth recipes for large-area 2D materials, such as MoS₂ and WSe₂, with controlled defect densities;
  • optimize transfer processes to integrate the grown 2D materials onto target device substrates, enabling heterogeneous integration;
  • develop scalable fabrication processes in the TU/e cleanroom (NanoLab@TU/e) for device arrays, including sensors and transistors;
  • engineer metal–semiconductor and dielectric interfaces to improve device performance;
  • characterize materials and devices, and work with circuit designers to link material properties to device and circuit performance;
  • publish your results in leading journals and present them at international conferences;
  • supervise Bachelor’s and Master’s student projects.

Your research environment
You will join the NanoComputing Research Lab (NanoComputing Research Lab), in the Integrated Circuits group of the Department of Electrical Engineering at TU/e. You will be supervised by Dr. Abhishek Singh Dahiya (project leader) and Prof. Aida Todri-Sanial. You will have access to TU/e’s state-of-the-art cleanroom and characterization facilities.

What we're looking for
A master’s degree in electrical engineering, nanotechnology, or a related field, with a solid foundation in semiconductor materials and device physics, and prior experience in the growth of nanomaterials (preferably 2D materials using CVD), nanofabrication processes such as atomic layer deposition, lithography, etching etc., and 2D material transfer process.

jobs.title: PhD Position: Transcranial Ultrasound Stimulation and Computational Affective Neuroscience
jobs.description_html:
Are you passionate about affective neuroscience computational modelling and transcranial ultrasound stimulation? Come and join our PhD project on approach-avoidance decisions under threat, funded by the ERC Advanced Grant HEART2ADAPT, and work with a dynamic team.

Why do some people remain calm and make flexible decisions under stress, while others freeze or flee? HEART2ADAPT aims to answer this question. We are developing a new model to understand how the body’s autonomic stress state shapes responses to threat and how the balance between sympathetic and parasympathetic activity supports adaptive decision making in dynamic environments.

Using state-of-the-art methods to track brain and bodily signals in real time – such as heart rate, posture and advanced neuroimaging – we will investigate how stress influences decision-making. A key component of this specific PhD project is testing causal mechanisms using transcranial ultrasound stimulation (TUS), including both offline TUS and the development of MR-compatible online TUS.

Funded by a European Research Council (ERC) Advanced Grant, the project HEART2ADAPT offers you the opportunity to contribute to protocol development, data collection and computational modelling of behavioural and neural data. You will apply TUS to key nodes of our model, including the amygdala, ventral striatum and dorsal ACC.

You will work closely with colleagues at the Donders Institute and the Behavioural Science Institute, as well as with international collaborators. Responsibilities may also include mentoring of BSc and MSc students.

Would you like to learn more about what it’s like to pursue a PhD at Radboud University? Visit the page about working as a PhD candidate.

jobs.title: PhD Candidate - Spatial multi-omics and single cell analysis of human diseases
jobs.description_html:
Welcome to Maastricht University!

Are you interested in developing and applying cutting-edge spatial multi-omics and single-cell technologies to study human diseases? At the Maastricht MultiModal Molecular Imaging (M4i) Institute, you will contribute to the development of next-generation technologies for biomedical research.

PhD Candidate - Spatial multi-omics and single cell analysis of human diseases
  • Our goal: We seek to advance the understanding of human disease by integrating spatial multi-omics and single-cell approaches. Combining molecular information across tissues, cell populations and local microenvironments enables us to uncover disease-driving mechanisms, identify novel biomarkers and support the development of more precise diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.
  • Your colleagues: You will join the multidisciplinary research environment of the Maastricht MultiModal Molecular Imaging (M4i) Institute, embedded within the Faculty of Health, Medicine and Life Sciences (FHML) at Maastricht University. You will collaborate with experts in molecular imaging, mass spectrometry, computational biology, pathology and clinical research. You will be supervised by Dr. Eva Cuypers and become part of M4i's vibrant and internationally recognized research community. The position offers extensive opportunities for method development, translational biomedical research and participation in national and international collaborations.

What you do
You will develop and apply advanced spatial multi-omics and single-cell approaches to investigate the molecular architecture of human diseases. The project focuses on mapping biological processes within complex tissues by integrating complementary technologies that capture molecular information across different spatial and cellular scales.

Using state-of-the-art platforms such as MALDI mass spectrometry imaging (MALDI-MSI), laser microdissection, spatial transcriptomics, single-cell omics, digital pathology and AI-driven data analysis, you will generate and integrate multidimensional datasets from patient-derived samples. In addition, you will contribute to the development of innovative workflows that combine spatially resolved molecular profiling with cellular-level characterization.

By linking tissue-wide molecular patterns to individual cells and their local environments, you will help reveal how cellular interactions and molecular pathways contribute to disease development and progression. The resulting methodologies will be applied across a broad range of biomedical questions, including cancer, inflammatory diseases, metabolic disorders and environmental health research.

This position offers a unique opportunity to gain expertise in spatial biology, mass spectrometry, computational analysis and translational medicine while contributing to next-generation technologies for biomedical research.

Are you ready to set the course for the years ahead? Then we’d love to meet you.

What you bring
We’re not looking for checkboxes; we’re interested in who you are and what you bring. Do you recognize yourself in this?
  • A master’s degree in Biomedical Sciences, Medicine, (Bio)Chemistry, Analytical Science and Technology, or a related subject
  • Proficiency in English (C1 or higher according to CEFR)
  • Hands-on basic laboratory experience in the molecular analysis of biological systems
  • Interest in and ability to carry out practical research activities, including experimental work, data collection and analysis.
  • The ability to communicate scientific information clearly and effectively, both orally and in writing in English.

Other experience / skills that would be helpful for the project:
  • Imaging technologies (example spatial mass spectrometry, spatial transcriptomics, clinical imaging techniques)
  • Mass spectrometry (theoretical and/or practical experience in reading mass spectra and understanding the information they provide about the molecular composition of samples)
  • Ion beams and ion optics (knowledge of the principles of ion beams and ion optics, including their role in the generation, manipulation or focusing of ions in analytical instruments)
  • Laser based imaging systems (knowledge of or experience with laser-based imaging systems and their application in imaging or analysing biological samples)Data science and data analysis (experience with data processing, statistical analysis and interpretation of research data, as well as familiarity with programming languages such as R or Python)
  • Biological sample preparation (experience with the preparation and handling of biological samples for analysis, including the safe handling of human biological materials in accordance with relevant laboratory procedures)

What we offer
At Maastricht University, you’ll work in an international, open, and engaged environment. We offer:
  • A 12-month contract (1.0 FTE) with the prospect of a 3 year extension.
  • A gross monthly salary between €3.204 and €4.051 (based on full-time employment of 38 hours per week). 8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% year-end bonus.
  • 29 vacation days (based on full-time), four additional days off (Carnival Monday and Tuesday, Good Friday, and Liberation Day), and the possibility to accrue up to 12 extra days through compensation hours.
  • Flexible working hours, a home office allowance, and the option to work from home.
  • Freedom and space to shape your work independently and develop your ideas.
  • A close-knit community of colleagues to collaborate and grow with.
  • A solid pension plan via ABP, company fitness schemes, and access to various university sports facilities.
  • An inspiring work environment in the heart of Europe.

jobs.title: Promovendus 'Evaluatie van een digitale COPD-coach'
jobs.description_html:
Functie
Ben jij nieuwsgierig naar hoe kunstmatige intelligentie kan bijdragen aan betere zorg voor mensen met COPD? En wil je wetenschappelijk onderzoek doen dat direct impact heeft op de praktijk? Binnen het DACIL-project zoeken we een enthousiaste promovendus die de effectiviteit van een innovatieve digitale COPD-coach gaat onderzoeken.

Over DACIL
DACIL (Developing A digital COPD companion for Improving Lifestyle) is een meerjarig onderzoeksproject gericht op de ontwikkeling van een digitale coach voor mensen met COPD. De digitale coach maakt gebruik van spraakanalyse, sensoren en kunstmatige intelligentie om verslechteringen van de ziekte vroegtijdig te signaleren en patiënten te ondersteunen bij een gezonde leefstijl. Het project wordt uitgevoerd door een multidisciplinair consortium van zorgprofessionals, onderzoekers, data scientists, AI-specialisten en maatschappelijke partners.

Jouw rol
Als promovendus ben je verantwoordelijk voor het klinisch evalueren van de DACIL-app. Je onderzoekt in hoeverre de app betrouwbare en valide informatie geeft over veranderingen in de gezondheidstoestand van mensen met COPD en of het gebruik van de app leidt tot betere gezondheidsuitkomsten.

Je werkzaamheden bestaan onder andere uit:
  • Het uitvoeren en rapporteren van studies naar de validiteit en diagnostische waarde van de DACIL-app.
  • Het opzetten en uitvoeren van een proof-of-conceptstudie.
  • Het ontwerpen en coördineren van een gerandomiseerde gecontroleerde studie (RCT) naar de effectiviteit van de digitale coach.
  • Het verzamelen en analyseren van gegevens van deelnemers over onder andere longaanvallen, klachten, kwaliteit van leven, leefstijl en zorggebruik.
  • Het nauw samenwerken met patiënten, zorgverleners en andere onderzoekers binnen het consortium.

jobs.title: PhD Position in ML-Based Interpretation of Geophysical Legacy Data for Mineral Exploration
jobs.description_html:
Develop and test new methods for deep exploration of sediment-hosted copper systems by integrating legacy seismic and well-log data with basin modelling, geochemistry and machine learning.

Job description
We are looking for a PhD candidate who is keen to explore how legacy seismic and well-log data acquired for petroleum exploration can be transformed into a new resource for deep mineral exploration. The candidate will combine quantitative geophysical interpretation, basin modelling and machine learning to investigate a challenging target: the thin Kupferschiefer horizon buried beneath the Netherlands and the North Sea.

The Dutch subsurface offers an exceptional dataset of more than 6,000 wells, including approximately 1,700 in which the Kupferschiefer has been identified, together with extensive high-quality 2D and 3D seismic reflection data and available cores. Yet these data were acquired and interpreted for hydrocarbon exploration. Recognizing and mapping a horizon a few metres thick at kilometers depth, and identifying features associated with its mineral potential, requires methods that can extract information across datasets with very different resolution, coverage and physical meaning.

The goal of this PhD project is to develop an integrated methodology for characterizing the Kupferschiefer and its geological context. You will analyse well logs to identify the target horizon and extrapolate it to wells where it has not yet been recognized. You will use seismic data for cross-well correlation and improved spatial characterization, and basin analysis to investigate the roles of stratigraphy, faulting and basin evolution. Geological, petrophysical, geochemical and mineralogical information will be integrated to identify characteristics and fingerprints associated with copper mineralization.

Machine learning will be an important part of this methodological development. You will establish robust and interpretable baseline models for well-log analysis and investigate approaches designed for sequential data, including convolutional and transformer-based models. You will also contribute to multimodal methods that combine seismic, well-log, geological and geochemical information while incorporating geological knowledge and physical constraints. A postdoctoral researcher will work alongside you for one year, focusing primarily on advanced multimodal and physics-informed machine-learning developments.

The research is part of the EU-funded INTELLIGENT project. Results from the Dutch basin will be combined with complementary studies by other groups working on the Kupferschiefer and related systems to develop a regional-scale mineral-system model and transferable exploration workflows. Your multidisciplinary research work will be carried out within the Applied Geophysics and Petrophysics Section and the Resource Engineering Section of GSE at TU Delft. Through close collaboration with TNO, the National Materials Observatory and partners from universities, geological surveys, research institutes and industry across Europe, you will test new methodological ideas within an international network and against a real, societally relevant exploration challenge.

Job requirements
Being creative and independent, you have the ability to conduct independent research and collaborate across geoscience, engineering and data-science disciplines.

You also have:
  • An MSc degree in geophysics, geology, earth sciences, geological or petroleum engineering, or a closely related discipline.
  • Interest in applied geophysics and resource exploration and machine learning methods.
  • Experience in scientific programming (preferably Python or Matlab).
  • Good writing and communication skills.

Experience in one or more of the fields below is considered an advantage:
  • Basin analysis, basin modelling or sedimentary-basin evolution.
  • Quantitative interpretation of seismic reflection data and well logs.
  • Petrophysics, low temperature geochemistry and mineralogy.
  • Machine Learning (deep learning and/or statistical learning methods).

TU Delft (Delft University of Technology)
Working at TU Delft means contributing to solutions that really make a difference.

For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow. These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future.

At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional. Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward.

Faculty of Civil Engineering and Geosciences
The Faculty of Civil Engineering & Geosciences (CEG) is committed to outstanding international research and education in the field of civil engineering, applied earth sciences, traffic and transport, water technology, and delta technology. Our research feeds into our educational programmes and covers societal challenges such as climate change, energy transition, resource availability, urbanisation and clean water. Our research projects are conducted in close cooperation with a wide range of research institutions. CEG is convinced of the importance of open science and supports its scientists in integrating open science in their research practice. The Faculty of CEG comprises 28 research groups in the following seven departments: Materials Mechanics Management & Design, Engineering Structures, Geoscience and Engineering, Geoscience and Remote Sensing, Transport & Planning, Hydraulic Engineering and Water Management.

Click here to go to the website of the Faculty of Civil Engineering & Geosciences.

Conditions of employment
Doctoral candidates will be offered a 4-year period of employment in principle, but in the form of 2 employment contracts. Followed by an additional contract for the remaining 2,5 years assuming everything goes well and performance requirements are met.

As a PhD candidate you will be enrolled in the TU Delft Graduate School. The TU Delft Graduate School provides an inspiring research environment with an excellent team of supervisors, academic staff and a mentor. The Doctoral Education Programme is aimed at developing your transferable, discipline-related and research skills.

The TU Delft offers a customisable compensation package, discounts on health insurance, and a monthly work costs contribution. Flexible work schedules can be arranged.

Will you need to relocate to the Netherlands for this job? TU Delft is committed to make your move as smooth as possible! The HR unit, Coming to Delft Service, offers information on their website to help you prepare your relocation. In addition, Coming to Delft Service organises events to help you settle in the Netherlands, and expand your (social) network in Delft. A Dual Career Programme is available, to support your accompanying partner with their job search in the Netherlands.

Additional information

When the outcome of the assessment is negative, the candidate will be informed. The processing of personal data in the context of the risk assessment is carried out on the legal basis of the GDPR: performing a public task in the public interest. You can find more information about this assessment on our website about knowledge security.

jobs.title: Promovendus
jobs.description_html:
In de zorg wordt elke dag een grote hoeveelheid ongebruikte medicijnen weggegooid. Dat is zonde, het is niet duurzaam en het kost onnodig veel geld. Er zijn verschillende redenen waarom dit gebeurt. De farmaceutische keten is vooral lineair ingericht: van producent via apotheek naar patiënt, en als het niet gebruikt wordt de afvalbak in. Redenen voor het niet gebruiken van medicatie zijn divers. Ook wet- en regelgeving maken het lastig om over te stappen op een circulaire werkwijze. Daarnaast weten we nog onvoldoende onder welke kwaliteitscondities circulair medicijngebruik mogelijk is, binnen welke wettelijke kaders het is toegestaan en hoe de bekostiging van de keten verspilling in stand houdt of juist kan helpen voorkomen.

Er zijn dus meerdere elementen die de transformatie naar duurzaam medicijngebruik in de praktijk tegenhouden. In het REMARK-onderzoek brengen we deze elementen in kaart en zoeken we naar manieren om wél circulair met medicijnen om te gaan, zodat verspilling wordt voorkomen. In dit promotieonderzoek breng je in kaart binnen welke juridische, kwaliteits- en financiële kaders circulair medicijngebruik mogelijk is. Zo draag je direct bij aan de transformatie naar duurzame zorg.

Projectomschrijving
REMARK is een uniek project waarin een breed consortium samenwerkt aan de transformatie naar duurzame zorg. Het is een samenwerking tussen Tilburg University, de Technische Universiteit Eindhoven, Erasmus Universiteit, samen met vele andere consortiumpartners, bijvoorbeeld zorginstellingen, apotheken, ondernemers en ketenpartijen.

Het onderzoek richt zich op de langdurige zorg, waaronder verpleeghuizen en langdurige psychiatrie. In deze context is nog weinig onderzoek gedaan, terwijl er juist veel impact te behalen is door de grote volumes van medicatie die wordt weggegooid.

Promotietraject: regelgeving, kwaliteit en financiering van de farmaceutische keten

In dit promotietraject onderzoek je welke stappen een medicijn doorloopt tot het bij de cliënt in een zorginstelling terechtkomt, en welke regels, kwaliteitseisen en geldstromen daarbij een rol spelen. Vervolgens onderzoek je onder welke voorwaarden deze keten circulair kan worden ingericht. Je werkt aan samenhangende deelstudies:

  • het in kaart brengen van de wet- en regelgeving rondom de farmaceutische keten in de langdurige zorg, op nationaal en Europees niveau, en het identificeren van de juridische ruimte en knelpunten voor het hergebruik van medicijnen;
  • het vaststellen van de kwaliteits- en veiligheidscondities waaronder ongebruikte medicijnen verantwoord opnieuw kunnen worden uitgegeven, bijvoorbeeld rond bewaarcondities, verpakking, houdbaarheid en traceerbaarheid;
  • het analyseren van de financiering en bekostiging van de keten: welke geldstromen en prikkels houden verspilling in stand, en welke bekostigingsmodellen maken circulair werken mogelijk;
  • het samen met zorginstellingen, apotheken en andere ketenpartners vertalen van deze inzichten naar oplossingen die de circulaire logistieke farmaceutische keten verbeteren.
  • Het samen met alle stakeholders uittesten in de praktijk van de oplossingen.

Zo is dit promotietraject niet alleen theoretisch werk. Je duikt echt de praktijk in en onderzoekt wat wel werkt en wat niet en waarom.

Jouw functie
Als promovendus krijg je de ruimte om wetenschappelijke diepgang te combineren met maatschappelijke impact. Je bent verantwoordelijk voor het opzetten en uitvoeren van de deelstudies binnen jouw promotietraject. Je werkt nauw samen met de andere REMARK-promovendi, met de onderzoekers van de universiteiten en met de consortiumpartners.

Je combineert verschillende methoden, zoals documentanalyse van wet- en regelgeving en beleid, ketenanalyses, interviews en expertsessies met bijvoorbeeld apothekers, zorgprofessionals, toezichthouders, zorgkantoren en zorgverzekeraars, en de evaluatie van praktijkpilots. Je vertaalt je onderzoeksbevindingen naar wetenschappelijke publicaties, die uiteindelijk samenkomen in een proefschrift. Daarnaast draag je bij aan kennisverspreiding naar de praktijk en het beleid, en presenteer je jouw resultaten op nationale en internationale congressen.

Je standplaats is Tilburg. De betrokken organisaties zitten op verschillende plekken in Nederland, waardoor je regelmatig op locatie werkt. Dat maakt de functie afwisselend en dynamisch.

Tranzo verzorgt de mastertrack Health, Wellbeing & Society en de mastertrack Sociaal Werk, in de Sociologie master. Er wordt van alle Tranzo medewerkers verwacht dat men een bijdrage levert aan het onderwijs, bijvoorbeeld in de vorm van verzorgen werkgroepen/colleges of nakijkwerk. Afspraken hierover worden met de leidinggevende gemaakt.

jobs.title: Promovendus Inclusie van Kinderen met Beperkingen
jobs.description_html:
Als promovendus werk je - samen met een breed consortium van praktijk en kennispartners - aan het onderzoeksproject OPEN: Opportunities for Participation, Empowerment and Networks. Learning together beyond social barriers for an inclusive society. Het OPEN-project richt zich op het versterken van de inclusie en participatie van kinderen met een beperking of chronische aandoening. Samen met kinderen, ouders, onderwijs-, zorg- en welzijnsprofessionals onderzoeken en ontwikkelen we praktische oplossingen die bijdragen aan een inclusieve speel-, leer- en leefomgeving. In drie Living Labs combineren we wetenschappelijk onderzoek met co-creatie en praktijkinnovatie, met als doel duurzame systeemverandering en gelijke kansen voor ieder kind om mee te doen en zich optimaal te ontwikkelen.

Binnen het OPEN-project onderzoek je eerst welke factoren inclusie en participatie van kinderen met een beperking bevorderen of belemmeren, met bijzondere aandacht voor belangrijke overgangsmomenten zoals de start van spelen in de buurt en de start op school. Daarbij breng je de ervaringen en perspectieven van kinderen, ouders en professionals uit onderwijs, zorg en het sociaal domein in kaart. Op basis van deze inzichten ontwikkel en test je samen met betrokkenen praktische oplossingen, tools en aanbevelingen die inclusie in spelen en onderwijs versterken. Daarnaast draag je bij aan de opbouw van een lerend netwerk waarin kennis, ervaringen en succesvolle werkwijzen worden gedeeld tussen praktijk, beleid en onderzoek. Tot slot werk je aan de verspreiding, zowel nationaal en internationaal, en implementatie van de ontwikkelde kennis en producten, zodat deze breed toepasbaar zijn en bijdragen aan duurzame en inclusieve participatie van kinderen in hun dagelijks leven.

Je maakt deel uit van het brede landelijk OPEN-consortium, waarin kennisinstellingen, zorg- en onderwijsorganisaties, maatschappelijke partners en andere stakeholders samenwerken. Als promovendus lever je een actieve bijdrage aan deze samenwerking en bouw je een waardevol netwerk op van onderzoekers en professionals uit verschillende disciplines. Hierdoor ontstaat een sterke verbinding tussen onderzoek, praktijk en maatschappelijke impact.

Het project start in januari 2027 en heeft een looptijd van 48 maanden

jobs.title: Promovendus Cardiogenetica: Cardiomyopathie en risicovoorspelling
jobs.description_html:
Welkom bij de Universiteit Maastricht!
Wil jij bijdragen aan een nieuwe generatie van gepersonaliseerde risicovoorspelling voor patiënten en families met genetische gedilateerde cardiomyopathie? Binnen het MIRACLE-DCM-project onderzoek je hoe specifieke genetische mutaties het risico op ernstige hartritmestoornissen en het ontstaan van DCM beïnvloeden.

Promovendus Cardiogenetica: Cardiomyopathie en risicovoorspelling
  • Ons doel: Het MIRACLE-DCM-project heeft als doel de risicovoorspelling voor patiënten en families met genetische gedilateerde cardiomyopathie (DCM) te verbeteren. Door mutatiespecifieke genetische informatie te integreren in bestaande risicomodellen willen we individuele risico’s op ernstige hartritmestoornissen en het ontstaan van DCM nauwkeuriger kunnen voorspellen. De resultaten kunnen bijdragen aan betere klinische besluitvorming en meer gepersonaliseerde zorg.
  • Jouw collega’s: Je werkt binnen een multidisciplinair team op het grensvlak van cardiologie, klinische genetica, epidemiologie en data science. Je werkt nauw samen met cardiologen, klinisch genetici, onderzoekers en andere betrokken experts en draagt bij aan de ontwikkeling van een online interactief risicoplatform. Het MIRACLE-DCM zal het primaire project zijn, waarbij er ook ruimte is om je eigen input aan het onderzoek te geven. Binnen het project zal de promovendus met vele (internationale) partners samenwerken.

Als PhD-kandidaat binnen het MIRACLE-DCM-project onderzoek je hoe mutatiespecifieke genetische informatie kan worden geïntegreerd in bestaande modellen voor risicovoorspelling bij gedilateerde cardiomyopathie (DCM). Je richt je op het kwantificeren van het risico op maligne ventriculaire aritmieën (MVA), het ontstaan van DCM bij asymptomatische familieleden en de toepassing van genetische risicoinformatie bij pre-implantatie genetische testen (PGT). Je analyseert patiënt- en populatiegegevens om verschillen in risico tussen individuele mutaties en genetische domeinen in kaart te brengen. Daarnaast ontwikkel en valideer je risicomodellen voor onder andere TTN en evalueer je de toegevoegde waarde van mutatiespecifieke informatie in bestaande risicocalculators. Je vertaalt complexe genetische en klinische gegevens naar kwantitatieve individuele risicoschattingen die kunnen bijdragen aan betere klinische besluitvorming.

Wat jij doet
Het onderzoek heeft een sterke translationele component, waarbij de resultaten worden vertaald naar klinische toepassingen en uiteindelijk kunnen bijdragen aan de ontwikkeling en actualisatie van nationale en internationale richtlijnen.

Een belangrijk voordeel van dit project is dat er al een omvangrijke database met genetische en klinische gegevens beschikbaar is. Hierdoor hoef je niet eerst zelf data te verzamelen, maar kun je direct aan de slag met het analyseren van deze gegevens en het ontwikkelen en valideren van risicomodellen.

Binnen het project houd je je onder andere bezig met:
  • Identificeren en karakteriseren van specifieke mutaties met een afwijkend MVA-risico binnen LMNA, FLNC en TTN
  • Analyseren en integreren van genetische, klinische en populatiegegevens
  • Toepassen en evalueren van bestaande risico-calculators voor genetische DCM
  • Bepalen van mutatiespecifieke risico’s op DCM-ontwikkeling bij asymptomatische familieleden
  • Evalueren van de meerwaarde van mutatiespecifieke risico-informatie voor klinische besluitvorming en PGT
  • Vertalen van onderzoeksresultaten naar een interactieve online toepassing en aanbevelingen voor (inter)nationale richtlijnen

Ben jij klaar om koers te zetten voor de komende jaren? Dan ontmoeten we je graag.

Wat jij meebrengt
Het gaat ons niet om vinkjes, maar om wie jij bent en wat jij meebrengt. Herken jij jezelf hierin?

Je bent analytisch en wetenschappelijk nieuwsgierig en kunt complexe vraagstukken vanuit verschillende perspectieven benaderen. Je werkt nauwkeurig en gestructureerd en bent in staat om zelfstandig onderzoeksactiviteiten te plannen, uit te voeren en kritisch te evalueren. Je combineert een onderzoekende houding met een sterke interesse in de klinische toepassing van wetenschappelijke inzichten. Daarnaast werk je graag samen in een multidisciplinair team en communiceer je helder met onderzoekers en zorgprofessionals uit verschillende vakgebieden. Daarnaast beschik je over:
  • Een afgeronde masteropleiding in geneeskunde.
  • Goede beheersing van zowel de Nederlandse als Engelse taal op minimaal C1 niveau volgens CEFR.
  • Aantoonbare interesse in cardiologie en/of genetica, bijvoorbeeld door een eerdere onderzoeks- of klinische stage binnen deze vakgebieden.
  • Ervaring met wetenschappelijk onderzoek en het analyseren van klinische en/of genetische data. Je kunt toelichten welke gegevens je hebt geanalyseerd en welke methoden je hiervoor hebt gebruikt binnen een onderzoek gerelateerd aan genetica of cardiologie.
  • Kennis van statistiek, biostatistiek en epidemiologische onderzoeksmethoden, bijvoorbeeld voor het analyseren en interpreteren van onderzoeksgegevens.
  • Ervaring met statistische programmeertalen, bij voorkeur R, is een pré
  • Affiniteit met genetische data-analyse en genotype-fenotypeonderzoek, waarbij je geïnteresseerd bent in de relatie tussen genetische variaties en klinische kenmerken of ziekteverschijnselen.
  • Ervaring met het schrijven van wetenschappelijke publicaties en/of werken met grote datasets is een pré.

Wat je van ons mag verwachten
Bij de Universiteit Maastricht werk je in een internationale, open en betrokken omgeving. We bieden:
  • Een jaarcontract (1.0 fte), bij wederzijdse tevredenheid wordt het contract verlengd met 3 jaar.
  • Een bruto salaris tussen €3.204,00 en €4.051,00 bruto per maand (bij een fulltime dienstverband van 38 uur per week), exclusief 8% vakantiegeld en een 8,3% eindejaarsuitkering.
  • 29 vakantiedagen (op basis van fulltime), vier extra vrije feestdagen, en de mogelijkheid om 12 extra dagen op te bouwen via compensatie-uren.
  • Flexibele werktijden, een thuiswerkvergoeding en hybride werken.
  • Vrijheid en ruimte om je werk zelfstandig in te richten en je eigen ideeën te ontwikkelen.
  • Een hechte community van collega’s waarmee je nauw samenwerkt.
  • Een goede pensioenregeling via het ABP, bedrijfsfitness en toegang tot een uitgebreid sportaanbod.
  • Een inspirerende werkomgeving in het hart van Europa.

Lees meer over de PhD-journey aan de Universiteit Maastricht, van de start van je onderzoek tot het afronden van je promotie en daarna.

Over de Faculty of Health, Medicine and Life Sciences (FHML)
FHML werkt aan gezondheid in de breedste zin van het woord: van molecuul tot mens, en van gezondheidszorg tot preventie. We leiden zorgprofessionals en onderzoekers op binnen innovatieve onderwijsprogramma’s, en doen baanbrekend onderzoek op het gebied van gezondheid en welzijn. Als onderdeel van het Maastricht UMC+ (MUMC+) vormt onze internationale en interdisciplinaire gemeenschap een unieke samenwerking tussen universiteit en academisch ziekenhuis, waar onderwijs, onderzoek en zorg samenkomen.

Over de Universiteit Maastricht
Aan de Universiteit Maastricht zoeken we samen naar antwoorden waarmee we de wereld vooruithelpen. Dat doen we samen met 23.300 studenten en 5.400 medewerkers, verspreid over 5 steden in de regio, 6 faculteiten en ruim 70 onderzoeksinstituten in de Euregio. Hier krijg je de ruimte om grenzen te verleggen en nieuwe kansen te ontdekken; voor jezelf en voor de wereld om je heen. Want echte antwoorden vinden we samen.

De vacature staat open voor interne- en externe kandidaten. Bij gelijke geschiktheid hebben interne kandidaten voorrang.

Bij Maastricht University nemen we graag zelf contact op met potentiële kandidaten. We vragen daarom vriendelijk om geen acquisitie of aanbiedingen van bureaus of tussenpersonen.

Universiteit Maastricht zet zich in voor het bevorderen en behouden van een diverse en inclusieve gemeenschap. Wij geloven dat diversiteit in onze medewerkers- en studentenpopulatie bijdraagt aan de kwaliteit van onderzoek en onderwijs aan de UM. Dit willen we mogelijk maken door middel van inclusief beleid en innovatieve projecten in samenwerking met studenten en medewerkers. We moedigen je aan om voor deze functie te solliciteren.

jobs.title: PhD Position: Biodiversity for Nature-Inclusive Dairy Farming
jobs.description_html:
In this PhD position, you will develop integrated and innovative biodiversity monitoring and data analysis techniques to aid in the decision-making of businesses within the dairy sector for the benefit of biodiversity.

Biodiversity recovery is essential to sustain resilient food systems, robust businesses and healthy societies. A transition to a more nature-inclusive dairy sector in the Netherlands would be pivotal to biodiversity recovery, because of its influence in shaping landscapes through land use and management, and because of its socio-economic relevance.

To properly assess the suitability and effectiveness of key performance indicators and the effects of management practices on local biodiversity, it is crucial to monitor, for example, breeding birds, bats, insect communities and soil life (depending on the KPI).

By adapting and developing biomonitoring techniques programmes at dairy farms that are in line with long-running or recently developed monitoring schemes, you will utilise the full potential of datasets and methods to quantify biodiversity gains resulting from nature-inclusive farming as well as the potential for further biodiversity recovery. Novel instruments such as DIOPSIS smart insect cameras, LED buckets and bat loggers generate huge amounts of biodiversity data from across the Netherlands and can be used to detect and identify biodiversity automatically.

National schemes like the breeding bird monitoring project, the butterfly monitoring scheme and the dragon fly monitoring scheme (standardised and coordinated by NGOs such as Sovon and Dutch Butterfly Conservation, and powered by thousands of citizen scientists) generate standardised long-term trends based on thousands of plots around the country. You will design novel, integrated analyses to quantify the effects on biodiversity from existing and new data while accounting for factors such as observers' bias, weather and surrounding landscape configuration.

In this project you will:
  1. Bring coherence across the diverse monitoring systems and KPI developed so far and adapt sets of KPI's suited to peat soils.
  2. Document the relationships between different nature-inclusive measures taken by heterogeneous farm types, and the different aspects of biodiversity and ecosystem services considered. The precise type of monitoring and the number and locations of monitoring points will be decided in collaboration with stakeholders.
  3. Further develop effective and integrated monitoring to guide decision-making in businesses and develop reward schemes.

Your teaching load may be up to 10% of your working time.

jobs.title: PhD Position: Multisynaptic Plasticity in Dendrites
jobs.description_html:
Are you an enthusiastic young scientist with a Master's degree in a neuroscience-related field? And would you like to figure out how plasticity at multiple synapses is coordinated within dendrites? Then you have a part to play as a PhD candidate in our research team. Put your ideas to the test at our green campus and push your boundaries in an internationally friendly environment.

Synaptic plasticity is considered to be the foundation of brain adaptation and learning. Multiple signalling pathways have been identified that are underlying synaptic plasticity of single synapses, depending on induction protocol and cell type. However, linking these molecular pathways to behavioural adaptation and learning turned out to be difficult. Under physiological conditions in vivo, multiple synapses will be activated simultaneously and plasticity pathways will inherently interfere.

In this PhD project, we will use a combination of single cell electrophysiology, advanced microscopy techniques and novel biosensors to examine molecular pathways underlying multisynaptic plasticity in dendrites of hippocampal CA1 neurons in brain slices.

Research in the Wierenga lab focuses on the formation and plasticity of inhibitory synapses and the interactions between inhibitory and excitatory synapses within dendrites. In this project, you will use two-photon glutamate uncaging in hippocampal slices to induce synaptic plasticity at multiple spines and you will exploit novel biosensors to study interactions between molecular pathways within the dendrite. Furthermore, you will explore how these interactions are affected by neuromodulators. Pilot experiments with four spine stimulation have shown that large calcium signals emerge within the dendritic shaft that continue even after the stimulation has ended, and that there are at least two modes of spine growth that seem to be regulated independently.

The research has the following objectives:
  1. To determine how calcium release from internal stores contributes to dendritic calcium signals.
  2. To investigate how PKA and PKC activity interacts with calcium signals.
  3. To assess if these interactions can explain the two modes of spine growth.
  4. To examine when and where molecular signalling molecules (aka retrograde messengers) are produced.

Your teaching load may be up to 10% of your working time.

jobs.title: PhD Candidate: Psychosocial, Environmental and Economical Impact in Non-Ischemic Cardiomyopathies
jobs.description_html:
Welcome to Maastricht University!

How does cardiomyopathy (heart failure in young adults) affect patients beyond their physical health? And how can we better understand how psychosocial and environmental factors, such as stress, obesity and physical activity, influence the disease process and patients’ quality of life and mental well-being? As a PhD candidate, you will use Health Technology Assessment (HTA) methods to study the psychosocial and economic impact of cardiomyopathy-related complications as well as the role of psychosocial and environmental factors in the disease process, and contribute to evidence on the value and cost-effectiveness of healthcare strategies.

PhD Candidate: Psychosocial, Environmental and Related Economical Impact in Non-Ischemic Cardiomyopathies (Heart Failure in Young Adults)
  • Our goal: The goal of this research is to understand how psychosocial and environmental factors influence the cardiomyopathy disease process and related biological changes in the heart, as well as their impact on quality of life, mental well-being and societal burden in young patients with non-ischemic cardiomyopathy. By combining clinical phenotyping, questionnaires, patient-reported outcomes, healthcare use, employment and cost data, the project aims to link these factors and biological and clinical findings to better understand, detect, prevent or treat cardiomyopathy complications.
  • Your colleagues & research context: You will join the Heart Failure Research team of Prof. dr. Stephane Heymans at CARIM and Maastricht UMC+ and work within a large Dutch research consortium. You will collaborate with the team of Prof. dr. Jan Y. Verbakel at KU Leuven, Department of Public Health and Primary Care, and work closely with the HTA and health economics group at KU Leuven. The research uses a prospective cohort, biobank and omics of more than 1,300 cardiomyopathy patients. You will be based in Maastricht (CARIM / Maastricht UMC+) and make regular working visits to Leuven. Supervision will take place by both Dr. Stephane Heymans and dr. Verbakel.

The project focuses on Health Technology Assessment (HTA) and on understanding the psychosocial and economic impact of cardiomyopathy-related complications. An important part of the research is to examine how psychosocial and environmental factors, including factors such as stress, obesity and physical activity, are related to the cardiomyopathy disease process and biological changes in the heart. Using a prospective cohort, biobank and omics, you will integrate clinical phenotyping, questionnaires, patient-reported outcomes, biosamples and multi-omics to study cardiomyopathy and associated psychosocial, economical, environmental and behaviourial conditions.

You will link these data to healthcare use, cost, work, quality of life, mental well-being, patient preferences and societal burden to generate evidence for HTA and cost-effectiveness analyses.You will have the freedom to identify their original projects, e.g. where biological findings in the heart (e.g. RNA/protein data) can be linked to psychosocial and environmental factors, as part of the gene-environmental interactions paradigm.

What you do
  • Quantify the psychosocial and economic impact of cardiomyopathy complications using questionnaires, patient-reported outcomes, healthcare use, employment and cost data.
  • Investigate how psychosocial and environmental factors, such as stress, obesity and physical activity, may influence the cardiomyopathy disease process and related biological changes in the heart.
  • Evaluate the value and cost-effectiveness of strategies to detect, prevent or treat cardiomyopathy-related complications in patients with cardiomyopathy, incorporating patient preferences and societal impact.
  • Where relevant and if time allows, and in close collaboration with the molecular research team, translate selected cohort findings into patient-derived iPSC or experimental animal models.

Are you ready to set the course for the years ahead? Then we’d love to meet you.

What you bring
We’re not looking for checkboxes; we’re interested in who you are and what you bring. Do you recognize yourself in this?

You bring strong analytical and communication skills and enjoy working in a multidisciplinary team. You are motivated to contribute to research at the intersection of clinical, psychosocial and economic perspectives.

Furthermore:
  • You have a Master’s degree in Medicine, AKO arts klinisch onderzoeker. You have interest/experience in health sciences or related fields
  • You have an interest in and/or experience with Health Technology Assessment (HTA), with focus on psychosocial and related economic impact of cardiomyopathy on patients’ lives, including quality of life and patient-reported outcomes.
  • You are familiar with the Northern European and/or Dutch healthcare system.
  • You have experience with, or are willing to learn, statistical software such as R or Stata.
  • You have an excellent command of English and Dutch, both written and spoken, at minimum C1 level (CEFR).

What we offer
At Maastricht University, you’ll work in an international, open, and engaged environment. We offer:
  • A 12-month contract (1,0 FTE) with the prospect of a 3 year extension based on mutual satisfaction.
  • A gross monthly salary between € 3.204 and € 4.051 (based on full-time employment of 38 hours per week). 8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% year-end bonus.
  • 29 vacation days (based on full-time), four additional days off (Carnival Monday and Tuesday, Good Friday, and Liberation Day), and the possibility to accrue up to 12 extra days through compensation hours.
  • Flexible working hours, a home office allowance, and the option to work from home.
  • Freedom and space to shape your work independently and develop your ideas.
  • A close-knit community of colleagues to collaborate and grow with.
  • A solid pension plan via ABP, company fitness schemes, and access to various university sports facilities.
  • An inspiring work environment in the heart of Europe.

jobs.title: PhD in Physics-informed generative AI for dynamic cardiac MRI
jobs.description_html:
Do you want to make cardiac MRI safer for patients and the environment? Join PRIMA-CMR, a EuroTech Universities Alliance project between TU/e and the Technical University of Munich (TUM) and help to develop trustworthy generative AI that makes it possible to scan with far less contrast agent.

Information
Cardiac MRI gives unmatched insight into heart disease, but some of its most important exams depend on gadolinium-based contrast agents. Gadolinium can build up in the body, cannot be given to all patients, and is now an environmental pollutant. A large reduction in the dose would make cardiac MRI safer and available to more patients. At low doses, however, the images no longer contain enough signal for a reliable diagnosis. Current AI methods can make images that look realistic, but they cannot guarantee that what they show is real.

We are looking for a motivated PhD candidate to develop new generative AI methods that recover diagnostic information from low-dose cardiac MRI in a reliable and trustworthy way. Your work will combine knowledge of MR imaging physics, patient-specific clinical information, and uncertainty quantification. The aim is a model whose outputs clinicians can trust, and which tells them when it is not certain. You will validate the methods on real clinical data together with our clinical partners.

This PhD position is part of PRIMA-CMR, a collaborative project within the EuroTech Universities Alliance programme. You will be based at TU/e and spend six months at TUM in the group of prof. Julia Schnabel, which is a world leader in generative and multimodal AI. You will also work with international clinical and academic partners across Europe. This position is embedded in the Medical Image Analysis group, Department of Biomedical Engineering, TU/e. You will be supervised by dr. Cian Scannell, and co-supervised by prof. Julia Schnabel (TUM).

jobs.title: PhD Candidate EPIC Project
jobs.description_html:
Project overview

Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a major healthcare challenge. Prosthetic joint infections, often caused by Staphylococcus aureus and Staphylococcus epidermidis, are difficult to treat because these bacteria form biofilms that protect them from antibiotics and host defenses.

Within the NWO-funded EPIC (Endolysin-based Protective Implant nanoCarriers) consortium, ACTA, the University of Twente, Micreos, LipoCoat, and clinical partners are developing innovative endolysin-loaded nanocarriers to prevent and treat implant-associated infections.

We seek a highly motivated PhD candidate to investigate the antimicrobial efficacy, anti-biofilm activity, biosafety, and host compatibility of novel endolysin formulations.

Your role

You will:
  • Investigate the antimicrobial efficacy and biosafety of endolysin-based formulations
  • Evaluate activity against planktonic and biofilm-associated S. aureus and S. epidermidis, including MRSA
  • Develop advanced in vitro biofilm and infection models, including microfluidic systems
  • Assess activity against intracellular staphylococci and monitor resistance development
  • Evaluate cytotoxicity, immune responses, and effects on bone-related cells using human cell culture and 3D tissue models
  • Collaborate with academic and industrial consortium partners
  • Publish findings in peer-reviewed journals and present at scientific conferences

You will be based in both the Department of Preventive Dentistry and the Department of Oral Cell Biology at ACTA and work in an interdisciplinary environment spanning microbiology, cell biology, biomaterials, and host-microbe interactions.

The supervisory team consists of Prof. dr. Bastiaan Krom, Prof. dr. Astrid Bakker, dr. ing. Michel Hoogenkamp, and dr. Jianfeng Jin.

jobs.title: PhD Candidate in Complex Networks
jobs.description_html:
The Mathematical Institute (MI) of Leiden University and the Leiden Institute of Advanced Computer Science (LIACS) are looking for a PhD Candidate in Complex Networks to commence at the earliest possible date and no later than April 2027.

The project investigates how structural properties observed in complex networks can be understood and modeled using mathematically tractable network models. The research will combine theoretical modeling with computational and data-driven investigation of real-world networks, with a particular emphasis on understanding how features such as spatial structure, clustering, heterogeneity, and connectivity shape network behavior.

Possible research directions include, but are not limited to, network science, spatial network modeling, random graph models, and data-driven methods for network analysis. We welcome candidates with an interest in real-world network data as well as in developing and analyzing mathematical models of complex networks. The precise balance between theoretical, computational, and data-driven work will depend on the candidate’s background and interests.

The position will be co-supervised by dr. Moritz Otto (MI) and dr. Akrati Saxena (LIACS). Michel Mandjes (MI) will act as promotor. Academic excellence is the main selection criterion.

What you will do
  • Conducting complex networks research at the intersection of mathematics and computer science.
  • Writing a publication-based PhD thesis.
  • Engaging in a limited number of teaching and supervision activities.

Where you will work
The PhD candidate will be employed at the Mathematical Institute and also be affiliated with the Leiden Institute of Advanced Computer Science and AI (LIACS). In particular, the candidate will become part of the Leiden AlFa (Algorithmic Fairness: https://alfa.liacs.nl) group and the Probability research group, and collaborate closely with the Network Science group.
Both the research groups and the institutes are highly international and feature a mix of disciplinary and cultural backgrounds. There are plenty of additional opportunities for other types of interaction and collaboration, for example, at the Faculty of Science through the Leiden Complex Networks Network (LCN2) and nationally through the Dutch Network Science Society.

The Mathematical Institute focuses on four key research themes: Algebra, Geometry, and Number Theory; Analysis and Dynamical Systems; Probability; and Statistics and Data Science. There is extensive collaboration between these themes. For more information about the Mathematical Institute, see https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/science/mathematics.
LIACS is one of the leading computer science departments in the Netherlands. We strive for excellence in a supportive institute where academic achievement, enjoyment, and diversity go hand in hand. For more information about LIACS, visit our website: http://www.cs.leiden.edu

What you bring
  • A university degree* in mathematics, computer science or a closely related field.
  • Knowledge in an area of research related to network science/complex networks, e.g., graph theory, probability, random graphs, complex systems, or topological data analysis.
  • Programming experience, preferably in Python, and willingness to develop strong computational skills (please mention your level of proficiency and knowledge of other programming languages in your CV).
  • Strong motivation for academic research.
  • Good English communication skills.
  • The ability to work independently and in a team.
  • You live and are officially registered as resident in The Netherlands or are willing to relocate upon starting the position.
    • Candidates who expect to complete their Master’s degree by early spring 2027 are also encouraged to apply.

jobs.title: PhD position: Bacterial packaging of biocatalytic nanofactories
jobs.description_html:
What you will do
With the recent rapid progress in synthetic cells, sometimes known as artificial cells, the toolbox for liposome-encapsulated biocatalyst has massively expanded, creating complex systems that can act as ‘chemical nanofactories’ for biocatalytic cascade reactions. In this PhD project, you will optimise, apply and exploit a new technology in which biocatalysts are ‘packaged’ and confined in lipid vesicles during bacterial expression, which not only massively enriches biocatalyst yields, but also creates a ready-to-go liposome-encapsulated systems.

About the project
This project is a good match if:
  • you are interested in the expression, characterisation and engineering of biocatalysts.
  • you like working in a multidisciplinary team.
  • you are interested in contributing to the field of Synthetic Cells and biotechnology.

What you bring
We are looking for a highly motivated candidate who:
  • has a Master’s degree in Life Sciences and Technology, Biochemistry, Biotechnology, or a related discipline
  • has experience in cloning, expression, purification and characterisation of biocatalysts, and preferably also in the preparation and analysis of lipid vesicles.
  • has a strong interest in structure-function relationship of enzymes, with proven excellent technical experimental and analytical skills and ability to work independently.
  • has a good proficiency in (scientific) English, and excellent communication skills.
  • feels comfortable working in a collaborative environment.

jobs.description_html:
The Institute of Environmental Sciences CML and Faculty of Science is looking for:
PhD student on Key Performance Indicators for biodiversity-inclusive agriculture

In collaboration with Technical University Eindhoven and Wageningen University and Research, you will design validated and tangible key performance indicators of biodiversity improvements in agriculture and horticulture.

What you will do
Are you motivated to contribute to the transition towards nature-inclusive agriculture and horticulture? Do you want to work at the interface of innovation science, system dynamics, value chains, biodiversity restoration, and real-world decision-making by farmers and agrifood stakeholders? Join the NWO-KIC project RISE – Resilient Integrated Systems for Ecosystem restoration as a PhD candidate and co-develop a system dynamics model for agrifood transitions in an interdisciplinary team of four PhD candidates, with farmers and societal stakeholders.

Within that project, your key responsibilities are:
  • Evaluating the barriers and opportunities for nature-inclusive initiatives in farming practices.
  • Designing validated Key Performance Indicators for biodiversity improvement in farming practices for two regional case areas.
  • Creating actionable biodiversity strategies and indicators for regional agricultural stakeholders.
  • Upscaling frameworks of biodiversity strategies in agricultural landscapes to new applications.

jobs.title: PhD Researcher: Environmental Impacts of Spatial Demographic Change
jobs.description_html:
The Institute of Environmental Sciences CML and Faculty of Science is looking for:
PhD Researcher: Environmental impacts of spatial demographic change

Excited to use geospatial and environmental analysis tools to explore the implications of spatial demographic change for urban planning, resource demand, and the environment?

Key responsibilities
The primary objective of this PhD project is to advance understanding of how spatial population distribution, demographic change (including aging population and smaller households), and urban form jointly shape future resource demand and GHG emissions. The project will evaluate core trade-offs in material and energy requirements and emissions, balancing the efficiency gains of urban density against the rise in vacant buildings and underutilized infrastructure caused by regional depopulation. Ultimately, the research will inform urban and regional development strategies to minimize net land take and GHG emissions, while catering to the needs of changing populations across the rural-urban continuum in Europe.

As a PhD researcher on this project, you will:
  • Develop high-resolution activity demand models for building and transport sectors under future spatially refined scenarios of European demographic change.
  • Integrate activity demand projections with material flow and life-cycle models to quantify future energy requirements, material intensity, and GHG emissions.
  • Evaluate adaptive reuse and circular strategies for vacant buildings and underutilized transport infrastructure in depopulating and/or aging regions.
  • Design integrated spatial planning scenarios combining built environment transformations with transport infrastructure investments to support high wellbeing and low resource/emissions pathways across population change and urban/rural contexts

jobs.title: PhD in Photonic Sensors for Light-Starved Applications
jobs.description_html:
Are you passionate about cutting-edge semiconductor technology for solving real societal problems? Then this PhD position could be a fit for you. In this project you will push the limit of spectroscopic analysis by developing novel photonic chips working at ultralow light levels (down to femtowatts). These chips will form the core of sensors which are crucial for advancing healthcare and the energy transition.

Information
Near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) allows characterizing materials and tissues, and it is widely used in industry. Our group has recently developed integrated spectral sensors, based on an advanced nanophotonic platform. These low-cost spectral chips, already commercialized by our spin-off MantiSpectra, provide detailed spectral information in the spectral region 900-1700 nm and allow measuring materials properties. However, they are based on reflection and therefore require a powerful light source to illuminate the object. Their application could be widely extended if they were sensitive enough to measure light emitted by a sample through fluorescence or Raman scattering. This requires pushing the limit of spectral sensing technology to combine spectral discrimination and detection at the femtowatt/low picowatt level, in a single device. To this aim the project will explore advanced device designs and fabrication methods, and collaborate with other TU/e research groups for the integration with low-noise amplification. The sensors will be fabricated at the NanoLab@TU/e cleanroom facility, using advanced semiconductor equipment. Their application to low-light sensing applications will also be explored during the project, in collaboration with industrial partners.

jobs.title: PhD on Ultracold electron source development for time-resolved protein crystallography
jobs.description_html:
Are you excited to solve technical challenges with a real-world application?
Are you eager to build something truly unique in the world?

Development of a pulsed electron source with extreme transverse bunch brightness, based on photo-ionization of laser-cooled atoms, for time-resolved protein crystallography.

Context: ERC-funded project “Cool T-ReX”

Goal: Develop a unique and innovative instrument to enable time-resolved protein crystallography with electrons (and be the first in the world in doing so).

Scientific relevance: Understanding how proteins function is crucial to improving medicine and unraveling processes that are fundamental to life. Time-resolved protein crystallography uniquely allows following the conformational change of a protein with unprecedented spatial and temporal resolution, yielding a “molecular movie” of how the protein performs its function. This is currently only possible on large-scale X-ray facilities. In this project we will build the very first instrument that can make such movies through time-resolved protein crystallography with electrons rather than X-rays, on a laboratory-scale setup. Next, through collaboration with leading research groups in time-resolved protein crystallography, we will demonstrate the instrument’s capabilities in time-resolved crystallography experiments on photo-active proteins with medical relevance (and used in the field of optogenetics, awarded this year’s Nobel Prize in Medicine!).

Your role: Drive the development of this unique instrument. You will build on our research group’s two decades of experience in building electron sources based on the photo-ionization of laser-cooled atoms. This technique has demonstrated electron pulses with record-low transverse temperatures, corresponding to a high transverse coherence, as needed for protein crystallography. In this project we will push this transverse coherence even further, making use of some of the unique capabilities of this source technology. The result will be an electron beam with a “transverse bunch brightness” that is three orders of magnitude beyond the current state of the art. To reach this ambitious goal, you will work with a team of experienced technicians, a second PhD student, a PostDoc, and the PI (Julius Huijts). We are part of the larger Coherence and Quantum Technology group in the Department of Applied Physics.

jobs.title: PhD position on forensic tracing of tropical timber
jobs.description_html:
Are you passionate about the reducing illegal timber trade from tropical forests? Do you aspire developing scientific tools to curb illegal trade? Then this PhD position could be a good fit for you! We are looking for a bright and highly qualified team player in this applied research project.

The illegal trade in tropical timber is a major environmental problem. New international legislation aimed at curbing this trade requires independent techniques to verify timber origin. In this NWO-funded research project we develop these tools.

We have two PhD vacancies: this PhD analyses timber forensic data with geostatistical tools to verify timber origin; the other PhD focuses on radar remote sensing to detect logging activities. You can apply only to one of the positions.

You will use state-of-the-art timber forensics measurements and combine these with innovative predictive geostatistical models to verify the origin of tropical timber. Your results are used to develop a publicly accessible dashboard to validate claimed timber origin. Authorities, timber industry and NGOs are members of the project’s user committee. In addition, the project involves international partners in Central Africa, South-East Asia, and South and North America.

Your duties and responsibilities include:
  • Conduct wood chemical analyses of available wood samples with a mass spectrometer
  • Develop and test multivariate geostatistical models of forensic data to verify timber origin
  • Lead analyses and writing of multi-authored scientific publications, culminating in a PhD thesis
  • Collaborate with international partners and members of the user committee
  • Provide your data and results to the timber verification dashboard

Your team
You will work at Wageningen University, with possible trips to visit international collaborators and conferences. No fieldwork is foreseen. The research is embedded within the Forest Ecology and Forest Management group and the Laboratory of Geo-Information Science and Remote Sensing. You will be part of the Timtrace team, consisting of 2 PhD candidates, a post-doc and your supervisors. You are supervised by prof. dr. Pieter Zuidema prof. dr. Sytze de Bruin (PhD2); and dr. Mart Vlam.
