jobs.title: PhD student: Effect van interventies op luchtkwaliteit in Nederland
jobs.description_html:
Luchtverontreiniging is verantwoordelijk voor ongeveer 80% van de ziektelast. Wereldwijd is blootstelling thuis en op het werk naar schatting verantwoordelijk voor 16% van alle sterfgevallen. In Nederland wordt naar schatting 8,5% toegeschreven aan milieuvervuiling en nog eens 2,7% aan vervuiling op het werk. Het Institute for Risk Assessment Sciences (IRAS) van de Universiteit Utrecht onderzoekt hoe lokale interventies en bredere maatschappelijke transities de luchtverontreiniging beïnvloeden in praktijkgerichte Living Labs en aan de hand van beschikbare data.

Wat ga je doen?
Je gaat werken aan het NWA-ORC project ExpACT: een onderzoeksproject dat de gezondheidseffecten van luchtverontreiniging onderzoekt. Het project ontwikkelt verbeterde monitoringtechnologieën en methoden die kunnen inspelen op veranderende niveaus en bronnen van luchtverontreiniging. Je onderzoekt hoe interventies en transities in de praktijk de luchtverontreiniging in de ExpACT Living Labs veranderen. Interventies zijn lokale maatregelen, zoals een geluidsscherm langs een spoorlijn of de tijdelijke sluiting van een luchthaven. Ook onderzoek je hoe goed de gebruikte meet- en modelleermethoden deze effecten kunnen vaststellen. In elk Living Lab worden de onderzoeksvragen en methoden doorlopend bijgesteld door middel van co-creatie met relevante belanghebbenden, onder wie inwoners en professionals. Je werkt daarbij nauw samen met de Living Labs en met ExpACT-partners die nieuwe sensoren en apparatuur ontwikkelen. Je integreert hun technologieën en modelleertechnieken in de Living Labs.

In landelijke gebieden, waar veranderingen in de landbouw invloed hebben op de ammoniakuitstoot, gaat het onder meer om uitbreiding van een passief NH3-meetnetwerk, evaluatie van een mobiele NH3-sensor en onderzoek naar de vraag of filters kunnen worden gebruikt om bio-organische deeltjes en pollen te detecteren.

In stedelijke gebieden kan het onderzoek bestaan uit het meten van metalen en mogelijk andere emissies van spoorwegen, en het vaststellen van het effect van een gepland geluidsscherm op deze concentraties.

In Eindhoven onderzoek je het effect van de geplande tijdelijke sluiting van Eindhoven Airport op de concentraties ultrafijnstof. Je bespreekt gedurende het hele project met inwoners en professionals wat er gemeten moet worden, wat de resultaten betekenen en hoe bruikbaar de instrumenten in de praktijk zijn.

Je wordt begeleid binnen het Institute for Risk Assessment Sciences (IRAS) van de Universiteit Utrecht. Je profiteert van nauwe samenwerking met onderzoekers, onderzoeksinstituten en partners van Living Labs in heel Nederland.

jobs.title: Promovendus 'Klimaatadaptatie, thermofysiologie en gezondheid'
jobs.description_html:
Functie
Periodes van extreme hitte komen steeds vaker voor. Daarom wordt het aanpassen van bestaande woningen steeds belangrijker om bewoners te beschermen tegen ongezonde binnenklimaten en om het toekomstige energieverbruik voor koeling te beperken. Als promovendus bij het Radboudumc ga je onderzoek doen binnen het door NWO gefinancierde project 'Nature4Homes'.

Dit project heeft een looptijd van 5,5 jaar en gaat in december 2026 van start. Het doel van het project is het ontwikkelen van op de natuur gebaseerde of door de natuur geïnspireerde interventies aan woningen gericht op het verhogen van de energie-efficiëntie van woningen, en verminderen van hittestress en thermisch ongemak bij bewoners. Specifiek richten we ons op: I) groene gevels, II) natuurlijke visuele patronen en III) natuurlijke variatie in het binnenklimaat.

De ingrepen worden ontworpen door de consortiumpartners (TU Delft, TU Eindhoven, WUR), terwijl wij als Radboudumc verantwoordelijk zijn voor de fysiologische en perceptuele evaluatie van hoe deze op de natuur geïnspireerde interventies invloed hebben op de hittestress en gezondheid van bewoners tijdens de zomer.

Als promovendus ben je verantwoordelijk is voor het van A tot Z uitvoeren van wetenschappelijke onderzoeken, zowel in het laboratorium als in de praktijk. Deze onderzoeken zullen plaatsvinden op de afdeling Medische BioWetenschappen van het Radboudumc binnen de sectie Humane Fysiologie.

Je gaat gedurende meerdere zomers (van mei tot en met september) continu thermofysiologische gegevens verzamelen over hittestress en gezondheid bij bewoners (waar de betreffende interventies zijn toegepast), gebruikmakend van een vooraf vastgestelde meetset. Daarnaast voer je, in samenwerking met de TU Eindhoven, een laboratoriumstudie uit naar de invloed van het zien van groen (met behulp van VR) op de thermische beleving en de thermoregulatie van het lichaam.

In jouw rol als promovendus ga je interdisciplinair te werk en heb je nauw contact met deelnemers, collega-onderzoekers en stakeholders binnen en buiten het Radboudumc. Je gaat verschillende studies opzetten, uitvoeren en analyseren om antwoorden te vinden op bovenstaande vragen. Daarnaast schrijf je diverse wetenschappelijke artikelen, wat zal resulteren in een proefschrift aan het einde van je contract.

Kenmerken van dit project zijn de multidisciplinaire samenwerking op het snijvlak van klimaatverandering en gezondheid. In het project wordt je begeleid door een team van onderzoekers. Daarnaast is er voldoende vrijheid voor eigen inbreng in het onderzoek. Je komt te werken in een dynamische omgeving met een groot aantal andere promovendi die zich onder andere bezighouden met (thermo)fysiologische vraagstukken.

Taken en verantwoordelijkheden
  • Het opzetten en uitvoeren van een grootschalig veldonderzoek gedurende de zomer, gebruikmakend van niet-invasieve en eenvoudig toepasbare draadloze monitoring.
  • Het uitvoeren van een thermofysiologisch experiment in een temperatuur-gecontroleerde kamer.
  • Het begeleiden van studenten en andere medewerkers die bijdragen aan de uitvoering van de veldonderzoeken.
  • Dataverwerking en statistische analyse.
  • Het schrijven van wetenschappelijke artikelen en het presenteren van de resultaten op (inter)nationale congressen.
  • Mogelijkheid om bij te dragen aan het onderwijsprogramma van de opleidingen Biomedische Wetenschappen en Geneeskunde.

jobs.title: PhD in supramolecular interactions in organic mixed ionic-electronic conductors
jobs.description_html:
Are you fascinated by how molecular-scale interactions determine the real-world performance of functional materials? In this PhD project, you will study a new class of materials that find application in future technologies ranging from neuromorphic computing and bioelectronics to energy storage. Are you ready to help unravel the inner workings of these fascinating materials by investigating them during operation?

Your research
In your PhD project, you will uncover how intermolecular interactions and supramolecular morphology govern the functionality of organic mixed ionic-electronic conductors (OMIECs). Bridging the fields of OMIECs and supramolecular chemistry, you will investigate these relationships through in-depth operando characterization.

OMIECs are soft materials that conduct both electrons and ions, highly promising for applications ranging from energy storage and solar fuels to bioelectronics and neuromorphic computing. However, electrons, ions, solvent and the molecular structure all reorganize during operation, making it difficult to disentangle how molecular-scale interactions ultimately determine macroscopic function.

You will develop characterization methods and experimental setups to probe intermolecular interactions as OMIECs operate. Spectroelectrochemistry will be a key tool; developing operando cells, setups, and experiments that enable you to discern dynamic spectral signatures of molecular packing. By following changes in supramolecular organization during electrochemical doping, your work will reveal how doping affects supramolecular organization.

You will also determine how supramolecular packing governs doping efficiency and dynamics, linking morphology to device-relevant properties, by studying varied samples of available supramolecular building blocks. These fundamental insights will provide a supramolecular knob for tuning material functionality, thereby introducing new ways to control material behavior.

The key outcome of your research is a mechanistic framework describing the bidirectional interplay between OMIEC doping and supramolecular interactions. Building on this framework, you will ultimately design switchable supramolecular OMIEC systems in collaboration with other researchers, targeting applications in in-material computing. Beyond these systems, your fundamental insights will contribute to the general development of next-generation computing and adaptive bioelectronics.

Your environment and support
As a member of the Optoelectronic Mixed Conductors group at the Department of Chemical Engineering and Chemistry, you will conduct your research under the supervision of Prof. Tom van der Pol. Your project is highly interdisciplinary, with opportunities to collaborate with researchers across the department. You will become part of a broad and vibrant scientific community, including the Institute for Complex Molecular Systems.

At TU/e and within the Optoelectronic Mixed Conductors group, curiosity-driven research and personal development go hand in hand. You will have the freedom to pursue ambitious scientific questions while receiving the guidance and support needed to develop your own ideas and expertise. Your supervisory team will support you in developing the skills, confidence, and scientific perspective needed to uncover the mechanisms that govern OMIECs and to shape your own path as a researcher.

jobs.title: PhD in Multifunctional Polymer Composites
jobs.description_html:
Are you inspired to push the limits of polymeric materials for lighter and smarter defense platforms? Join us to develop a new generation of 3D-printed composite panels that shield electronics from electromagnetic threats and withstand impact.

Information
We are offering 2 PhD positions within project VALOR, an ambitious, interdisciplinary collaboration between academia, industry and government partners. The project aims to develop a new generation of lightweight composite panels that both shield sensitive electronics from electromagnetic threats and withstand impact events, helping to make defense platforms safer and more resilient.

Naval ships, drones and military vehicles increasingly depend on electronic radar, communication and navigation systems that must be protected against electromagnetic interference and radar detection. Today, this is mostly done with metals, which block practically all wave power with only a thin layer. However, they add weight, corrode, and reflect electromagnetic waves, making platforms easier to detect. Project VALOR tackles this challenge by merging two fields that have so far been developed separately: absorption-based electromagnetic shielding and impact-resistant sandwich structures. By combining 3D-printed architected nanocomposite materials with predictive modelling into one integrated design strategy, the project will construct a design framework for panels that are able to both carry loads and absorb electromagnetic waves, with a performance that can be tailored to specific (defense) applications.

Your role
We are recruiting two PhD candidates who will work as a team throughout the project, i.e. from material screening to design and testing of larger scale panel demonstrators. Both candidates will conduct a combination of experimental and numerical work and collaborate closely with industrial partners within the consortium. More specifically:
  • PhD 1 focuses on mechanics and manufacturing: 3D printing nanocomposite lattice materials, fabricating composite facesheets, conducting mechanical tests, constructing and validating mechanical finite element models.
  • PhD 2 focuses on electromagnetic testing and design: formulating polymer nanocomposite materials and characterizing their electromagnetic behaviour, designing and testing absorbing architected nanocomposite structures, conducting electromagnetic shielding simulations.

Your team and network
You will join the Processing and Performance of Materials section in the Department of Mechanical Engineering at TU/e. The group has around 20 PhD and post-doctoral researchers working on how processing, structure and properties connect in polymers and polymer-based composite materials. The group is known for its integrated experimental-numerical approach to tailor the performance of these materials. You will have access to state-of-the-art computational facilities and laboratories dedicated to rheology, polymer processing (incl. additive manufacturing) and mechanical testing. You will be supervised by Frederik Van Loock (project leader), Ruth Cardinaels and Tom Engels.

jobs.title: PhD in Communication-Optimized Inference in Large Language Models
jobs.description_html:
Are you interested in the communication networks behind modern AI systems? Would you like to combine mathematical modeling with experiments on programmable network hardware to make AI infrastructure faster and more energy-efficient? In this PhD project, you will develop models and orchestration methods for the networks that connect GPUs during large language model inference. Are you our next PhD candidate in high-performance AI networking?

Your research challenge
Large language models rely on powerful computing infrastructure to generate responses. When inference is distributed across multiple GPUs, these devices must continuously exchange intermediate results. Network congestion and communication overhead can therefore limit performance and increase energy consumption, even when substantial computing resources are available.

In the project Communication-Optimized Inference in Large Language Models (COIL), you will investigate how analytical network models can support the design and operation of AI clusters. The project combines network performance modeling, optimization, and experimental research, giving you the opportunity to connect mathematical foundations with practical challenges in AI infrastructure.

You will develop fast, composable analytical models using Network Calculus, a mathematical framework for analyzing communication networks. These models will capture interactions between inference traffic, network architecture, and mechanisms such as flow control and congestion feedback. They will provide bounds on communication latency and buffer requirements, complemented by energy estimates based on measurement-calibrated power models.

Building on these models, you will explore how architectural choices—including network topology, link bandwidth, and parallelization strategies—affect performance and energy consumption. You will develop tools that help cluster designers evaluate promising configurations efficiently.

You will also investigate how the models can guide runtime decisions, such as workload placement, prioritization, routing, or resource reservation. A focused prototype will demonstrate how model-informed decisions can improve the operation of an existing network.

Experimental validation will be an integral part of your research. You will use measurements from AI infrastructure and conduct reproducible experiments on programmable networking testbeds. Technologies of interest include Ethernet-based AI networks, emerging Ultra Ethernet mechanisms, P4-programmable switches, and SmartNICs. Finally, you will evaluate the results from the testbeds on real AI infrastructure in collaboration with our partner SURF.

Through this combination of theory, software development, and experimentation, you will contribute to more responsive and energy-efficient AI infrastructure. The project also offers opportunities to share your findings with networking standardization communities and to release research tools and experimental results openly.

An interdisciplinary and international environment
You will conduct your research under the main supervision of Prof. Lisa Maile who leads the Network Modeling and Design (NoMaD) lab. NoMaD is part of the Electronic Systems group in the Department of Electrical Engineering at Eindhoven University of Technology. Your supervision will also include partners from the Advanced Models by Open Research and Engineering (AMOR/e) Lab of Computer Science and the Model-Based Design Lab from Electrical Engineering.

The position is funded through the EuroTech programme, which promotes research collaboration between leading technical universities across Europe. As part of this project, you will collaborate closely with Prof. Georg Carle and his research group on Network Architectures and Services at the Technical University of Munich (TUM). As part of this collaboration, you will spend six-month in Munich with the group at TUM, where you will gain hands-on experience with programmable network hardware and reproducible experimental infrastructure.

jobs.title: PhD Position in Digital Twins for Flood-Resilient Infrastructure
jobs.description_html:
Develop and implement a Digital Twin that strengthens our ability to protect critical infrastructure against flooding.

Job description
Current and future impact of flooding to critical infrastructure (e.g. dikes, bridges) is a major concern worldwide. Unfortunately, the management of flood-prone structures is extremely challenging because underlying processes are complex and uncertain. If our capacity to anticipate flood-induced impacts on infrastructure does not improve, societal and economic consequences are likely to be unsustainable.

Digital Twins (DTs) offer a promising opportunity to combine recent advances in modelling, data assimilation and machine learning. However, for DTs to support the management of flood-prone infrastructure, they must be effectively integrated with flood-risk modelling. The scientific challenge is to develop methods that enable Digital Twins to leverage multiple models, datasets and computational techniques to improve predictive capacity in real flood-risk contexts.

FlooDT (Digital Twin for flood-resilient infrastructure management) is a prestigious and ambitious project funded by NWO. It aims to develop a new methodological framework to exploit the capability of DTs for managing flood risk “from climate prediction to structure protection”. TU Delft is leading the project and a consortium that involves multiple universities (e.g. ETH Zurich, Univ. Polytechnica of Catalunya) and stakeholders (e.g. Deltares, Rijkswaterstaat). The project has also the support of the TU Delft Digital Competence Centre (DCC).

For this unique project we are seeking a motivated and talented PhD candidate for a 4-year appointment. In your role you will:
  • Develop functional modules for Digital Twins, such as risk analysis, scenario modelling and processing of monitoring data.
  • Develop hybrid (physics based/machine learning) modelling for flood risk.
  • Apply and validate the Digital Twin functionalities for simplified representation of infrastructure (first) and real case studies (second).
  • Implement the developed functionalities into end users' platforms.
  • Co-organise workshops and co-coordinate stakeholder engagement (e.g. regular meetings, presentations, visits).

You will join the FlooDT team and the Flood Risk and Hydraulic Structures section, a collaborative and international team where curiosity, interdisciplinary research and scientific excellence are valued. Our section closely collaborates with the other sections within the Department of Hydraulic Engineering, other departments within our Faculty of Civil Engineering and Geoscience and many research groups around the world. We offer strong support for your professional growth, including mentoring, training, and ample opportunities for international collaboration and networking.

This position will open doors to exciting career opportunities in both academia and the future-facing companies that are shaping the next generation of digital technologies.

Job requirements
We are looking for an excellent, enthusiastic and inquisitive computational researcher who enjoys working in an international and multidisciplinary environment. You have:
  • A MSc degree in Civil Engineering, Computer Science or Hydro-informatics (or in a related discipline).
  • Demostrated experience in numerical modelling, hydrodynamic simulation and data management.
  • Scientific and/or practical knowledge of machine learning.
  • Excellent programming skills (e.g. in Python, SQL, Java, PyTorch, etc.).
  • A critical, creative and pro-active approach to research, with distinctive problem-solving skills.
  • Proven experience with writing scientific reports/publications.
  • Confidence/willingness in engaging with partners and stakeholders.
  • Excellent command of English (oral and written).

Previous internship experience with non-academic institutions is desiderable.

TU Delft (Delft University of Technology)
Working at TU Delft means contributing to solutions that really make a difference.

For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow. These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future.

At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional. Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward.

Faculty of Civil Engineering and Geosciences
The Faculty of Civil Engineering & Geosciences (CEG) is committed to outstanding international research and education in the field of civil engineering, applied earth sciences, traffic and transport, water technology, and delta technology. Our research feeds into our educational programmes and covers societal challenges such as climate change, energy transition, resource availability, urbanisation and clean water. Our research projects are conducted in close cooperation with a wide range of research institutions. CEG is convinced of the importance of open science and supports its scientists in integrating open science in their research practice. The Faculty of CEG comprises 28 research groups in the following seven departments: Materials Mechanics Management & Design, Engineering Structures, Geoscience and Engineering, Geoscience and Remote Sensing, Transport & Planning, Hydraulic Engineering and Water Management.

Click here to go to the website of the Faculty of Civil Engineering & Geosciences.

Conditions of employment
Doctoral candidates will be offered a 4-year period of employment in principle, but in the form of 2 employment contracts. An initial 1,5 year contract with an official go/no go progress assessment within 15 months. Followed by an additional contract for the remaining 2,5 years assuming everything goes well and performance requirements are met.

Salary and benefits are in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, increasing from €3204 - €4051 gross per month, from the first year to the fourth year based on a fulltime contract (38 hours), plus 8% holiday allowance and an end-of-year bonus of 8.3%.

As a PhD candidate you will be enrolled in the TU Delft Graduate School. The TU Delft Graduate School provides an inspiring research environment with an excellent team of supervisors, academic staff and a mentor. The Doctoral Education Programme is aimed at developing your transferable, discipline-related and research skills.

The TU Delft offers a customisable compensation package, discounts on health insurance, and a monthly work costs contribution. Flexible work schedules can be arranged.

Will you need to relocate to the Netherlands for this job? TU Delft is committed to make your move as smooth as possible! The HR unit, Coming to Delft Service, offers information on their website to help you prepare your relocation. In addition, Coming to Delft Service organises events to help you settle in the Netherlands, and expand your (social) network in Delft. A Dual Career Programme is available, to support your accompanying partner with their job search in the Netherlands.

Additional information
All information are cointained here and general questions will not be answered. For specific requests, please contact Maria Pregnolato (m.pregnolato@tudelft.nl).

After the first selection, online interviews will be held in December.

The candidate is expected to start in March/April 2027.

Application procedure
Are you interested in this vacancy? Please apply no later than 18 November 2026 via the application button and upload the following documents:
  • CV (max 4 pages).
  • Cover letter (max 1 page) describing your motivation and qualifications for the position.
  • Applicants selected for an interview will be asked to provide contact information of at least 2 references.

Doing a PhD at TU Delft requires English proficiency at a certain level to ensure that the candidate is able to communicate and interact well, participate in English-taught Doctoral Education courses, and write scientific articles and a final thesis. For more details please check the Graduate Schools Admission Requirements.

Please note:
  • You can apply online. We will not process applications sent by email and/or post.
  • As part of knowledge security, TU Delft conducts a risk assessment during the recruitment of personnel. jobs.title: PhD Candidate in Cell-Matrix Interactions in Dynamic Hydrogels
jobs.description_html:
Welcome to Maastricht University!

Join us in developing cell-instructive and adaptive supramolecular biomaterials. In this PhD project, you will investigate how the molecular organization, mechanics, dynamics, and presentation of biological signals within hydrogels influence cell behavior. You will then help extend these principles toward living materials in which engineered cells actively modify their surrounding matrix.

PhD Candidate in Cell-Matrix Interactions in Dynamic Hydrogels

Discover how dynamic supramolecular matrices instruct cells and how cells can, in turn, reshape and improve the material around them
  • Our goal: To establish predictive relationships between supramolecular hydrogel design and cell response, and to use these insights to create adaptive materials with two-way communication between cells and their matrix.
  • Your colleagues: You will join the BioMatt group of Dr. Matthew Baker (https://merlninstitute.com/discover-merln/departments-and-groups/research-groups/biomatt-polymeric-biomaterials). The BioMatt group is part of MERLN’s Department of Instructive Biomaterials Engineering (IBE), which develops biomaterials that actively interact with and guide biological systems. Within this environment, BioMatt combines molecular and polymer design with cell biology and tissue engineering to create dynamic materials for biomedical applications.

Working at MERLN means joining an international network of researchers from approximately 25 nationalities and a collaborative community spanning biomaterials, chemistry, mechanobiology, tissue engineering, biofabrication, microbiology, and cell biology. You will work in newly renovated laboratories with access to state-of-the-art facilities and close scientific support from colleagues across the SupraValent team.

What you do
This position leads the cell–matrix interaction and mechanobiology line within the ERC Consolidator project SupraValent. You will use both design and use established hydrogel platforms and processing workflows from the team to determine how material properties are sensed by cells and how cells feed back on their environment. You will:
  • Design and create supramolecular hydrogels with control over biofunctionalization via peptide cues
  • Establish robust 2D and 3D cell-culture workflows in supramolecular and dynamically reinforced hydrogels.
  • Determine how stiffness, stress relaxation, network architecture, and dynamic covalent reinforcement influence cell adhesion, morphology, mechanotransduction, phenotype, and matrix production.
  • Investigate how the molecular-scale presentation and accessibility of cell-adhesive or other bioactive ligands affect cellular responses, including cases where bulk material properties are closely matched.
  • Study reciprocal cell–matrix interactions, including cell-mediated remodeling, deposition of extracellular matrix, and changes in hydrogel structure or mechanics over time.
  • Work closely with team members to evaluate engineered cells within hydrogel environments and determine whether their activity can controllably build, reinforce, functionalize, or remodel the material.
  • Contribute to experimental design, data analysis, publications, conference presentations, and supervision of students within the multidisciplinary BioMatt team.

The project will initially use well-defined cells and previously created materials and will develop toward novel materials designs with engineered living-material concepts in collaboration. Specific cell types and biological questions will be selected according to the strongest mechanistic opportunities and collaborations.

Are you ready to connect molecular material design with cell function? Then we would love to meet you.

Scientific background
Cells respond not only to the chemical composition and stiffness of their extracellular matrix, but also to its viscoelasticity, molecular organization, ligand presentation, and capacity to change over time. These variables are difficult to control independently in conventional hydrogels. SupraValent combines reversible benzene-1,3,5-tricarboxamide (BTA) self-assembly with covalent and dynamic-covalent modification to create materials whose mechanics, dynamics, and functionality can be adjusted after assembly. The project has established a growing molecular toolbox and hydrogel platforms with tunable stress relaxation, self-healing, reinforcement, and processing behavior.

The next challenge is to determine how to make these material features more biologically meaningful. This PhD project will move beyond simple viability testing to resolve how cells sense local and bulk properties, how these cues influence mechanotransduction and matrix production, and how cellular activity changes the material over time. In the later phase, the candidate will work towards a central SupraValent concept: living cells that do more than survive within a hydrogel, instead actively contributing to its construction, reinforcement, or functional adaptation.

This fully funded 4-year PhD position offers training at the interface of supramolecular and polymer chemistry, mechanobiology, cell biology, and biomaterials, while remaining embedded in a highly collaborative research environment.

Key references
  • Hafeez et al. Advanced Materials 2023, 35, 2207053. https://doi.org/10.1002/adma.202207053
  • Hafeez et al. Advanced Materials 2023, 35, 2301242. https://doi.org/10.1002/adma.202301242
  • Ruiter et al. Advanced Science 2022, 9, 2200543. https://doi.org/10.1002/advs.202200543
  • Rijns et al. JACS 2024, 146, 17539–17588. https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.4c02980

What you bring
We are interested in the combination of experience, motivation, and perspective you would bring. The ideal candidate is a careful and curious experimental scientist who wants to understand cell–material interactions on a molecular scale. You are comfortable 1) working with cells, interested in quantitative analysis, or 2) molecularly designing and characterizing soft polymer materials. In the project you should be excited to learn both as part of the PhD trajectory.

Furthermore, you bring:
  • An MSc (or equivalent) in Biomaterials, Polymer Chemistry, Tissue Engineering, Cell Biology, Biotechnology, Bioengineering, or a closely related field. Candidates with an equivalent research qualification from an educational system without a separate Master’s degree are also encouraged to apply; eligibility will be assessed individually
  • Substantial hands-on experience with either mammalian cell culture or biomaterials design acquired through an MSc thesis, extended research project, or relevant research position, including (cell culture) aseptic technique, experimental planning, and reliable maintenance of cell-based assays or (biomaterials) polymer functionalization, soft matter characterization, hydrogel formation.
  • Experience studying cells in contact with biomaterials, hydrogels, extracellular-matrix models, or other engineered microenvironments. Direct experience with 3D cell culture or cell encapsulation is highly desirable.
  • Interest in mechanobiology and in relating cell behavior to material properties such as stiffness, stress relaxation, ligand presentation, or remodeling. Prior rheology or mechanical-characterization experience is helpful but not required.
  • The ability to document experiments clearly, analyze data critically, troubleshoot protocols, and communicate across disciplinary boundaries.
  • Experience with extracellular-matrix deposition, cell-mediated remodeling, engineered cells, microbial culture, or engineered living materials is considered an advantage, but is not required.
  • Excellent command of scientific English (minimum CEFR level C1), as English is the working language of the group.

Availability to start the position on short notice is highly desirable; however, the start date remains flexible for highly qualified applicants.

What we offer
At Maastricht University, you’ll work in an international, open, and engaged environment. We offer:
  • A 12-month contract (1,0 FTE) with the prospect of a 3 year extension based on mutual satisfaction.
  • A gross monthly salary between € 3.204 and € 4.051 (based on full-time employment of 38 hours per week). 8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% year-end bonus.
  • 29 vacation days (based on full-time), four additional days off (Carnival Monday and Tuesday, Good Friday, and Liberation Day), and the possibility to accrue up to 12 extra days through compensation hours.
  • Freedom and space to shape your work independently and develop your ideas.
  • A close-knit community of colleagues to collaborate and grow with.

  • An inspiring work environment in the heart of Europe.

We train healthcare professionals and researchers through innovative educational programs and conduct groundbreaking research in health and well-being. Research Institute MERLN (Institute for Technology-Inspired Regenerative Medicine) within FHML develops new technologies for the repair, regeneration, and in vitro modeling of tissues and organs. Within MERLN, the Department of Instructive Biomaterials Engineering (IBE) uses materials science and engineering to design biomaterials for applications ranging from medical devices and scaffolds for regenerative therapies to predictive in vitro models. jobs.title: PhD in experimental physics: how do you make the first antimatter molecule?
jobs.description_html:
When a proton meets a hydrogen atom, the pair can emit a photon and stay together as H₂⁺. This is how the first molecules formed after the Big Bang, and it is one of the proposed routes to the first antimatter molecule, yet it has never been measured. In the NWO Vidi project SAMURAI, you will study these collisions one quantum state at a time: instead of colliding atoms, we use lasers to prepare a hydrogen molecule at the moment of a collision and watch it fall apart. You will be part of a small group in which experiment and theory go hand in hand.

Your duties
  • excite H₂ with two tunable extreme-ultraviolet lasers (60–205 nm), built in our lab and unique in the Netherlands, and image the fragments with velocity-map imaging
  • aim for the first spectroscopic observation of the excited electronic states of H₂⁺, calculated by Edward Teller in his PhD thesis in 1930 and never seen since
  • trap H₂⁺ ions and use millimetre waves and magnetic fields to control how they come apart
  • work towards the first measurement of radiative association: joining a cold proton and a cold hydrogen atom with light, next to a crystal of laser-cooled Be⁺ ions
  • compare your data with multichannel quantum-defect theory and scattering calculations, and contribute to the theory yourself if you like
  • develop your skills in lasers and nonlinear optics, ultrahigh vacuum, electronics, CAD design and scientific programming
  • present your results at international conferences and publish them in peer-reviewed journals

jobs.title: PhD Position: Safe Planning and Decision-Making under Uncertainty for Long-Horizon Robot Autonomy
jobs.description_html:
Join TU Delft and the EU-funded OPERA consortium. Push the frontier of general-purpose AI for robotics and tackle the fundamental tension between long-horizon reasoning and real-time safety guarantees.

Job description
Robots that operate for long periods among people must plan beyond the next few seconds while staying safe. They need to predict how their surroundings and the people in them will evolve, know how reliable these predictions are, and adapt their plans when the predictions fail. In the EU-funded OPERA project, TU Delft contributes to General-Purpose AI for robotics by developing methods that combine fast, reactive behavior with more deliberate reasoning, planning, and decision-making.

In this PhD position, you will develop planning and decision-making methods that let robots act safely and reliably over long time horizons when their knowledge of the environment and of the people around them is incomplete. The research sits at the intersection of model-based planning and control and learning-based models, and addresses the trade-off between safety, performance, and real-time computation. You will formulate the methods and analyze their guarantees and failure modes. This research is connected to OPERA's tasks on GPAI-powered planning and decision-making, on long-term reasoning in human-centered environments, and on adaptive human-robot and robot-environment interaction.

Depending on your background, the work may draw on optimal control and model predictive control, motion planning, probabilistic modeling and estimation, or learning-based methods. The emphasis is on methods with a clear formulation and well-understood failure modes, validated in simulation and on real robots.

You will work in the Cognitive Robotics Department at TU Delft under the supervision of Prof. Robert Babuška and Dr. Laura Ferranti, and you will be embedded in the Reliable Robot Control Lab (https://r2clab.com/). You will collaborate with OPERA partners across Europe on simulation, perception, and the OPERA open-source toolbox.

Job requirements
The ideal candidate for this PhD position has a strong background in control, optimization, or motion planning and is motivated by the question of how robots can plan safely and reliably over long time horizons. You have:

jobs.title: PhD Position Bayesian Modeling and Counterfactual Methods for Nanoparticle Transport in Human Tissue
jobs.description_html:
Shape the future of nanoparticle safety and design. Join TU Delft as a PhD researcher using Bayesian and counterfactual modelling to predict nanoparticle transport in human tissue.

Job description
We are looking for a PhD candidate to build the computational model at the center of a European project on nanoparticle transport in human tissue. You will join the research group of Dr. Sepinoud Azimi, working within the SYNERGIE project (Horizon Europe), a consortium of thirteen partners including Fraunhofer, Roche, the Karolinska Institute, University Hospital Aachen, Mimetas, Ruhr University Bochum and Maastricht University.

Small particles from the environment have been detected in human blood, placenta and brain tissue, but it is still not clear what they do there. Dose-response data for humans does not exist and animal studies have not transferred well, and as a result there is no exposure limit for these particles.

Part of the reason prediction is so hard is that a particle changes as it moves through the body. It acquires a layer of proteins, it aggregates with other particles, and depending on the material it may partly degrade, so that the particle reaching a given tissue is not the same object that was administered or characterised at the start. Most transport models do not account for this. They treat the particle as fixed, which means they are predicting the fate of something that has already changed.

The same difficulty affects engineered nanoparticles for drug delivery, and it is one of the reasons so few of them reach their intended target.

SYNERGIE is building a platform of nine human tissue-on-chip models that can be connected to follow a particle through uptake, circulation and storage. TU Delft leads the in silico work package.

As a PhD candidate, you will:
  • Build a mechanistic model of how particles move between nine human tissues, and calibrate it against experimental data using Bayesian inference.
  • Work out which physical and chemical properties of a particle decide where it ends up.
  • Develop methods that go beyond prediction: for a particle that behaves badly, what is the smallest change that would fix it, and when should that answer not be trusted.
  • Release the model as open-source software and support its use in regulatory dialogue.

You will also contribute to teaching in the department and to the supervision of BSc projects.

You will work alongside a postdoctoral researcher and PhD candidates on related problems, and interact with experimental partners across the SYNERGIE consortium. You will have access to the DelftBlue high-performance computing cluster.

The intended start date is January 2027.

  • Demonstrated experience with Bayesian inference in a probabilistic programming framework such as PyMC, Stan or NumPyro.
  • Strong scientific programming in Python. Please point us to a repository.
  • Excellent written and spoken English.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Causal inference or counterfactual reasoning.

jobs.title: PhD Position in Neuroimaging, LLM, Genetics and Cross-species comparison
jobs.description_html:
Do you enjoy working with complex neuroimaging data, large datasets and computational methods? Do you want to work at the intersection of genetics, neuroimaging, neuroscience, neurodiversity and cross-species analyses? We are looking for a highly motivated PhD candidate to join the Connectome Lab at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam

The Connectome Lab at the Center for Neurogenomics and Cognitive Research (CNCR), Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, is seeking a PhD candidate in Neuroimaging, Genetics and Cross-species comparison.

The project aims to understand how variation in brain anatomy and connectivity contributes to the remarkable diversity of the human brain, and how these features relate to principles of brain evolution. We will combine large-scale human neuroimaging datasets with comparative datasets across species to investigate variation in brain structure, connectivity and functional organization.

A central goal is to understand which aspects of brain organization are highly conserved, which show substantial variation between individuals, and which features may have emerged or expanded during human brain evolution. The project therefore brings together neuroimaging, connectomics, neurodiversity, comparative neuroscience and computational neuroscience.

You will work with large structural MRI, diffusion MRI and resting-state fMRI datasets and develop and apply computational approaches to quantify variation in brain organization across individuals, populations and species. There is particularly attention for the use of LLM in data mining.

You will be part of the computational neuroimaging Lab led by Prof. Martijn van den Heuvel and work in an interdisciplinary environment with researchers from neuroimaging, computational neuroscience, genetics, psychology, psychiatry and artificial intelligence.

Your duties
  • analyse large-scale structural MRI, diffusion MRI and resting-state fMRI datasets
  • develop and apply pipelines for cortical reconstruction, tractography, functional connectivity and connectome analysis
  • investigate individual variation and neurodiversity in brain structure and connectivity
  • integrate genetics with neuroimaging
  • perform comparative analyses of human and non-human brain organization in the context of brain evolution
  • integrate findings across different neuroimaging datasets and imaging modalities
  • develop and apply computational and statistical approaches for analysing brain networks
  • contribute to reproducible and open neuroimaging workflows
  • collaborate with researchers within the Connectome Lab, CNCR and international research networks
  • present your findings at national and international scientific meetings
  • write scientific manuscripts
  • contribute to teaching activities where appropriate

jobs.title: PhD Assessing Social Sustainability in Short Food Supply Chains
jobs.description_html:
Are you interested in how law and policy can make agri-food systems fairer and more socially sustainable? Do you enjoy combining legal analysis with empirical research and engaging with farmers and other food-system actors? Join the Law Group at Wageningen University & Research as a PhD candidate in the Horizon Europe project SOCIAL AGRI.

Social issues such as working conditions, farmer wellbeing, migrant worker integration and gender equality remain insufficiently captured in EU agricultural data and policy frameworks. This makes social costs and inequalities difficult to assess and address. SOCIAL AGRI aims to close this gap by collecting evidence on social conditions in agriculture, assessing their economic implications, and translating the findings into practical legal and policy instruments to make social sustainability a measurable and actionable dimension of European agricultural policy.

You will contribute to this objective through an in-depth socio-legal study of short food supply chains (SFSCs) in the Netherlands. You will investigate how different SFSC models operate, how EU and Dutch law and policy shape their development, and how their organisation affects social sustainability, including working conditions, inclusion, community relationships and the distribution of value.

Combining legal analysis with empirical research, you will use methods such as semi-structured interviews and stakeholder engagement activities, depending on the research design. You will identify legal and regulatory barriers to socially sustainable practices and explore how law and policy could better support their development.

Working with other project partners, you will also contribute to developing and assessing SOCIAL AGRI’s social-sustainability indicators. Your findings will inform the project’s comparative analysis and help translate evidence on social performance into feasible policy recommendations and legal instruments, including potential regulatory approaches and contractual provisions.

Your duties and responsibilities include:
  • Develop and carry out a PhD research plan aligned with SOCIAL AGRI, with a clear focus on the Dutch short food supply chain case study and its contribution to the project’s evidence-to-policy pathway.
  • Analyse relevant EU and Dutch legal and policy frameworks affecting short food supply chains and social sustainability in agriculture.
  • Collect and analyse empirical evidence on the social conditions and relationships within Dutch short food supply chains, using appropriate qualitative methods.
  • Contribute to the development actionable legal and policy instruments, including policy recommendations and model regulatory or contractual provisions, in collaboration with the wider consortium and relevant stakeholders, and of social-sustainability indicators.
  • Contribute to comparative research, collaboration and dissemination within SOCIAL AGRI, interdisciplinary teamwork, project meetings, workshops and academic publications, while actively participating in the academic life of the Law Group.

You will work here
The research is embedded within the chair Law Group.The Law Group is a vibrant, dynamic, intercultural research community that is closely integrated into the Department of Social Sciences. It has a critical, socio-legal orientation, and excels in interdisciplinary research. It collaborates closely with a range of global partners. The focus of the group’s work is detailed in its most recent Chair Plan.

You will work under the supervision of Dr Mirta Alessandrini, who is responsible for the SOCIAL AGRI Dutch case study, Dr Edwin Albals, and Dr Inga Winkler. You will also collaborate with colleagues and researchers from the wider SOCIAL AGRI consortium.

jobs.title: PhD: Developing methodological standards for studying the effectiveness of new digital interventions
jobs.description_html:
Join our interdisciplinary team at the Methodology of Educational Science Research Group (CMPO) and the Center for Contextual Psychiatry (CCP) at KU Leuven, one of Europe’s most renowned research universities. The CMPO, part of the Faculty of Psychology and Educational Sciences, is internationally recognized for its expertise in advanced statistical modeling and research methodology, encompassing both quantitative and qualitative approaches. Prof. Ginette Lafit leads innovative work to advance quantitative methods in ESM study design and drives methodological innovation in intensive longitudinal research. The CCP, housed within the Department of Neurosciences in the School of Medicine, is an internationally leading research center specializing in Experience Sampling Methodology (ESM) in mental health research. Under the leadership of Prof. Inez Myin-Germeys, the CCP brings together a vibrant group of 25 researchers from diverse backgrounds and is widely recognized for its expertise in designing, implementing, and analyzing experimental studies and clinical trials. You will join the eMotion project, an ambitious long-term research initiative dedicated to developing new interventions for the negative symptoms of psychosis. As a PhD student, you will play a central role in developing a statistical framework for optimizing the design of Ecological Momentary Interventions (EMIs) using Micro-Randomized Trials (MRTs).

Project
This research program uses Virtual Reality (VR) and the Experience Sampling Method (ESM) to examine the approach-avoidance mechanisms underlying amotivation, a core negative symptom of psychosis. A major advancement of the project is developing tailored interventions that combine EMIs with VR technology. As a PhD student, you will play a pivotal role in advancing statistical methodologies to optimize EMI design through MRTs, enhance EMI effectiveness by incorporating data from VR-based tasks, and develop rigorous measures to evaluate the clinical impact of the EMI-VR intervention framework.

Your Responsibilities

  • Apply quantitative methods to analyze ESM data, including time series analysis and multilevel modeling techniques.
  • Develop novel quantitative methods to construct EMIs and advance the EMI-VR integration using MRTs.
  • Write papers for publication in international peer-reviewed journals.
  • Collaborate closely with researchers across three research lines: (i) ESM methodology, statistics, and meta-science, (ii) Person-environment interactions in psychosis, and (iii) Development, efficacy testing, and implementation of Digital Mobile Mental Health.


This position is part of eMotion, a recently funded, large-scale research program aimed at creating new treatments for negative symptoms—among the most challenging aspects of psychiatric care. You will join a dynamic, interdisciplinary team of clinical psychologists, experimental psychologists, psychiatrists, and statisticians in an environment that fosters collaboration and scientific excellence.

Profile
The candidate holds a master’s degree in psychology or a related discipline (e.g., Mental Health, Psychiatry, Social or Health Sciences) and has demonstrated a strong interest in research. Solid experience with quantitative research methods and strong statistical skills are essential. Prior experience with, or knowledge of, the Experience Sampling Method is highly desirable. The candidate should be committed to open‑science practices and possess excellent written and spoken English skills (C1 proficiency level).

Offer
A contract for one year will be offered, which is renewable for another three years after a positive evaluation. Salaries for PhD students are competitive by international standards. The starting date is flexible, but no later than the first of March 2027.

Interested?
For this application, the following information will be considered:

  • Cover Letter (describing your motivation, research career goals, skills, and experience)
  • CV
  • Diploma and transcripts of records (BSc and MSc)
  • Contact details of at least two reference persons
  • Other information for consideration (e.g., a list of publications if applicable)


Please use the university’s job portal when applying for this position.

For more information, please contact Prof. Ginette Lafit at ginette.lafit@kuleuven.be.

You can apply for this job no later than December 07, 2026 via the application button.

KU Leuven strives for an inclusive, respectful, and socially safe environment. We embrace diversity among individuals and groups as an asset. Open dialogue and differences in perspective are essential for an ambitious research and educational environment. In our commitment to equal opportunity, we recognize the consequences of historical inequalities. We do not accept any form of discrimination based on, but not limited to, gender identity and expression, sexual orientation, age, ethnic or national background, skin colour, religious and philosophical diversity, neurodivergence, employment disability, health, or socioeconomic status. For questions about accessibility or support offered, we are happy to assist you at this email address: solliciteren@kuleuven.be.

jobs.title: PhD Position in Homotopy Theory
jobs.description_html:
Join us for a 4-year PhD position at Utrecht University’s Mathematical Institute. You will work within the NWO XL consortium project ‘Symmetry on the interface of topology and higher algebra’, a collaboration with Radboud University Nijmegen and Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, under Gijs Heuts’ supervision.

Your job
You will conduct cutting edge research with a focus on the interplay of topology and higher algebra. The precise goals of the research project are flexible, but within the scope of the large collaborative project.
